\paragraph{Related-work boundary.}
The literature is used in the main comparison table only at theorem level, with
the exact foundational theorem families named row by row.  On the probability
side, the record-law results belong beside finite
functions of Markov chains, discrete-time renewal processes, finite-dependence
CLTs, regenerative simulation, and batch-means output analysis
\cite{BlackwellKoopmans1957,Blackwell1957,Gilbert1959,Dharmadhikari1963Functions,Dharmadhikari1963Sufficient,Heller1965,BaumPetrie1966,MarzenCrutchfield2015Renewal,HoeffdingRobbins1948,Diananda1955,HendersonGlynn2001Regenerative,GlynnWhitt1991BatchMeans,VatsFlegalJones2019Multivariate}.
On the finite-law side, the renewal inclusion products are compared with
point-process inclusion theory and renewal-process foundations
\cite{CoxIsham1980,DaleyVereJones2003,Asmussen2003}.
On the response side, the conditional response-locus corollary is compared with
stationary UDW response and local-measurement theory
\cite{LoukoSatz2006,LoukoSatz2008,FewsterJuarezLouko2016,FewsterVerch2020,GisinEtAl2024ImpossibleMeasurements,PoloGomezEtAl2022,PapageorgiouFraser2024LocalMeasurement,PranziniKeskiVakkuri2025AQFT,Oeckl2025CausalMeasurement}.
The scope distinction is the one in \Cref{tab:main-jpa-comparison}: the
finite-dimensional law is obtained from renewal inclusion products and finite
inclusion--exclusion, the
inverse theorem is fixed-family quotient identifiability rather than generic
HMM identifiability, and the response corollary is a fixed-profile level-set
statement rather than a detector measurement theorem.

\section{Critical-rate branch and equal-rate limits}

Let
\[
p=e^{-\Gamma\Delta\tau},\qquad
s=e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau},\qquad
\sigma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau,\qquad
x=\frac{\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Delta\tau)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}} .
\]
The non-removable critical-rate equation is
\[
\log x=\sigma(x-1),
\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
x e^{-\sigma x}=e^{-\sigma}.
\]
Thus, away from the meeting point $\sigma=1$,
\[
\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Delta\tau)
=-\frac{1}{\Delta\tau}
W_k\!\left(-\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau\,e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau}\right),
\qquad
k=\begin{cases}
-1,&0<\sigma<1,\\
0,&\sigma>1.
\end{cases}
\]
The other real branch gives the removable solution $x=1$ of the multiplied
equation. At $\sigma=1$ the two branches meet and $\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}=\kappa_{\mathrm r}$.

When $\kappa_{\mathrm r}=\Gamma$ the distinct-root formulas for the renewal
law are interpreted by continuity. With $\alpha=\Gamma\Delta\tau$ and
$p=e^{-\alpha}$,
\[
\mathbb P(G=k)=
p^k\bigl[(1-p)+\alpha(k(1-p)-p)\bigr],
\qquad
\mathbb P(G\ge k)=p^k(1+\alpha k),
\]
and hence
\[
h_k=
\frac{(1-p)+\alpha(k(1-p)-p)}{1+\alpha k},
\qquad
(h_{k+1}-h_k)=\frac{\alpha^2p}{(1+\alpha k)(1+\alpha(k+1))}>0 .
\]
The hidden eigenvalue on the equal-rate line is
\[
\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}}=e^{-\Gamma\Delta\tau}(1-\Gamma\Delta\tau).
\]

For fast sampling at fixed $\kappa_{\mathrm r}$, the same critical equation
gives
\[
\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Delta\tau)
=
\frac{L+\log L+o(1)}{\Delta\tau},
\qquad
L=\log\frac{1}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau},
\qquad
\Delta\tau\downarrow0 .
\]

\section{Finite-counting identity}

The main text proves the covariance tail
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(A_0,A_n)=\rho(a-\rho)\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}}^{\,n-1},\qquad n\ge1,
\]
with $a<\rho$ and $|\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}}|<1$. For the block count
$N_N=\sum_{t=0}^{N-1}A_t$, stationarity gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}(N_N)
=N\rho(1-\rho)+2\sum_{n=1}^{N-1}(N-n)\rho(a-\rho)\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}}^{\,n-1}.
\]
Evaluating the geometric sum yields the finite-$N$ identity
\[
\operatorname{Var}(N_N)
=
N\rho(1-\rho)
+
\frac{2\rho(a-\rho)}{(1-\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}})^2}
\bigl(N(1-\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}})-1+\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}}^N\bigr).
\]
Dividing by $\mathbb E N_N=N\rho$ and letting $N\to\infty$ gives the
displayed main-text Fano limit
\(\lim_m\Var(N_m)/\EE N_m
=1-\rho+2(a-\rho)/(1-\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}})<1\).

\section{Ambient residual graph for ratio inversion}

For ambient algebraic radius bookkeeping, write
\[
\mathsf e=(\eta,c),\qquad c=(c_1,c_2),
\]
and define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two-mode-phi-main}
\Phi_m(\theta,\mathsf e)=R_m(\theta;\eta)-c_m,\qquad
\Phi=(\Phi_1,\Phi_2).
\end{equation}
For the physical detector settings, $c=C$ and
\[
\Phi(\theta,(\eta,C))=H(\theta,\eta).
\]
Exact generated data at the true parameter are denoted
\[
\eta_*=(r_{\varphi,1},r_{{\mathrm{mem}},1},
        r_{\varphi,2},r_{{\mathrm{mem}},2}),
\qquad
\mathsf e_*=(\eta_*,C),
\]
and on the fixed-detector slice we write
\[
\Phi_C(\theta,\eta)=\Phi(\theta,(\eta,C))=H(\theta,\eta).
\]

\begin{lemma}[Data-dependent residual graph]\label{lem:data-dependent-residual-graph-main}
Let $U_0\subset\RR^2$ and $W_0\subset\RR^q$ be open sets and let
$G:U_0\times W_0\to\RR^2$ be $C^1$. If $G(\theta_0,w_0)=0$ and
$D_\theta G(\theta_0,w_0)$ is nonsingular, then there are neighbourhoods
$U\subset U_0$ of $\theta_0$ and $W\subset W_0$ of $w_0$ and a unique
$C^1$ map $\Psi:W\to U$ such that $\Psi(w_0)=\theta_0$ and
\[
G(\Psi(w),w)=0\qquad(w\in W).
\]
After shrinking $U$ and $W$ if necessary, every solution of
$G(\theta,w)=0$ in $U\times W$ lies on this graph. Freezing the data first
would give only local uniqueness of a zero of $\theta\mapsto G(\theta,w_0)$;
the data-to-parameter map is the graph obtained with $w$ retained as the
parameter.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
This is the parameter-dependent implicit function theorem \cite{KrantzParks2002},
applied with $\theta$ as the unknown and $w$ as the parameter.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Ambient residual graph, not a shell-data inverse]\label{cor:ambient-ratio-graph-app-main}
In the two-mode inverse notation of the main text, let
\[
\mathcal E\subset\mathcal D\times(0,\infty)^2
\]
be the open algebraic data set on which \eqref{eq:two-mode-phi-main} is
defined, and fix $(\theta_*,\mathsf e_*)$ with $\Phi(\theta_*,\mathsf e_*)=0$.
Assume $D_\theta\Phi(\theta_*,\mathsf e_*)$ is nonsingular.

Then there are neighborhoods $U\subset\Theta$ of $\theta_*$ and
$W\subset\mathcal E$ of $\mathsf e_*$ and a unique $C^1$ map
\[
\Psi:W\to U,\qquad \Psi(\mathsf e_*)=\theta_*,
\]
such that
\[
\Phi(\Psi(\mathsf e),\mathsf e)=0\qquad(\mathsf e\in W).
\]
After shrinking $U$ and $W$, every solution in $U\times W$ lies on this graph.
On the fixed-detector slice
\[
W_C=\{\eta\in\mathcal D:(\eta,C)\in W\},
\qquad
\Psi_C(\eta)=\Psi((\eta,C)),
\]
there is an identity
\[
\Phi_C(\Psi_C(\eta),\eta)=0\qquad(\eta\in W_C),
\]
and if $\theta\in U$ and $\Phi_C(\theta,\eta)=0$ for some $\eta\in W_C$, then
$\theta=\Psi_C(\eta)$. This is only an ambient residual graph for the two ratio
equations. It does not assert that the radius quadruples in $W_C$ are physical
common-core shell data.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply the preceding lemma with $G=\Phi$ and $w=\mathsf e$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fixed-setting long-record local full-shell subset]\label{thm:full-shell-subset-main}
In the setting of \Cref{cor:ambient-ratio-graph-app-main}, shrink $W_C$ if
necessary so that the four radii remain in the coordinate range where the
background family and the response factors are defined. For $\eta\in W_C$ set
\[
\theta(\eta)=\Psi_C(\eta),
\]
and define the two mode amplitudes along the ratio graph by
\[
\mathcal A_m(\eta)=
\mathcal A_{\varphi,m}(\theta(\eta);\eta)
=
\mathcal A_{{\mathrm{mem}},m}(\theta(\eta);\eta),
\qquad m=1,2,
\]
where the equality is the within-mode equality forced by
$\Phi_C(\theta(\eta),\eta)=0$. Let
\[
E_C(\eta)=\mathcal A_1(\eta)-\mathcal A_2(\eta).
\]
Then the nearby full common-core shell records in the fixed-detector slice are
exactly
\begin{equation}\label{eq:full-shell-subset-main}
\mathcal P_C
=
\{\eta\in W_C:E_C(\eta)=0,\ \mathcal A_1(\eta)>0,
\text{ and the four radii are exterior-admissible}\}.
\end{equation}
The function $E_C$ is $C^1$. In particular, if the exact datum $\eta_*$ is
exterior-admissible and
\[
dE_C(\eta_*)\neq0
\]
as a covector on the ambient radius-record space $W_C$, then
$\mathcal P_C$ is, near $\eta_*$, a nonempty $C^1$ codimension-one submanifold
of $W_C$. If this transversality fails, the theorem still gives the exact local
zero-set characterization \eqref{eq:full-shell-subset-main}, but no manifold
structure is asserted.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For every $\eta\in W_C$, the defining property of the ambient graph gives
\[
\Phi_C(\theta(\eta),\eta)=0,
\]
which is the pair of physical ratio equations $H_m(\theta(\eta),\eta)=0$.
\Cref{lem:ratio-admissibility-main} says that each of these two ratio equations
is equivalent to equality of the ideal-benchmark and memory amplitude estimates
within the same mode. Hence the displayed definitions of
$\mathcal A_m(\eta)$ are unambiguous along the graph.

A full common-core shell record requires exactly one positive homogeneous
hardware prefactor for all four undivided shell equations, together with the
exterior-range restrictions. Along the ratio graph the two estimates within
each mode are already equal, so the only remaining cross-mode amplitude
condition is
\[
\mathcal A_1(\eta)=\mathcal A_2(\eta),
\]
which is $E_C(\eta)=0$. Positivity of the common amplitude and exterior
admissibility are the other two conditions in
\Cref{lem:ratio-admissibility-main}. This proves the set identity
\eqref{eq:full-shell-subset-main}.

The maps $\Psi_C$, $N$, and $\beta_\infty$ are $C^1$ on the neighbourhoods in
question, and the amplitude estimates are compositions of $C^1$ functions with
the smooth exponential function. Therefore $\mathcal A_m$ and $E_C$ are $C^1$.
At exact generated data, the common-core hypothesis gives
$E_C(\eta_*)=0$, so $\eta_*\in\mathcal P_C$ after shrinking to preserve
exterior admissibility and positivity. If $dE_C(\eta_*)\neq0$, the regular
level-set theorem makes $E_C^{-1}(0)$ a $C^1$ codimension-one submanifold of
$W_C$ near $\eta_*$. Positivity and exterior admissibility are open conditions,
so intersecting with them leaves the same local submanifold structure. Without
the nonvanishing derivative, only the proved zero-set characterization remains.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Restriction to full common-core shell records]\label{cor:full-shell-restriction-main}
In the setting of \Cref{thm:full-shell-subset-main}, let
$\mathcal P_C\subset W_C$ be the full common-core subset characterized in
\eqref{eq:full-shell-subset-main}.
For every $\eta\in\mathcal P_C$, the parameter $\Psi_C(\eta)$ is the unique
local background parameter in $U$ compatible with the corresponding full
common-core shell data, and the common amplitude is obtained by evaluating any
one of the four equal undivided amplitude estimates. Conversely, if
$\eta\in W_C$ is compatible with full common-core shell equations at some
$\theta\in U$, then $\theta=\Psi_C(\eta)$ and $\eta\in\mathcal P_C$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If $\eta\in\mathcal P_C$, then by definition the ratio equations hold at
$\Psi_C(\eta)$ and the undivided amplitude, positivity, and exterior-range
checks also hold there. Hence the full shell equations are satisfied with one
positive common amplitude. If another $\theta\in U$ satisfied the same full
shell equations, division within each mode would give
$\Phi_C(\theta,\eta)=0$, so the uniqueness part of
\Cref{cor:ambient-ratio-graph-app-main} gives $\theta=\Psi_C(\eta)$. The converse is
the same argument in reverse: full common-core shell equations imply the ratio
equations and the admissibility checks, hence the local root is $\Psi_C(\eta)$
and $\eta$ belongs to $\mathcal P_C$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Ratio admissibility and amplitude consistency]\label{rem:amplitude-consistency-main}
\Cref{thm:two-mode-main},
\Cref{cor:ambient-ratio-graph-app-main}, and
\Cref{lem:ratio-admissibility-main} separate checks that are sometimes
conflated. The fixed-radius map $\mathcal R_{\eta_*}$ contains the two
ratio-level observables and no unknown common amplitude; the main-text theorem
is the deterministic local inverse branch for those two values together with the fixed-setting long-record test
for whether the recovered parameter still yields one positive common amplitude.
If the radius record is also varied, the only general statement is the ambient residual graph in
\Cref{cor:ambient-ratio-graph-app-main}. \Cref{cor:full-shell-restriction-main}
is the step that restricts that graph to full shell data. A candidate
ratio-level solution is a full common-core solution only if the four undivided
amplitude estimates
\[
\mathcal A_{\varphi,1}(\theta;\eta),\quad
\mathcal A_{{\mathrm{mem}},1}(\theta;\eta),\quad
\mathcal A_{\varphi,2}(\theta;\eta),\quad
\mathcal A_{{\mathrm{mem}},2}(\theta;\eta)
\]
are positive and equal to one common value in the exact model. Thus
amplitude-free ratio inversion means that the amplitude is not needed to solve
the two ratio equations; it does not mean that arbitrary radius records
automatically come from one physical detector core.
\end{remark}

\section{Appendix-only calibrated Schwarzschild specialization}\label{app:schwarzschild-toy}

All Schwarzschild insertions are collected here, away from the main theorem
chain. They are only abstract calibrated toy-model calculations inside the
fixed response profile: the lapse profile is inserted into the homogeneous
response equations, and no exact nonconstant-lapse detector-field realization
with $\mathcal S_x(\Omega)\equiv\mathcal S(\Omega)$ is claimed.
The fixed-radius and branch-inverse formulas in this section are therefore
conditional algebra inside the displayed toy model, not additional physical
response theorems.

\subsection{Near-horizon Schwarzschild expansions}

For Schwarzschild with $r_H=2M$ and $h=r-r_H$, the proper distance from the
horizon is
\[
\rho=\int_{r_H}^{r_H+h}\frac{dr}{\sqrt{1-r_H/r}}
=2\sqrt{r_Hh}+O(h^{3/2}).
\]
Consequently
\[
h=\frac{\rho^2}{4r_H}+O(\rho^4),
\]
and the area excess of an areal sphere satisfies
\[
A-A_H=4\pi\bigl((r_H+h)^2-r_H^2\bigr)
=2\pi\rho^2+O(\rho^4).
\]
Together with the small-gap linearized proper-distance ratio from
\Cref{thm:horizon-main}, this gives the appendix Schwarzschild area-excess specialization
\begin{equation}\label{eq:area-ratio-main}
\frac{A_{\varphi}(t)-A_H}{A_{\mathrm{mem}}(t)-A_H}
=
C_D(t)^2\Bigl(1+O(\eta(t))+O(\epsilon(t)^2)\Bigr),
\end{equation}
under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:horizon-main}.

\subsection{Homogeneous Schwarzschild toy specialization}

The following formulas are only computations inside the toy calibrated
homogeneous response function
\[
R_\Omega(x)=\frac{\mathcal A}{e^{\beta_\infty\Omega N(x)}-1}
\]
from \Cref{lem:abstract-homogeneous-specialization-main}.

\paragraph{Reproducibility note for \Cref{fig:shell-radii}.}
The three curves in \Cref{fig:shell-radii} are direct evaluations on the grid
\[
s=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau\in
\{0.25,0.50,0.75,1.00,1.25,1.50,1.75,2.00,2.50,3.00,3.50,4.00\},
\qquad
\kappa_{\mathrm r}=5,\quad \Delta\tau=s/5 .
\]
For each \(s\), compute the non-removable critical root
\(\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}=\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}(5,s/5)\) from
\[
\log x=s(x-1),\qquad x=\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}/\kappa_{\mathrm r},\qquad x\ne1,
\]
using the continuous value \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\) at \(s=1\) for the plotted variable, equivalently \(\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau=1\).  Then
\[
\Gamma_\varphi=\frac{\log\varphi}{\Delta\tau},\qquad
\beta_\varphi=\log\!\left(1+
\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{sw}}^2\mathcal S(\Omega)\Delta\tau}{\log\varphi}
\right),
\qquad
\beta_{\mathrm{mem}}=\log\!\left(1+
\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{sw}}^2\mathcal S(\Omega)}{\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}}
\right),
\]
where \(\Omega=1\).  With
\(\lambda_{\mathrm{sw}}^2\mathcal S(\Omega)=2\) and
\(\beta_\infty=4\pi\), the panel~(a) curves are
\[
N_\varphi=\beta_\varphi/\beta_\infty,
\qquad
N_{\mathrm{mem}}=\beta_{\mathrm{mem}}/\beta_\infty .
\]
The exact solid curve in panel~(b) is obtained by converting each plotted lapse
to
\[
r_\star=\frac{1}{1-N_\star^2},\qquad
\rho_\star=\int_1^{r_\star}\frac{dr}{\sqrt{1-1/r}},
\qquad
\star\in\{\varphi,\mathrm{mem}\},
\]
and plotting \(\rho_\varphi/\rho_{\mathrm{mem}}\).  The dashed curve is the
leading-order predictor
\[
C_D=\frac{\Delta\tau\,\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}(5,\Delta\tau)}{\log\varphi}.
\]

For the Schwarzschild insertion used in \Cref{fig:shell-radii},
\[
N(r)=\sqrt{1-\frac{r_{\mathrm s}}{r}},
\qquad r_{\mathrm s}=1.
\]
For every exterior radius $r>r_{\mathrm s}$ one has
\[
0<N(r)<1.
\]
Hence any displayed target value $N_\star\in(0,1)$ determines a unique
exterior radius through
\[
r_\star=\frac{r_{\mathrm s}}{1-N_\star^2}>r_{\mathrm s},
\qquad
\star\in\{\varphi,\mathrm{mem}\},
\]
and the Schwarzschild regularity derivative is
\[
N'(r)=\frac{r_{\mathrm s}}{2r^2N(r)}\neq0
\qquad\text{for }r>r_{\mathrm s}.
\]
Thus every displayed target lapse in $(0,1)$ gives a unique exterior shell and
satisfies the regular level-set condition. Across the plotted window one reads
off
\[
0.003018\le N_\star\le 0.242932<1,
\qquad
\star\in\{\varphi,\mathrm{mem}\},
\]
so every plotted point satisfies the range check $0<N_\star<1$. For each
plotted ideal or memory value, the corresponding radius is the unique exterior
solution of $N(r)=N_\star$, namely
\[
r_\star=\frac{r_{\mathrm s}}{1-N_\star^2}>r_{\mathrm s},
\qquad
N'(r_\star)=\frac{r_{\mathrm s}}{2r_\star^2N_\star}>0.
\]
Hence every plotted point is an exterior regular shell of this toy
specialization rather than only a formal response-locus value.

\begin{proposition}[Abstract calibrated toy-model corollary: Schwarzschild algebra]\label{prop:schw-main}
Assume a fixed calibrated $R_\Omega$. The homogeneous Schwarzschild toy
specialization yields the following algebraic identities.
Work under the standing convention for the fixed-radius inverse results, and
assume the calibrated homogeneous spectral-weight regime, so that the fixed
calibrated response function $R_\Omega$ is homogeneous. Define the detector
constants
\begin{equation}\label{eq:beta-constants-main}
\beta_{\varphi}(D)=
\frac{1}{\Omega}
\log\!\left(1+\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{sw}}^2\mathcal S(\Omega)\Delta\tau}{\log\varphi}\right),
\qquad
\beta_{\mathrm{mem}}(D)=
\frac{1}{\Omega}
\log\!\left(1+\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{sw}}^2\mathcal S(\Omega)}
{\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Delta\tau)}\right).
\end{equation}
If model-admissible shell data generated by the same response amplitude occur
at distinct radii $r_{\varphi}\neq r_{\mathrm{mem}}$ in Schwarzschild, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:beta-infty-main}
\beta_\infty^2=
\frac{\beta_{\varphi}(D)^2r_{\varphi}-\beta_{\mathrm{mem}}(D)^2r_{\mathrm{mem}}}
{r_{\varphi}-r_{\mathrm{mem}}},
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:mass-main}
M=
\frac{r_{\varphi}r_{\mathrm{mem}}\bigl(\beta_{\varphi}(D)^2-\beta_{\mathrm{mem}}(D)^2\bigr)}
{2\bigl(\beta_{\varphi}(D)^2r_{\varphi}-\beta_{\mathrm{mem}}(D)^2r_{\mathrm{mem}}\bigr)}.
\end{equation}
These formulas use the undivided Schwarzschild lapse equations and the common
amplitude hypothesis; arbitrary radius pairs or ratio data do not determine a
physical shell record.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
In Schwarzschild,
\[
N(r)^2=1-\frac{2M}{r}.
\]
The two homogeneous shell equations are
\[
\frac{\beta_{\varphi}(D)^2}{\beta_\infty^2}=1-\frac{2M}{r_\varphi},
\qquad
\frac{\beta_{\mathrm{mem}}(D)^2}{\beta_\infty^2}=1-\frac{2M}{r_{\mathrm{mem}}}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\beta_\infty^2-\frac{2M\beta_\infty^2}{r_\varphi}=\beta_{\varphi}(D)^2,
\qquad
\beta_\infty^2-\frac{2M\beta_\infty^2}{r_{\mathrm{mem}}}=\beta_{\mathrm{mem}}(D)^2.
\]
This is a nonsingular linear system for $\beta_\infty^2$ and
$2M\beta_\infty^2$ when $r_\varphi\neq r_{\mathrm{mem}}$. Solving it gives
\eqref{eq:beta-infty-main} and \eqref{eq:mass-main}. The model-admissibility
hypothesis is what guarantees that the displayed right-hand sides are positive
and correspond to a shell outside the horizon; arbitrary pairs of radii and
detector constants need not do so.
\end{proof}

Proposition~\ref{prop:schw-main} is exact algebra only within this toy
calibrated model. It is not amplitude-free, because $\beta_\varphi(D)$ and
$\beta_{\mathrm{mem}}(D)$ still contain the common response amplitude.

\begin{corollary}[Abstract calibrated toy-model corollary: Schwarzschild branch inverse and residual check]\label{cor:schwarzschild-branch-main}
Assume a fixed calibrated $R_\Omega$. The Schwarzschild branch reduction has
the following one-parameter inverse and residual-check form inside the toy
calibrated model.
Assume the same fixed calibrated homogeneous response-model setting as in
\Cref{thm:two-mode-main}, and assume further that the background family
contains a Hartle--Hawking Schwarzschild branch
\[
\iota_{\mathrm{Schw}}:I_M\to\Theta,
\qquad
\iota_{\mathrm{Schw}}(M)=(8\pi M,M),
\]
defined on an open interval $I_M\subset(0,\infty)$. Fix an exact radius record
$\eta_*$ produced at some $M_*\in I_M$ by admissible full common-core shell
data on that branch with one positive shared amplitude $\mathcal A_*>0$, so
that
\[
\theta_*=\iota_{\mathrm{Schw}}(M_*),
\qquad
\mathcal R_{\eta_*}(\theta_*)=C
\]
and
\[
\mathcal A_{\varphi,1}(\theta_*;\eta_*)
=\mathcal A_{{\mathrm{mem}},1}(\theta_*;\eta_*)
=\mathcal A_{\varphi,2}(\theta_*;\eta_*)
=\mathcal A_{{\mathrm{mem}},2}(\theta_*;\eta_*)
=\mathcal A_*>0,
\]
with all four radii lying in the exterior coordinate range at $\theta_*$.
Choose one detector mode $j\in\{1,2\}$ as the estimation mode and let
$k\in\{1,2\}\setminus\{j\}$ be the remaining mode. Define the reduced
Schwarzschild branch ratio functions
\[
G_{m,\eta_*}(M)=R_m(\iota_{\mathrm{Schw}}(M);\eta_*),
\qquad m=1,2.
\]
Assume that the fixed radii in $\eta_*$ remain exterior-admissible on a
neighbourhood of $M_*$ in $I_M$ and that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:schwarzschild-branch-derivative-main}
\frac{d}{dM}G_{j,\eta_*}(M_*)\neq0.
\end{equation}
Then there are neighbourhoods $I_*\subset I_M$ of $M_*$ and
$Y_j\subset(0,\infty)$ of $C_j$, together with a unique $C^1$ inverse branch
\[
\mathcal J_{\eta_*,j}:Y_j\to I_*,
\qquad
\mathcal J_{\eta_*,j}(C_j)=M_*,
\]
such that
\[
G_{j,\eta_*}(\mathcal J_{\eta_*,j}(y_j))=y_j
\qquad(y_j\in Y_j).
\]
Hence nearby estimated values of the single ratio coordinate $y_j$ recover the
physical Schwarzschild parameter through
\[
\widehat M=\mathcal J_{\eta_*,j}(y_j),
\qquad
\widehat\beta_\infty=8\pi\,\widehat M.
\]
The second ratio does not provide an independent free coordinate on the
physical Schwarzschild branch; instead it gives the residual consistency check
\begin{equation}\label{eq:schwarzschild-branch-residual-main}
\mathfrak c_{\eta_*,k|j}(y_j,y_k)
=G_{k,\eta_*}(\mathcal J_{\eta_*,j}(y_j))-y_k.
\end{equation}
At the exact physical record one has
\[
\mathfrak c_{\eta_*,k|j}(C_j,C_k)=0.
\]
Moreover, if exact full fixed-setting shell data occur at the same detector
settings for a pair $(y_j,y_k)$ with $y_j\in Y_j$, then
\[
y_j=C_j,\qquad y_k=C_k,
\qquad
\mathfrak c_{\eta_*,k|j}(y_j,y_k)=0,
\]
by \Cref{thm:two-mode-main}. Thus on the physical
Hartle--Hawking Schwarzschild branch the inverse statement is genuinely
one-parameter, and the remaining ratio is a residual compatibility test rather
than a second independent inverse coordinate.

If, in addition, a scalar ratio estimator satisfies
\[
\sqrt{N}\,(\widehat y_{j,N}-C_j)\Longrightarrow \mathcal N(0,\sigma_j^2),
\]
then with
$
\widehat M_N=\mathcal J_{\eta_*,j}(\widehat y_{j,N})
$
and
$
\widehat\beta_{\infty,N}=8\pi\widehat M_N
$
one has
\[
\sqrt{N}\,(\widehat M_N-M_*)
\Longrightarrow
\mathcal N\!\left(0,
\frac{\sigma_j^2}{\bigl(G_{j,\eta_*}'(M_*)\bigr)^2}\right),
\]
and
\[
\sqrt{N}\,(\widehat\beta_{\infty,N}-8\pi M_*)
\Longrightarrow
\mathcal N\!\left(0,
\frac{(8\pi)^2\sigma_j^2}{\bigl(G_{j,\eta_*}'(M_*)\bigr)^2}\right).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Because $\iota_{\mathrm{Schw}}$, $\beta_\infty$, $N$, and the exponential map
are $C^1$, each $G_{m,\eta_*}$ is a $C^1$ function of $M$ on the
exterior-admissible branch interval. The exact shell-data hypothesis gives
$G_{j,\eta_*}(M_*)=C_j$. The nonvanishing derivative in
\eqref{eq:schwarzschild-branch-derivative-main} is precisely the one-variable
inverse-function condition, so the ordinary one-dimensional inverse function
theorem yields the neighbourhoods $I_*,Y_j$ and the unique $C^1$ inverse
branch $\mathcal J_{\eta_*,j}$.

The residual formula \eqref{eq:schwarzschild-branch-residual-main} is the
remaining ratio equation evaluated along that recovered branch. At the exact
record it vanishes because $G_{k,\eta_*}(M_*)=C_k$. If exact full fixed-setting
shell data were to occur at the same detector settings for some
$(y_j,y_k)$, then the recovered parameter would be
$\theta=\iota_{\mathrm{Schw}}(\mathcal J_{\eta_*,j}(y_j))$ and
\Cref{thm:two-mode-main} would force the full ratio datum to
equal the unique fixed target $C$, proving the stated necessity of
$y_j=C_j,y_k=C_k$.

The final two limits are the one-dimensional delta method applied to the $C^1$
map $\mathcal J_{\eta_*,j}$ at $C_j$, together with the linear relation
$\beta_\infty=8\pi M$ on the Hartle--Hawking Schwarzschild branch.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Abstract calibrated homogeneous Schwarzschild-lapse worked example}\label{subsec:worked-example}

The following worked example is only bookkeeping inside the toy calibrated
homogeneous response function
$R_\Omega(x)=\mathcal A/(e^{\beta_\infty\Omega N(x)}-1)$ of
\Cref{lem:abstract-homogeneous-specialization-main}.

Table~\ref{tab:worked} inserts the Schwarzschild lapse profile into the same
toy model with $r_{\mathrm s}=2M=1$ (so $\beta_\infty=4\pi$), $\Omega=1$, and
$\lambda_{\mathrm{sw}}^2\mathcal S(\Omega)=2$. Two detector modes
$D_1=(\Omega,\lambda_{\mathrm{sw}},0.5,\,8.0)$ and
$D_2=(\Omega,\lambda_{\mathrm{sw}},1.2,\,3.0)$ are listed. For each mode, the
critical rate $\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}$ comes from \eqref{eq:gamma-c-main}, the shell radii
come from \Cref{cor:homogeneous-main}, the quotient check uses the
self-contained homogeneous source-equation quotient in \Cref{thm:ratio-main}, and
\Cref{prop:schw-main} is then applied to the $D_1$
pair to recover $\beta_\infty$ and $M$. The table is bookkeeping for the
calibrated specialization only.

For the four tabulated shell values, the Schwarzschild shell calculation is
explicit:
\[
N(r)=\sqrt{1-\frac{r_{\mathrm s}}{r}},
\qquad
0<N(r)<1 \quad\text{for } r>r_{\mathrm s},
\]
\[
r=\frac{r_{\mathrm s}}{1-N^2}>r_{\mathrm s}
\qquad\text{for every }N\in(0,1),
\]
\[
N'(r)=\frac{r_{\mathrm s}}{2r^2N(r)}\neq0
\qquad\text{for }r>r_{\mathrm s}.
\]
Therefore any displayed target $N_\star\in(0,1)$ produces a unique exterior
shell radius
\[
r_\star=\frac{r_{\mathrm s}}{1-N_\star^2}>r_{\mathrm s},
\qquad
\star\in\{\varphi,\mathrm{mem}\},
\]
and satisfies the regular level-set condition. The table records the four
interval checks for $N_\varphi$ and $N_{\mathrm{mem}}$ in both detector modes,
together with the corresponding derivative values
\[
N'(r_\star)=\frac{r_{\mathrm s}}{2r_\star^2N_\star}>0.
\]
The table records these derivative values numerically, so each tabulated locus
is a genuine exterior regular shell inside the toy Schwarzschild
specialization.

For the physical Hartle--Hawking Schwarzschild inverse problem, however, the
parameter family is already constrained by $\beta_\infty=8\pi M$. The relevant
one-parameter statement is therefore the branch corollary
\Cref{cor:schwarzschild-branch-main}, not the ambient two-parameter Jacobian.
Using $D_1$ as the estimation mode, the branch function
\[
G_{1,\eta_*}(M)=R_1\bigl((8\pi M,M);\eta_*\bigr)
\]
has derivative
\[
G_{1,\eta_*}'(M_*)\approx -24.10,
\]
so nearby estimates of the first ratio coordinate recover $M$ and hence
$\beta_\infty=8\pi M$ locally. The second mode is then checked through the
residual
\[
\mathfrak c_{\eta_*,2|1}(y_1,y_2)
=G_{2,\eta_*}(\mathcal J_{\eta_*,1}(y_1))-y_2,
\]
which vanishes at the exact target pair up to the displayed table rounding.

For comparison with the abstract fixed-radius ratio map,
\Cref{thm:two-mode-main} can still be evaluated at the same fixed radius record
$\eta_*$ in the ambient coordinate chart $\theta=(\beta_\infty,M)$, giving
\[
\det D_\theta\mathcal R_{\eta_*}(\theta_*)\approx-2.97\times10^{-1}.
\]
That determinant confirms the abstract inverse branch of
\Cref{thm:two-mode-main} for nearby ratio values at fixed $\eta_*$. It is
ambient ratio-map bookkeeping, not the physical Hartle--Hawking branch
statement.

\section{Numerical bookkeeping}

The figures and the worked Schwarzschild table use the same detector constants
as the appendix toy model: $r_{\mathrm s}=2M=1$, $\beta_\infty=4\pi$, $\Omega=1$, and
$\lambda_{\mathrm{sw}}^2\mathcal S(\Omega)=2$. For mode $m$ the ratio target tabulated in the
worked example is
\[
C_m=\frac{\Delta\tau_m\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}(\kappa_{{\mathrm r},m},\Delta\tau_m)}
{\log\varphi}.
\]
The numerical values in the table are generated from the critical-rate branch
above and the homogeneous lapse-level equations in the article. The fixed-radius
ratio inverse check treats $(\beta_\infty,M)$ as independent coordinates
before imposing any Hartle--Hawking relation.

\subsection{Deterministic numerical reproduction recipe}\label{subsec:numerical-recipe}

The numerical items in the manuscript are deterministic evaluations of the
closed formulas proved in the manuscript and appendices. No stochastic simulation or
external fit is used. This subsection records a paper-local recipe for
reproducing
\Cref{fig:hazard-cov,fig:spectrum-fano,fig:shell-radii,tab:worked}
directly from those formulas. Throughout, use a
root-solve tolerance of $10^{-12}$ and round displayed table entries to six
decimal places.

deterministic evaluations of closed expressions proved in the main theorem
chain.  They are not simulations, fits, or independent numerical validation,
and they are not finite-record studentized confidence procedures.

\paragraph{Step 1: solve the critical rate $\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Delta\tau)$.}
Given positive $\kappa_{\mathrm r}$ and $\Delta\tau$, set
\[
s=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau,
\qquad
H_s(x)=\log x-s(x-1).
\]
If $|s-1|<10^{-12}$, use the equal-rate value
$\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Delta\tau)=\kappa_{\mathrm r}$. Otherwise solve
$H_s(x)=0$ for the non-removable root $x_c\neq1$ from
\Cref{lem:critical-rate-main}. A deterministic bisection scheme is:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.2em,itemsep=0.25em]
\item If $0<s<1$, set $x_{\mathrm{lo}}=1+10^{-12}$ and
$x_{\mathrm{hi}}=2$. While $H_s(x_{\mathrm{hi}})\ge0$, replace
$x_{\mathrm{hi}}$ by $2x_{\mathrm{hi}}$.
\item If $s>1$, set $x_{\mathrm{hi}}=1-10^{-12}$ and
$x_{\mathrm{lo}}=1/2$. While $H_s(x_{\mathrm{lo}})\ge0$, replace
$x_{\mathrm{lo}}$ by $x_{\mathrm{lo}}/2$.
\item Bisect the resulting bracket until both the bracket width and the
residual in \eqref{eq:gamma-c-main} are below $10^{-12}$, and then set
\[
\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Delta\tau)=\kappa_{\mathrm r}x_c.
\]
\end{enumerate}
The Lambert-$W$ form in \Cref{rem:edge-cases} gives the same answer and may be
used as an independent cross-check. After this common rate computation, the
remaining targets are listed below in the final manuscript numbering:
\Cref{fig:hazard-cov,fig:spectrum-fano,fig:shell-radii,tab:worked}.

\paragraph{Compact record-side code fragment.}
The following machine-readable fragment evaluates the four record-side
quantities used in the deterministic plots: the critical rate
\(\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}\), hazard \(h_k\), spectral density \(f(\theta)\), and Fano factor
\(F\). It assumes \(\texttt{exp},\texttt{cos}\) from Python's \texttt{math}
module and \texttt{brentq} from \texttt{scipy.optimize}.
\begingroup\scriptsize
\begin{verbatim}
def abc(G,k,d):
 p,s=exp(-G*d),exp(-k*d); q=1-p
 if abs(G-k)<1e-12: a,b,L=1-(1+G*d)*p,G*d*p,p*(1-G*d)
 else: a,b,L=(k*(1-p)-G*(1-s))/(k-G),k*(p-s)/(k-G),(k*s-G*p)/(k-G)
 return p,s,q,a,b,L,q*(1-s)/(q+b)
def Gamma_crit(k,d):
 H=lambda G: ((k*exp(-k*d)-G*exp(-G*d))/(k-G) if abs(G-k)>1e-12 else exp(-k*d)*(1-k*d))
 return brentq(H,1e-14,100*max(k,1/d,1.0))
def h_k(j,G,k,d):
 p,s,q,a,b,L,r=abc(G,k,d); A=G*d
 return 1-p*(1+A*(j+1))/(1+A*j) if abs(G-k)<1e-12 else (k*(1-p)*p**j-G*(1-s)*s**j)/(k*p**j-G*s**j)
def f(t,G,k,d):
 p,s,q,a,b,L,r=abc(G,k,d); return r*(1-r)+2*r*(a-r)*(cos(t)-L)/(1-2*L*cos(t)+L*L)
def F(G,k,d): return f(0.0,G,k,d)/abc(G,k,d)[6]
\end{verbatim}
\endgroup

\paragraph{Target A: \Cref{fig:hazard-cov} (hazard and covariance plot).}
Fix $\kappa_{\mathrm r}=5$, $\Delta\tau=0.3$, and the three rates
\[
\Gamma\in\{1.2,\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}(5,0.3),3.2\}.
\]
This target evaluates closed population formulas only; it is not a
studentized interval construction.
For each $\Gamma$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.2em,itemsep=0.25em]
\item Compute $p$ and $s$ from \eqref{eq:p-c-recall-main}, then $a$ and $b$
from \eqref{eq:a-b-recall-main}, $\rho$ from \eqref{eq:rho-main}, and
$\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}}$ from \eqref{eq:lambda-hid-main}.
\item For panel~(a), evaluate the hazard $h_k$ for $k=0,\dots,8$ from
\eqref{eq:hazard-main}; only if $\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}$ should the
equal-rate formula \eqref{eq:equal-rate-survival-hazard-main} be used instead.
\item For panel~(b), evaluate
\[
\frac{\operatorname{Cov}(A_0,A_n)}
     {\left|\operatorname{Cov}(A_0,A_1)\right|}
\]
for $n=1,\dots,8$ from \eqref{eq:cov-main}. No Monte Carlo sampling is needed;
the curve is a direct plot of the closed covariance formula.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Target B: \Cref{fig:spectrum-fano} (spectrum and Fano plot).}
This target likewise evaluates population spectral and Fano formulas.  It
does not add a studentizer for \(f(\theta)\) or \(F\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.2em,itemsep=0.25em]
\item For panel~(a), fix $\kappa_{\mathrm r}=5$, $\Delta\tau=0.3$, and use
\[
\Gamma\Delta\tau\in\{0.3,0.6,1.0\},
\qquad
\theta\in\left\{0,\frac{\pi}{12},\frac{2\pi}{12},\dots,\pi\right\}.
\]
For each of the three values of $\Gamma$, compute the same
$p,s,a,b,\rho,\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}}$ from
\eqref{eq:p-c-recall-main}, \eqref{eq:a-b-recall-main}, \eqref{eq:rho-main},
and \eqref{eq:lambda-hid-main}, and evaluate the spectral
density $f(\theta)$ from \eqref{eq:spectrum-main}.
\item For panel~(b), use the dimensionless grid
\[
\Gamma\Delta\tau\in\{0.1,0.2,\dots,2.0\},
\qquad
\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau\in\{0.5,1.0,1.5\}.
\]
Because the formula depends only on these two dimensionless combinations, one
may set $\Delta\tau=1$, $\Gamma=\Gamma\Delta\tau$, and
$\kappa_{\mathrm r}=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau$ when evaluating the curve.
For each pair, compute
\[
F=
1-\rho+\frac{2(a-\rho)}{1-\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}}},
\]
the asymptotic Fano factor from \Cref{prop:spectrum-main}, and plot the
reference line $F=1$ for the Poisson benchmark.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Target C: \Cref{fig:shell-radii} (shell-radii plot).}
Use the deterministic grid
\[
\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau\in
\{0.25,0.50,0.75,1.00,1.25,1.50,1.75,2.00,2.50,3.00,3.50,4.00\}
\]
with $\kappa_{\mathrm r}=5$, hence $\Delta\tau=s/5$. For each grid value:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.2em,itemsep=0.25em]
\item Compute $\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}$ by Step~1 and
$\Gamma_\varphi=\log\varphi/\Delta\tau$.
\item Compute $\beta_\varphi$ and $\beta_{\mathrm{mem}}$ from
\eqref{eq:betaphi-betamem-main} with $\Omega=1$ and
$\lambda_{\mathrm{sw}}^2\mathcal S(\Omega)=2$, then set
\[
N_\varphi=\beta_\varphi/\beta_\infty,
\qquad
N_{\mathrm{mem}}=\beta_{\mathrm{mem}}/\beta_\infty,
\qquad
\beta_\infty=4\pi.
\]
These are the plotted lapse values in panel~(a).
\item In the Schwarzschild lapse specialization with $r_{\mathrm s}=1$,
invert $N(r)^2=1-r_{\mathrm s}/r$ to obtain
\[
r_\star=\frac{1}{1-N_\star^2},
\qquad
\star\in\{\varphi,\mathrm{mem}\}.
\]
\item Compute the exact proper distances from the horizon by the radial line
element
\[
\rho(r)=\int_{1}^{r}\frac{dr'}{\sqrt{1-1/r'}} ,
\]
using any deterministic quadrature with absolute error below $10^{-12}$, and
plot the exact ratio
$\rho_\varphi/\rho_{\mathrm{mem}}$ for panel~(b).
\item Plot the dashed small-gap predictor in panel~(b) as
\[
C_D=\frac{\Delta\tau\,\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Delta\tau)}{\log\varphi},
\]
the leading-order ratio from \Cref{thm:horizon-main}.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Target D: \Cref{tab:worked} (worked Schwarzschild table).}
The following Schwarzschild calculations are not claimed to arise from an
independently derived exact UDW response with
$\mathcal S_x(\Omega)\equiv\mathcal S(\Omega)$. They are computations inside the
abstract calibrated homogeneous response function
$R_\Omega(x)=\mathcal A/(e^{\beta_\infty\Omega N(x)}-1)$ of
\Cref{lem:abstract-homogeneous-specialization-main}.

Use the same abstract homogeneous Schwarzschild-lapse specialization as in the
table caption:
\[
r_{\mathrm s}=1,\qquad
\beta_\infty=4\pi,\qquad
\Omega=1,\qquad
\lambda_{\mathrm{sw}}^2\mathcal S(\Omega)=2,
\]
with detector modes
\[
D_1:\ (\Delta\tau,\kappa_{\mathrm r})=(0.5,8.0),
\qquad

Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.2em,itemsep=0.25em]

\item Compute $\beta_\varphi(D_m)$ and $\beta_{\mathrm{mem}}(D_m)$ from

\approx

\qquad

import unittest

import numpy as np

from artifacts import verify_nstate_identifiability as verify


class SerialKilledLeakageTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_exact_three_inclusion_image_equation(self):
        examples = (
            (0.35, 0.8, 0.2),
            (0.7, 1.6, 1.0),
            (2.0, 2.0, 1.0),
            (4.0, 0.45, 0.7),
        )
        for gamma, recovery, delta in examples:
            inclusions = verify.two_state_inclusion_coordinates(
                gamma, recovery, delta
            )
            residual = verify.physical_image_residual(inclusions)
            self.assertLess(abs(residual), 2e-12)

    def test_physical_image_equation_detects_intensity_perturbation(self):
        inclusions = verify.two_state_inclusion_coordinates(0.7, 1.6, 1.0)
        perturbed = inclusions.copy()
        perturbed[0] *= 1.01
        self.assertGreater(abs(verify.physical_image_residual(perturbed)), 1e-4)

    def test_hidden_mode_obeys_sharp_global_bound(self):
        grid = np.geomspace(1e-4, 50.0, 181)
        values = np.array(
            [verify.hidden_mode_secant(x, y) for x in grid for y in grid]
        )
        self.assertGreaterEqual(float(values.min()), -np.exp(-2.0) - 2e-14)
        self.assertLess(float(values.max()), 1.0)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(
            verify.hidden_mode_secant(2.0, 2.0), -np.exp(-2.0), places=15
        )

    def test_small_sampling_interval_mean_expansion_has_sixth_order_remainder(self):
        gamma = 0.7
        recovery = 1.6
        normalized_errors = []
        for delta in (0.2, 0.1, 0.05):
            exact = delta * verify.mean_cycle_length(gamma, recovery, delta)
            approximation = verify.small_delta_mean_expansion(
                gamma, recovery, delta
            )
            normalized_errors.append(abs(exact - approximation) / delta**6)
        self.assertLess(max(normalized_errors), 2e-3)

    def test_kernels_are_stochastic_and_clicks_reset(self):
        for rates in ((0.7, 1.6), (0.7, 1.2, 2.3)):
            t0, t1 = verify.serial_killed_reset_kernels(rates)
            np.testing.assert_allclose((t0 + t1).sum(axis=1), 1.0, atol=1e-13)
            self.assertGreaterEqual(float(t0.min()), -1e-14)
            self.assertGreaterEqual(float(t1.min()), -1e-14)
            self.assertTrue(np.allclose(t1[:, :-1], 0.0, atol=1e-14))

    def test_hankel_pencil_recovers_unordered_sampled_poles(self):
        for rates in ((0.7, 1.6), (0.7, 1.2, 2.3)):
            tails = verify.visible_tail_coordinates(rates, 2 * len(rates))
            recovered = verify.recover_sampled_poles(tails, len(rates))
            expected = np.sort(np.exp(-np.asarray(rates)))
            np.testing.assert_allclose(recovered, expected, rtol=1e-9, atol=1e-11)

    def test_confluent_recurrence_recovers_collision_multiplicities(self):
        examples = (
            (0.7, 0.7),
            (0.7, 1.2, 1.2),
            (0.7, 1.2, 1.2, 2.3),
        )
        for rates in examples:
            tails = verify.visible_tail_coordinates(rates, 3 * len(rates) + 1)
            polynomial, residual = verify.recover_minimal_recurrence(
                tails, len(rates)
            )
            expected = np.poly(np.exp(-np.asarray(rates, dtype=float)))
            np.testing.assert_allclose(
                polynomial, expected, rtol=2e-8, atol=2e-10
            )
            self.assertLess(residual, 2e-12)

    def test_collision_does_not_lower_serial_hankel_rank(self):
        examples = ((0.7, 0.7), (0.7, 1.2, 1.2), (0.7, 0.7, 2.3, 2.3))
        for rates in examples:
            tails = verify.visible_tail_coordinates(rates, 2 * len(rates))
            diagnostics = verify.hankel_diagnostics(tails, len(rates))
            self.assertEqual(diagnostics.rank, len(rates))
            self.assertGreater(diagnostics.smallest_singular_value, 1e-8)

    def test_visible_moments_are_permutation_invariant(self):
        rates = (0.45, 0.95, 1.8)
        baseline = verify.visible_click_moments(rates, 7)
        permuted = verify.visible_click_moments((1.8, 0.45, 0.95), 7)
        np.testing.assert_allclose(permuted, baseline, rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-13)

    def test_stochastic_similarity_changes_kernel_not_visible_law(self):
        examples = ((0.7, 1.6), (0.7, 1.2, 2.3), (0.7, 1.2, 1.2, 2.3))
        for rates in examples:
            t0, _ = verify.serial_killed_reset_kernels(rates)
            transformed = verify.equivalent_killed_reset_kernel(t0, epsilon=0.02)
            self.assertGreater(np.linalg.norm(transformed - t0), 1e-4)
            self.assertGreaterEqual(float(transformed.min()), -1e-13)
            base = verify.kernel_tail_coordinates(t0, 25)
            equivalent = verify.kernel_tail_coordinates(transformed, 25)
            np.testing.assert_allclose(equivalent, base, rtol=1e-11, atol=1e-12)

    def test_reset_preserving_similarity_tangent_has_expected_dimension(self):
        for n_states in (2, 3, 4):
            basis = verify.reset_similarity_lie_basis(n_states)
            self.assertEqual(len(basis), (n_states - 1) ** 2)
            reset = np.zeros(n_states)
            reset[-1] = 1.0
            for tangent in basis:
                np.testing.assert_allclose(tangent @ np.ones(n_states), 0.0)
                np.testing.assert_allclose(reset @ tangent, 0.0)

\section{Finite-Record Regenerative Tools}\label{app:finite-record-regenerative-tools-main}

This appendix collects auxiliary renewal facts used in \Cref{sec:records}.
The paper-level retained inclusion covariance estimator is proved in the
main-text adjacent-gap master theorem
\Cref{thm:main-calendar-stopped-separated-batch-plugin}.  The fixed-range
facts below are auxiliary standard regenerative tools used only by secondary
diagnostics and supplementary protocols.

\begin{proposition}[Separated-batch covariance for fixed-range gap rewards]\label{thm:regenerative-separated-batch-covariance-main}
Fix an integer \(m\ge0\) and a dimension \(d\).  Let
\((G_j)_{j\in\mathbb Z}\) be i.i.d. with
\(\EE e^{\eta G_0}<\infty\) for some \(\eta>0\), and let
\[
Y_j=f(G_j,\ldots,G_{j+m})\in\RR^d,\qquad
\EE Y_j=0,\qquad \EE\|Y_j\|^4<\infty .
\]
Set
\[
T_m=\operatorname{Var}(Y_0)+
\sum_{h=1}^m\{\operatorname{Cov}(Y_0,Y_h)+\operatorname{Cov}(Y_h,Y_0)\}.
\]
Let \(b_N\to\infty\), \(b_N/N\to0\),
\(M_N=\lfloor N/(b_N+m)\rfloor\), and define the separated batches
\[
I_{\ell,N}=\{(\ell-1)(b_N+m),\ldots,
(\ell-1)(b_N+m)+b_N-1\},\qquad
B_{\ell,N}=\sum_{j\in I_{\ell,N}}Y_j ,
\]
for \(1\le\ell\le M_N\).  On \(M_N\ge2\), put
\(\bar B_N=M_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_N}B_{\ell,N}\).  Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regenerative-separated-batch-covariance-main}
\left\|
\frac{1}{b_N(M_N-1)}
\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_N}(B_{\ell,N}-\bar B_N)
(B_{\ell,N}-\bar B_N)^\top
-T_m
\right\|_{\operatorname{op}}
=O_{\PP}\left(b_N^{-1}+\sqrt{\frac{b_N}{N}}\right).
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The separated blocks \(I_{\ell,N}\) are independent because the reward has
range \(m\).  Stationarity gives
\(b_N^{-1}\Var(B_{\ell,N})=T_m+O(b_N^{-1})\), and the fourth-moment expansion
for \(m\)-dependent sums gives \(\EE\|B_{\ell,N}\|^4\le Cb_N^2\).  Applying
Kolmogorov's maximal inequality entrywise to the independent centered matrices
\[
b_N^{-1}\{B_{\ell,N}B_{\ell,N}^\top-\EE(B_{\ell,N}B_{\ell,N}^\top)\}
\]
over the deterministic prefix \(M_N=\lfloor N/(b_N+m)\rfloor\) gives the
\(\sqrt{b_N/N}\) fluctuation term, and the empirical batch mean contributes
only \(O_{\PP}(M_N^{-1})\).  This proves
\eqref{eq:regenerative-separated-batch-covariance-main}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Calendar-stopped separated batches with plug-in centering]\label{prop:calendar-stopped-separated-batch-plugin-main}
Let \((G_j)_{j\ge0}\) be i.i.d. nonnegative integer-valued gaps with
\(\EE e^{\eta G_0}<\infty\) for some \(\eta>0\), put
\(L_j=G_j+1\), \(\mu=\EE L_0\), and
\[
S_k=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}L_j,\qquad
K_N=\max\{k:S_k<N\}.
\]
Fix \(m\ge0\), \(d\ge1\), and
\[
Y_j=f(G_j,\ldots,G_{j+m})\in\RR^d,\qquad
\EE Y_j=0,
\]
where
\[
\|f(g_0,\ldots,g_m)\|\le C_f\left(1+\sum_{i=0}^m g_i\right).
\]
Let
\[
\mathcal T_m=\Var(Y_0)+
\sum_{h=1}^{m}\{\operatorname{Cov}(Y_0,Y_h)+\operatorname{Cov}(Y_h,Y_0)\}.
\]
For \(b_N=\lfloor N^\beta\rfloor\), \(0<\beta<1\), set
\(d_N=b_N+m\) and
\[
I_{\ell,N}=\{(\ell-1)d_N,\ldots,(\ell-1)d_N+b_N-1\},
\qquad
B_{\ell,N}=\sum_{j\in I_{\ell,N}}Y_j .
\]
Fix an integer \(q\ge0\), representing the fixed terminal endpoint and
look-ahead deletion.  The all-complete-cycle stopped batch count is
\[
M_N=\max\{M\ge0:\ (M-1)d_N+b_N-1+m+q\le K_N-1\},
\]
with \(M_N=0\) if the set is empty.  On \(M_N\ge2\), define
\(\bar B_N=M_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_N}B_{\ell,N}\) and
\[
\widehat\Sigma_N^{Y}
=
\frac{K_N}{N}\frac1{b_N(M_N-1)}
\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_N}(B_{\ell,N}-\bar B_N)
(B_{\ell,N}-\bar B_N)^\top .
\]
Then \(M_N\ge2\) with probability tending to one and, with the harmless
auxiliary definition \(\widehat\Sigma_N^{Y}=0_{d\times d}\) on \(M_N<2\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:calendar-stopped-separated-batch-rate-main}
\left\|\widehat\Sigma_N^{Y}-\frac{\mathcal T_m}{\mu}
\right\|_{\operatorname{op}}
=O_{\PP}\left(b_N^{-1}+\sqrt{\frac{b_N}{N}}\right).
\end{equation}

Moreover, let \(\Delta_N=O_{\PP}(N^{-1/2})\) be an \(\RR^d\)-valued
finite-record plug-in error and set
\[
\widehat Y_j=Y_j-\Delta_N L_j,\qquad
\widehat B_{\ell,N}=\sum_{j\in I_{\ell,N}}\widehat Y_j,\qquad
\overline{\widehat B}_N=M_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_N}\widehat B_{\ell,N}.
\]
The mean \(\overline{\widehat B}_N\) is used only on \(M_N\ge2\).
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:calendar-stopped-plugin-block-main}
\max_{1\le\ell\le M_N}
\left\|\widehat B_{\ell,N}-B_{\ell,N}\right\|
=O_{\PP}(b_NN^{-1/2})
\end{equation}
and the Algorithm~1 covariance object with plug-in rewards satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:calendar-stopped-plugin-covariance-rate-main}
\left\|
\frac{K_N}{N}\frac1{b_N(M_N-1)}
\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_N}
(\widehat B_{\ell,N}-\overline{\widehat B}_N)
(\widehat B_{\ell,N}-\overline{\widehat B}_N)^\top
-\frac{\mathcal T_m}{\mu}
\right\|_{\operatorname{op}}
=O_{\PP}\left(b_N^{-1}+\sqrt{\frac{b_N}{N}}\right),
\end{equation}
again with the auxiliary zero completion on \(M_N<2\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The renewal estimates
\[
K_N=N/\mu+O_{\PP}(\sqrt N),\qquad
\max_{j\le K_N+m+q+1}L_j=O_{\PP}(\log N)
\]
follow from the exponential moment.  Hence the fixed endpoint/look-ahead
deletion changes the stopped batch count by at most \(O(1)\), and
\[
M_N=\frac{N}{\mu(b_N+m)}
     +O_{\PP}\!\left(\frac{\sqrt N}{b_N}+1\right).
\]
Conditional on any deterministic prefix in the high-probability range
\(\ell\le C N/b_N\), the separated batch sums are independent by the
range-\(m\) separator.  The deterministic-prefix estimate in
\Cref{thm:regenerative-separated-batch-covariance-main}, combined with the
random-prefix replacement above and \(K_N/N\to1/\mu\), gives
\eqref{eq:calendar-stopped-separated-batch-rate-main}.  For the plug-in part,
\[
\widehat B_{\ell,N}-B_{\ell,N}
=-\Delta_N\sum_{j\in I_{\ell,N}}L_j,
\]
and a Chernoff bound plus a union bound over \(O_{\PP}(N/b_N)\) retained
batches gives the uniform block bound
\eqref{eq:calendar-stopped-plugin-block-main}.  Expanding the centered
quadratic covariance then gives the same cross-term and pure plug-in bounds as
in the main adjacent-gap theorem, proving
\eqref{eq:calendar-stopped-plugin-covariance-rate-main}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Standard complete-cycle and separated-batch facts]\label{prop:standard-complete-cycle-separated-batch-facts-main}
Let \((A_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}\) be a stationary binary renewal process with
click epochs \((\tau_j)\), i.i.d. gaps \(G_j\), cycle lengths
\(L_j=G_j+1\), mean \(\mu=\EE L_0\in(0,\infty)\), and
\(\EE e^{\eta G_0}<\infty\) for some \(\eta>0\).  Let
\(K_N=\max\{k:\tau_k<N\}\), with \(K_N=-1\) if no click is observed.  The
following standard regenerative conclusions are used in the main text
\cite{GlynnIglehart1990STS,AsmussenGlynn2007,GlynnWhitt1991BatchMeans,
VatsFlegalJones2019Multivariate}.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=2.4em,itemsep=0.25em]
\item Every bounded local window
\[
Z_n=\psi(A_{n-r},\ldots,A_{n+\ell}),\qquad \bar z=\EE Z_0,
\]
has a complete-cycle reward
\[
U_j=\sum_{n=\tau_j}^{\tau_{j+1}-1}Z_n,\qquad
Y_j=U_j-\bar zL_j,
\]
with Palm centering
\begin{equation}\label{eq:local-window-palm-inversion-main}
\EE U_j=\mu\bar z,\qquad \EE Y_j=0 .
\end{equation}
Moreover \(Y_j\) is a measurable function of finitely many adjacent gaps and
is therefore fixed-range dependent.  Endpoint and fixed look-ahead/look-back
trimming changes the calendar sum by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:local-window-endpoint-main}
\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}Z_n-\sum_j U_j=O_{\PP}(\log N),
\end{equation}
where the cycle sum is over the complete cycles intersecting the observed
calendar window, with the same \(O_{\PP}(\log N)\) bound after any fixed
endpoint trimming.

\item If \(Y_j=f(G_j,\ldots,G_{j+m_{\rm dep}})\in\RR^{d_{\rm rew}}\),
\(\EE Y_j=0\), and
\[
\|f(g_0,\ldots,g_{m_{\rm dep}})\|
\le C_f\left(1+\sum_{i=0}^{m_{\rm dep}}g_i\right),
\]
then, for any all-complete-cycle index set \(J_N\) obtained from
\(\{0,\ldots,K_N-1\}\) by deleting only fixed endpoint/look-ahead indices,
\[
\sqrt N\,\frac1N\sum_{j\in J_N}Y_j
\Rightarrow
\mathcal N\left(0,\frac{\mathcal T_{m_{\rm dep}}}{\mu}\right),
\]
where
\[
\mathcal T_{m_{\rm dep}}
=\Var(Y_0)+
\sum_{h=1}^{m_{\rm dep}}
\{\operatorname{Cov}(Y_0,Y_h)+\operatorname{Cov}(Y_h,Y_0)\}.
\]

\item For \(b_N=\lfloor N^\beta\rfloor\), \(0<\beta<1\),
\(d_N=b_N+m_{\rm dep}\), and separated batches
\[
I_{\ell,N}:=\{(\ell-1)d_N,\ldots,(\ell-1)d_N+b_N-1\},
\qquad
C_{\ell,N}=\sum_{j=(\ell-1)d_N}^{(\ell-1)d_N+b_N-1}Y_j ,
\]
let \(M_N\) be the number of all-complete-cycle batches retained before
calendar time \(N\), and put
\(\bar C_N=M_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_N}C_{\ell,N}\) on \(M_N\ge2\).  Then the
retained batch covariance satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:separated-batch-covariance-estimator-rate-main}
\left\|
\frac{K_N}{N}\frac1{b_N(M_N-1)}
\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_N}(C_{\ell,N}-\bar C_N)(C_{\ell,N}-\bar C_N)^\top
-\frac{\mathcal T_{m_{\rm dep}}}{\mu}
\right\|_{\operatorname{op}}
=O_{\PP}\left(b_N^{-1}+\sqrt{b_N/N}\right).
\end{equation}
Equivalently, before multiplying by \(K_N/N\), the cycle-time sample covariance
estimates \(\mathcal T_{m_{\rm dep}}\) at the same rate.

\item If plug-in rewards have the form
\[
\widehat Y_j=Y_j-(\widehat r_N-r)L_j,\qquad
\widehat r_N-r=O_{\PP}(N^{-1/2}),
\]
and \(b_N\) is polynomial, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:separated-batch-plugin-block-main}
\max_{\ell\le M_N}
\left\|\sum_{j\in I_{\ell,N}}(\widehat Y_j-Y_j)\right\|
=O_{\PP}(b_NN^{-1/2})
\end{equation}
and replacing \(Y_j\) by \(\widehat Y_j\) in the separated-batch covariance
changes it by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:separated-batch-plugin-covariance-main}
O_{\PP}\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{b_N}{N}}\right)
+O_{\PP}\!\left(\frac{b_N}{N}\right).
\end{equation}

\item For every fixed \(C\), \(\PP(K_N<C)\to0\), and the same conclusion holds
after deleting any fixed number of endpoint, look-back, or look-ahead cycles.

\item If \(b_N=\lfloor N^\beta\rfloor\), \(0<\beta<1\), and
\(M_N=O_{\PP}(N/b_N)\), then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:uniform-calendar-block-length-main}
\max_{1\le \ell\le M_N}
\frac1{b_N}\sum_{j\in I_{\ell,N}}L_j
=O_{\PP}(1).
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The only model-specific input to this proposition is that the click epochs
form a stationary renewal process with an exponential gap moment.  The
Palm-cycle identity gives
\[
\EE Z_0=\frac{\EE U_j}{\EE L_j},\qquad
U_j=\sum_{n=\tau_j}^{\tau_{j+1}-1}Z_n,
\]
and hence \(\EE U_j=\mu\bar z\) and \(\EE Y_j=0\).  Because \(Z_n\) is a fixed
local window, \(Y_j\) depends on only finitely many adjacent gaps; call this
range \(m_{\rm dep}\).  Exponential tails imply that the largest cycle
intersecting any fixed enlargement of \([0,N-1]\) is \(O_{\PP}(\log N)\), so
endpoint, look-ahead, and look-back deletions give
\eqref{eq:local-window-endpoint-main}.

The CLT and the calendar-time scale are the standard regenerative-reward
facts: apply the ordinary finite-range-dependent CLT to the stationary
sequence \(Y_j=f(G_j,\ldots,G_{j+m_{\rm dep}})\), then use the renewal law of
large numbers \(K_N/N\to1/\mu\) and the usual random-index replacement
\cite[Chs.~IV.3 and VI.3]{AsmussenGlynn2007}.  This gives the covariance
\(\mathcal T_{m_{\rm dep}}/\mu\).

For the separated-batch estimator, apply the fixed-range wrapper
\Cref{prop:calendar-stopped-separated-batch-plugin-main} to the gap reward
\(Y_j=f(G_j,\ldots,G_{j+m_{\rm dep}})\), with \(q\) fixed endpoint and
look-ahead cycles deleted by the particular complete-cycle set.  It gives the
random calendar-stopped batch count bound
\(M_N=K_N/(b_N+m_{\rm dep})+O_{\PP}(\sqrt N/b_N+1)\), controls the maximal
deleted endpoint cycle, subtracts the empirical batch mean, and gives exactly
\eqref{eq:separated-batch-covariance-estimator-rate-main}.

For the plug-in perturbation, write
\(\Delta_N=\widehat r_N-r=O_{\PP}(N^{-1/2})\).  Each batch changes by
\[
\widehat C_{\ell,N}-C_{\ell,N}
=-\Delta_N\sum_{j\in I_{\ell,N}}L_j .
\]
\Cref{prop:calendar-stopped-separated-batch-plugin-main} gives the uniform
block-length bound, the block perturbation
\eqref{eq:separated-batch-plugin-block-main}, and the covariance perturbation
\eqref{eq:separated-batch-plugin-covariance-main}.  Finally,
\((K_N+1)/N\to1/\mu\) gives the fixed-low-cycle statement, and the preceding
uniform block-length bound is exactly \eqref{eq:uniform-calendar-block-length-main}.
\end{proof}

\ifdefined\SUPPLEMENTARYFULLPROTOCOLS
\subsection{Finite-domain diagonal certification for implementation extensions}
\label{app:finite-domain-diagonal-certification-main}

The submitted manuscript uses only the point certificate at \(z=1/2\).  The
following interval-cover verifier is retained as implementation machinery for a
future extension that prints additional point or interval transcripts.  It is
not a paper-level theorem claim for any candidate outside \(z=1/2\).

\begin{algorithmiclemma}[Finite interval-cover diagonal branch certification]\label{lem:diagonal-certified-interval-cover-main}
Let \(I=[z^-,z^+]\Subset(0,1)\) be a compact diagonal candidate interval that
is reported as coverage-certified in an implementation extension.  The
deterministic branch verifier is as follows.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.4em,itemsep=0.25em]
\item Start with the queue containing \(I\) and with an empty certified list
\(\mathcal C\).
\item Remove one interval \(J\) from the queue.  Apply the outward-rounded
evaluation in \Cref{lem:diagonal-interval-branch-certificate-main} on the
whole interval \(J\).
\item If exactly one of the four branch tests in
\Cref{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main} succeeds on \(J\), append
\((J,\mathrm{branch})\) to \(\mathcal C\).
\item If no branch test succeeds and the prescribed maximum subdivision depth,
precision budget, or exact-symbolic fallback has not been exhausted, bisect
\(J\) and return the two children to the queue.
\item If no branch test succeeds after the declared resources are exhausted,
append \(J\) to the undecided list \(\mathcal U\).
\end{enumerate}

The extension transcript contains the input interval \(I\), the precision and
rounding mode, every terminal interval, the branch label and margin for every
interval in \(\mathcal C\), the undecided list \(\mathcal U\), and an exact
rational endpoint check proving
\[
I=\bigcup_{(J,\mathrm{branch})\in\mathcal C}J\ \cup\
\bigcup_{J\in\mathcal U}J
\]
with disjoint interiors.  The interval \(I\) is a certified extension interval
only when this verifier returns a finite terminal list and
\(\mathcal U=\varnothing\).  In that case
\[
I=\bigcup_{j=1}^M I_j
\]
and directed interval evaluation proves exactly one branch condition on each
\(I_j\).  Therefore every candidate \(z\in I\) belongs to a certified
subinterval on which the population branch of
\(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) is fixed.  If \(\mathcal U\ne\varnothing\), the union of
the undecided intervals is displayed and those candidates remain diagnostic.
\end{algorithmiclemma}

\begin{proof}
All branch assertions made on a terminal interval are consequences of
\Cref{lem:diagonal-interval-branch-certificate-main}, so each accepted
terminal interval has a proved population branch for every \(z\) in that
interval.  The four branch outcomes in
\Cref{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main} are mutually exclusive for the
actual nonnegative definite matrix \(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) by
\Cref{lem:dmap-diagonal-covariance-alternatives-main}.  Hence two distinct
branch labels cannot both be valid at the same population point; the verifier
therefore accepts a terminal interval only when its directed enclosures prove a
single outcome uniformly over the interval.

The equality of the endpoint union is a finite rational check in the transcript,
independent of floating-point arithmetic.  When the undecided list is empty,
the accepted terminal intervals cover all of \(I\), and every point in \(I\)
inherits the unique branch proved on the terminal interval containing it.  If
the list is nonempty, no coverage-certified extension is invoked on that
undecided subunion.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Diagonal branch certificates}\label{app:diagonal-branch-certificate-protocol-main}

This subsection contains the finite branch-certificate convention and
outward-rounded verifier used by Theorem~E.  It is implementation certificate
machinery for the analytic covariance alternatives of
\Cref{lem:dmap-diagonal-covariance-alternatives-main}.

\begin{definition}[Certified diagonal covariance branch]\label{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main}
Fix \(0<z<1\) and form the actual D-MAP covariance
\(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) by \eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-finite-main}.  Put
\[
n_z=(-z,1)^\top,\qquad t_z=(1,z)^\top .
\]
For each reported diagonal candidate \(z\), a diagonal branch certificate at
\(z\) is the following finite object.
It contains:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)},leftmargin=2.4em,itemsep=0.2em]
\item an exact description of the input \(z\), or an interval enclosure
\([z]\Subset(0,1)\) if the reported branch is asserted uniformly on that
input interval;
\item an outward-rounded enclosure \([\theta]\) of
\(\theta=-\log z\), or a symbolic identity for \(\theta\);
\item outward-rounded interval enclosures for every scalar arithmetic operation
in \eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-r-finite-main} and
\eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-finite-main};
\item the three outward-rounded branch quantities
\[
[I_{\tau}]\supset \operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z),\qquad
[I_{\det}]\supset \det\Sigma_\sigma(z),\qquad
[w]\supset \Sigma_\sigma(z)t_z,
\]
computed from the enclosed matrix by the directed-rounding formulas in
\Cref{lem:diagonal-interval-branch-certificate-main}.
\item in the rank-one non-normal branch, an outward-rounded enclosure
\[
[a_{\rm rn}]
\supset
\left(
1-\frac{n_z^\top\Sigma_\sigma(z)n_z}
{\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)\,\|n_z\|^2}
\right)^2
\]
of the scalar projected-line scale used in
\Cref{lem:certified-rank-one-nonnormal-projected-gaussian-quantile-main}.
\end{enumerate}
The certificate transcript printed in the manuscript, or an explicitly
included appendix transcript, must specify the precision, rounding mode, and
the displayed branch margin \(\eta>0\) whenever it asserts a strict positive
inequality.  A repository script may reproduce the transcript, but the
coverage-certified branch status is attached to the printed interval
transcript, not to an undisplayed local file.  This branch transcript is only
one component of a finite diagonal report certificate.  A realized
finite-record accept/reject/undecided output additionally requires the
record-specific critical-value bracket and statistic interval in the tuple
\(\mathcal C(z,\alpha,N)\) of
\Cref{thm:certified-diagonal-inference-main}.  Equalities used to assert a
rank-deficient branch must be exact equalities, either symbolic identities or
interval enclosures of width zero in the certified arithmetic; a small
floating-point residual is not an equality certificate.

The four admissible certified outcomes are:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=2.4em,itemsep=0.25em]
\item \textbf{Full rank.}  The certificate proves
\[
[I_{\det}]\subset[\eta,\infty).
\]
\item \textbf{Rank one, normal range.}  The certificate proves
\[
[I_{\det}]=[0,0],\qquad
[I_{\tau}]\subset[\eta,\infty),\qquad
[w]=\{(0,0)^\top\}.
\]
\item \textbf{Rank one, non-normal range.}  The certificate proves
\[
[I_{\det}]=[0,0],\qquad
[I_{\tau}]\subset[\eta,\infty),\qquad
[q]\subset[\eta,\infty),
\]
where \([q]\) is the outward-rounded enclosure of
\(\|w\|^2=w_1^2+w_2^2\) obtained from \([w]\), and also supplies
\([a_{\rm rn}]\Subset(0,1]\).
\item \textbf{Zero covariance.}  The certificate proves
\[
\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0
\]
entrywise, equivalently \(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0\) for this
nonnegative definite matrix.
\end{enumerate}
If none of these certificates is available, the diagonal rank branch is
declared inconclusive.  An inconclusive branch may still be used to display the
projected-Gaussian diagnostic \(Q_N(z)\) and the ideal conditional quantile,
but it is not a coverage-certified report in Theorem~E.  Conversely, even a
conclusive branch certificate is not by itself a finite decision transcript:
it must be paired with \([L,U]\) and \([Q]\) in
\(\mathcal C(z,\alpha,N)\).

The certification convention is deliberately finite.  This paper does not use
an unproved global analytic sign classification of
\(\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) on \(0<z<1\), and a floating-point eigenvalue
calculation at a candidate is not a substitute for a certificate.  The worked
certificate in \Cref{rem:worked-diagonal-branch-certificate-main} supplies only
the single submitted candidate \(z=1/2\); no continuum branch classification
and no neighbouring-point certificate is inferred from it.  The finite-domain
interval-cover machinery needed for a later implementation extension is not
part of the paper-level theorem and is recorded in
\Cref{app:finite-domain-diagonal-certification-main}.
\end{definition}

\begin{algorithmiclemma}[Outward-rounded diagonal branch certificate]\label{lem:diagonal-interval-branch-certificate-main}
For a fixed point \(0<z<1\), or for a closed input interval
\([z]\Subset(0,1)\), the branch certificate in
\Cref{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main} is reproducibly obtained from
the finite formulas of \Cref{prop:computable-diagonal-covariance-main} as
follows.
Work in an interval arithmetic system with directed rounding.  Enclose the
input by \([z]\), enclose \(\theta=-\log z\) over that whole input enclosure by
\([\theta]\), and then evaluate the displayed formulas
\[
[g_0]=(1-[z])-[\theta][z],
\qquad
[g_1]=[z]\{(1-[z])(1+[\theta])-[\theta][z]\},
\]
\[
[\mu]=\frac1{1-[z]}+\frac{[\theta][z]}{(1-[z])^2},
\qquad
[\nu]=\frac{1+[z]}{(1-[z])^2}
     +\frac{[\theta][z](3+[z])}{(1-[z])^3},
\qquad
[m_2]=[g_1]+[g_0]^2.
\]
Set
\[
[r]=\frac1{[\mu]}(1,[g_0],[m_2])^\top
\]
and form the interval matrices \([A_z]\), \([B_z]\) and interval vectors
\([e_z]\), \([d_z]\) from the displayed formulas immediately preceding
\eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-r-finite-main}.  Directed evaluation of
\[
[\Sigma_r]=\frac1{[\mu]}\left\{
[A_z]-[e_z][r]^\top-[r][e_z]^\top+[\nu][r][r]^\top
+[B_z]-[d_z][r]^\top+[B_z]^\top-[r][d_z]^\top
\right\}
\]
encloses the regenerative covariance.
Next compute the quotient-Jacobian interval \([J_\Phi]\) from
\eqref{eq:lambda-gradient-main}--\eqref{eq:phi-jacobian-main}, with every
division checked to have a denominator interval not containing zero, and put
\[
[\Sigma]=[J_\Phi]\,[\Sigma_r]\,[J_\Phi]^\top .
\]
Writing
\[
[\Sigma]=\begin{pmatrix}
[a]&[b]\\
[c]&[d]
\end{pmatrix},
\]
the branch quantities required by \Cref{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main}
are not optional diagnostics but the certificate data:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:diagonal-branch-interval-quantities-main}
[I_{\tau}]=[a]+[d],\qquad
[I_{\det}]=[a][d]-[b][c],\qquad
[w]=
\binom{[a]+[z][b]}{[c]+[z][d]},
\qquad
[q]=[w_1]^2+[w_2]^2 .
\end{equation}
For a rank-one non-normal outcome, also compute the scalar-law enclosure
\begin{equation}\label{eq:diagonal-rank-one-nonnormal-scale-certificate-main}
[a_{\rm rn}]
=\left(
1-\frac{[n]^\top[\Sigma][n]}{[I_{\tau}]\,([z]^2+1)}
\right)^2,
\qquad [n]=(-[z],1)^\top .
\end{equation}
If the intervals in \eqref{eq:diagonal-branch-interval-quantities-main}
satisfy one of the four certified outcomes in
\Cref{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main}, then the corresponding
population branch of \(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) is proved for the fixed candidate,
or uniformly for every candidate in the certified input interval.  If none of
the interval separations succeeds, the branch is reported as inconclusive.
\end{algorithmiclemma}

\begin{proof}
The formulas for \(g_0,g_1,\mu,\nu,m_2,r,A_z,e_z,d_z,B_z\) are exactly the
finite D-MAP covariance formulas of
\Cref{prop:computable-diagonal-covariance-main}.  Directed interval arithmetic
is inclusion isotone for addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division
by an interval excluding zero.  Therefore each displayed interval contains the
corresponding real scalar or matrix entry.  The quotient denominator is
nonzero at every fixed diagonal point by
\eqref{eq:diagonal-quotient-denominator-main}, so sufficiently sharp input
enclosures make the Jacobian divisions certified.  The sandwich product then
contains the real covariance
\(\Sigma_\sigma(z)=D\Phi(r(z))\Sigma_r(z)D\Phi(r(z))^\top\).  Finally,
\eqref{eq:diagonal-branch-interval-quantities-main} is precisely the directed
interval evaluation of
\(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)\), \(\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)\),
\(\Sigma_\sigma(z)(1,z)^\top\), and its squared norm.  Interval exclusion from
zero proves the stated strict inequalities, while a zero-width interval or a
symbolic identity proves the asserted equalities.  The branch conclusion is
then the \(2\times2\) nonnegative-definite rank/range classification of
\Cref{lem:dmap-diagonal-covariance-alternatives-main}.  In the rank-one
non-normal case, write
\(\Sigma_\sigma(z)=\lambda vv^\top\), \(\lambda>0\), \(\|v\|=1\).  Since
\(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=\lambda\),
\[
\frac{n_z^\top\Sigma_\sigma(z)n_z}
{\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)\|n_z\|^2}
=\frac{(n_z^\top v)^2}{\|n_z\|^2},
\]
so \eqref{eq:diagonal-rank-one-nonnormal-scale-certificate-main} encloses the
scale \(a(z,v)\) in
\Cref{lem:certified-rank-one-nonnormal-projected-gaussian-quantile-main}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Worked diagonal branch certificate]\label{rem:worked-diagonal-branch-certificate-main}
The self-contained certificate used by this manuscript is the interval
transcript in \Cref{app:self-contained-diagonal-branch-certificate-main}.  The
paper-local script, stored JSON transcript, replay environment, command lines,
and transcript hash are supplementary reproducibility material.  The main
article uses only the printed interval transcript and its proved determinant
margin.  The accepted arithmetic is base-ten decimal interval arithmetic with
precision \(90\) significant digits and directed rounding downward for every
lower endpoint and upward for every upper endpoint; the input interval and all
branch enclosures are printed in
\Cref{app:self-contained-diagonal-branch-certificate-main}.  Thus the
certificate used below is tied to the printed formulas rather than to a
rounded midpoint table.

For this point certificate the exact substitution into
\eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-r-finite-main} is
\[
z=\frac12,\qquad
\theta=\log2,\qquad
g_0=\frac{1-\log2}{2},\qquad
g_1=\frac14,
\]
\[
\mu=2+2\log2,\qquad
m_2=g_1+g_0^2 .
\]
Substituting these values in \eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-r-finite-main} and
then in
\(\Sigma_\sigma(z)=D\Phi(r(z))\Sigma_r(z)D\Phi(r(z))^\top\), the directed
interval transcript encloses the entries of \(\Sigma_\sigma(1/2)\) as follows:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Sigma_{11}&\in[25.0645227916080864,25.0645227916080865],\\
\Sigma_{12}&\in[17.2222593244352288,17.2222593244352289],\\
\Sigma_{21}&\in[17.2222593244352288,17.2222593244352289],\\
\Sigma_{22}&\in[11.8884649865292259,11.8884649865292260].
\end{aligned}
\]
The branch decision uses these outward-rounded intervals directly; no rounded
midpoint matrix is used in the certificate.
\[
\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(1/2)
\doteq 36.9529877781373,
\qquad
\det\Sigma_\sigma(1/2)
\doteq 1.37248537400032.
\]
The appendix transcript records outward-rounded enclosures of all these
displayed quantities; in short display form, the corresponding branch
intervals are
\[
\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(1/2)
\in[36.95298777813731,36.95298777813732],
\]
\[
\det\Sigma_\sigma(1/2)
\in[1.372485374000321,1.372485374000322].
\]
These two intervals are deliberately rounded outward for compact display; the
full precision determinant, trace, matrix, tangent-vector, rounding-mode, and
input intervals are part of the manuscript in
\Cref{app:self-contained-diagonal-branch-certificate-main}.  The determinant
enclosure is separated from zero, so the certificate proves the full-rank
branch with margin, for instance, \(\eta=1.37\).  The same transcript
also records the outward-rounded vector enclosure for
\(\Sigma_\sigma(1/2)(1,1/2)^\top\); it is not needed for the full-rank
decision but is included because the branch protocol always records the
tangent-direction test.
This is a point certificate only: it certifies the full-rank branch for the
single reported candidate \(z=1/2\), not for neighbouring \(z\)'s and not for
the continuum \(0<z<1\).
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[D-MAP diagonal covariance alternatives]\label{lem:dmap-diagonal-covariance-alternatives-main}
Work at a fixed constrained D-MAP exchange-diagonal population point
\(\sigma_z=(2z,z^2)\), \(0<z<1\), and form the actual diagonal covariance
\(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) by the finite formula
\eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-finite-main}.  Let \(n_z=(-z,1)^\top\).  Exactly
one of the following mutually exclusive
alternatives holds:
\[
\operatorname{rank}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=2,
\]
\[
\operatorname{rank}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=1
\quad\text{and}\quad
\operatorname{Range}\Sigma_\sigma(z)\ne\operatorname{span}\{n_z\},
\]
\[
\operatorname{rank}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=1
\quad\text{and}\quad
\operatorname{Range}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=\operatorname{span}\{n_z\},
\]
or
\[
\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0 .
\]
The first two alternatives have a continuous projected-Gaussian statistic and
therefore supply exact-level projected-Gaussian cases for all confidence
levels.  In the third alternative the limiting statistic has law
\(\frac12\delta_0+\frac12\chi^2_1\): its distribution function is
\(1/2+F_{\chi^2_1}(t)/2\) for \(t>0\).  Hence its lower \(p_c\)-quantile is
zero for \(p_c\le1/2\), but for \(p_c>1/2\) it is
\(F_{\chi^2_1}^{-1}(2p_c-1)\) and is continuous.  The
fourth alternative has an identically zero limiting statistic.  The occurrence
of the covariance alternative is not a modelling choice: it is obtained by
evaluating the finite matrix
\eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-finite-main}.  The paper does not prove a
closed-form analytic sign classification of this determinant for every
\(0<z<1\).  Therefore the operational diagonal coverage branches in
Theorem~E are conditional on the certified population branch in
\Cref{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main}, operationally generated by
\Cref{lem:diagonal-interval-branch-certificate-main}, not on a global
closed-form \(z\)-classification and not on an uncertified floating-point rank
label.  In
the rank-one-normal covariance
alternative, the theorem-level branch still depends on the requested quantile
level \(p_c=1-\alpha\): exact unbuffered coverage for \(p_c>1/2\),
and buffered conservative coverage for \(p_c\le1/2\).

Equivalently, because \(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) is \(2\times2\) and nonnegative
definite, these cases are checked directly from the actual D-MAP covariance by
\[
\operatorname{rank}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)>0,
\]
\[
\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0,
\]
and, with \(t_z=(1,z)^\top\) tangent to the exchange diagonal,
\[
\operatorname{Range}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=\operatorname{span}\{n_z\}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0,\quad
\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)>0,\quad
\Sigma_\sigma(z)t_z=0 .
\]
The remaining case
\[
\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0,\quad
\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)>0,\quad
\Sigma_\sigma(z)t_z\ne0
\]
is the rank-one non-normal exact-level alternative.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The matrix \(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) is a \(2\times2\) nonnegative definite matrix
because it is obtained by sandwiching the nonnegative definite regenerative
covariance \(\Sigma_r(z)\) with the deterministic Jacobian \(D\Phi(r(z))\).
Thus its rank is \(0\), \(1\), or \(2\).  In rank one its range is a single
line, which is either the normal line \(\operatorname{span}\{n_z\}\) or is not
that line.  These alternatives are exhaustive and mutually exclusive.

For a \(2\times2\) nonnegative definite matrix, full rank is equivalent to
positive determinant, and the zero matrix is equivalent to zero trace.  In the
remaining rank-one case, \(\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0\) and
\(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)>0\).  Since
\(t_z=(1,z)^\top\) spans the tangent line orthogonal to \(n_z=(-z,1)^\top\),
the range is \(\operatorname{span}\{n_z\}\) exactly when the kernel is the
tangent line, equivalently \(\Sigma_\sigma(z)t_z=0\).  If this kernel test
fails, the rank-one range is not the normal line.  The statements about
continuity, the half-mass at zero, and the zero statistic are precisely
\Cref{thm:projected-gaussian-continuity-degeneracy-main} applied to
\(\Sigma=\Sigma_\sigma(z)\).  The certificate definition is only the same
case analysis written as a reproducible branch-selection rule: each positive
inequality gives the displayed margin, and each asserted rank deficiency is
accepted only when the corresponding equality has been proved exactly.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Model verification.}
We now specialize the generic renewal tools to the standing record experiment
of \Cref{ass:fixed-sampled-boundary-record-main}.  The exponential-tail lemma
verifies the renewal hypothesis for this model.  Theorem~C then states the
exact finite-record statistic for the three inclusion coordinates and applies
the generic complete-cycle CLT to that statistic.


\subsection{Finite projected-Gaussian certificates}\label{app:finite-projected-gaussian-certificates-main}

This subsection contains the mechanical quantile brackets, midpoint-undecided
outputs, DKW simulation domination, and finite diagonal report conventions
cross-referenced from Theorem~E.  These are executable certificate protocols,
not additional paper-level theorem targets.

\begin{algorithmiclemma}[Certified deterministic projected-Gaussian quantile bracket]\label{lem:certified-deterministic-projected-gaussian-quantile-main}
Fix \(0<z<1\), \(0<q<1\), and a positive definite \(2\times2\) covariance
matrix \(\Sigma\).  Suppose the data used by the numerical report are given by
outward-rounded interval enclosures \([z]\), \([\Sigma]\), and \([Q]\), where
\([Q]\) contains the computed statistic \(Q\).  Then the lower quantile
\[
c_q(z,\Sigma)=\inf\{c\ge0:F_{z,\Sigma}(c)\ge q\}
\]
from \Cref{lem:deterministic-full-rank-projected-gaussian-quantile-main} has
a reproducible deterministic \emph{bracket} certificate of the following form.
The routine certifies endpoint containment and leaves unresolved midpoint
comparisons explicitly undecided.  For
any requested abscissa tolerance \(\eta_c>0\), probability tolerance
schedule \((\eta_k)_{k\ge0}\) of positive rationals with \(\eta_k\downarrow0\),
and finite midpoint refinement budget \(J\ge1\), the outward-rounded
computation terminates after finitely many rational split points and returns
one of two transcripts.

The first, called a \emph{resolved bracket}, consists of numbers
\[
L<U,\qquad U-L\le\eta_c,
\]
and certified distribution-function enclosures at the two endpoints satisfying
\[
F^+(L)<q\le F^-(U).
\]
The second, called an \emph{undecided but bracketed midpoint}, consists of a
current bracket \(L<U\), a rational split point \(m\in(L,U)\), and certified
distribution-function enclosures satisfying
\[
F^+(L)<q\le F^-(U),\qquad
F^-(m)<q\le F^+(m).
\]
In either case the transcript certifies the quantile bracket
\[
L<c_q(z,\Sigma)\le U.
\]
The undecided transcript is a legitimate finite output: it records that the
available outward-rounded calculation has not decided on which side of the
ideal lower quantile the split point lies, and it does not assert equality or
force an accept/reject decision at \(m\).

Moreover any resolved or undecided bracket gives a rigorous comparison of
\(Q\) with the ideal quantile whenever the certified intervals are separated:
\[
[Q]^+\le L\quad\Longrightarrow\quad Q<c_q(z,\Sigma),
\]
and
\[
[Q]^->U\quad\Longrightarrow\quad Q>c_q(z,\Sigma).
\]
If neither separation holds, the routine returns the certified statement
\[
Q-c_q(z,\Sigma)\in
\bigl[[Q]^--U,\,[Q]^+-L\bigr],
\]
so the only undecided cases are those lying within the declared numerical
quantile/statistic enclosure.

The computation is the following one.  First compute an outward-rounded
Cholesky enclosure \([C]\) for \(\Sigma=C C^\top\), together with interval
enclosures for \(\Sigma^{-1}\).  Write \(Y\sim\mathcal N(0,I_2)\) and
\(Z=CY\).  For a requested CDF tolerance \(\eta>0\), choose \(R=R(\eta)>0\)
so that the certified Mills-ratio bound
\begin{equation}\label{eq:certified-gaussian-tail-truncation-main}
4\,\frac{\exp(-R^2/2)}{R\sqrt{2\pi}}\le\eta_{\rm tail}
\end{equation}
holds, with \(0<\eta_{\rm tail}<\eta/4\).  Then
\[
\PP\{\|Y\|_\infty>R\}\le\eta_{\rm tail},
\]
so all probability outside the square \(S_R=[-R,R]^2\) is charged only to the
upper distribution-function bound.

For a candidate value \(c\ge0\), partition \(S_R\) into finitely many closed
axis-parallel boxes \(B\).  On each box use directed interval arithmetic to
enclose
\[
s_B=n_{[z]}^\top [C]B,\qquad
q_B^{\rm in}=([C]B)^\top[\Sigma^{-1}]([C]B),
\]
and, for the exterior projected region,
\[
[P_z u]
=u-\frac{(u_2-[z]u_1)_+}{1+[z]^2}\binom{-[z]}{1},
\qquad
q_B^{\rm out}=([P_z C B])^\top[\Sigma^{-1}]([P_z C B]).
\]
The lower sum \(F^-(c)\) adds the exact product-normal mass
\[
\gamma(B)=
\{\Phi(b_1)-\Phi(a_1)\}\{\Phi(b_2)-\Phi(a_2)\},
\qquad B=[a_1,b_1]\times[a_2,b_2],
\]
for every box certified to lie in the first projected region and satisfy
\((q_B^{\rm in})^+\le c\), and for every box certified to lie in the second
