projected region and satisfy \((q_B^{\rm out})^+\le c\).  The upper sum
\(F^+(c)\) adds \(\gamma(B)\) for every box not certified to be outside the
corresponding event, namely for boxes whose interval tests do not prove
\(s_B>0\) or \((q_B^{\rm in})^->c\) in the inside integral, and do not prove
\(s_B\le0\) or \((q_B^{\rm out})^->c\) in the outside integral.  Finally set
\[
F^-(c)=\sum_{\text{certified inside/outside accepted boxes}}\gamma(B),
\qquad
F^+(c)=\eta_{\rm tail}+\sum_{\text{not certified rejected boxes}}\gamma(B).
\]
Then
\[
F^-(c)\le F_{z,\Sigma}(c)\le F^+(c).
\]
For each rational \(c\ge0\) and each rational tolerance \(\eta>0\), choose
the corresponding \(R(\eta)\), build the square \(S_{R(\eta)}\), and refine
the partition until \(F^+(c)-F^-(c)\le\eta\).  Denote this finite subroutine
by \(\mathsf{CDF}(c,\eta)\).

The bracket construction is mechanical.  First run
\(\mathsf{CDF}(0,\eta_j)\), \(j=0,1,\ldots\), until \(F^+(0)<q\), and set
\(L=0\).  Next dovetail the dyadic upper search: for stages
\(s=0,1,2,\ldots\), compute \(\mathsf{CDF}(2^r,\eta_s)\) for every
\(0\le r\le s\), using rational directed arithmetic at each dyadic point.
Stop at the first stage \(s\) for which some inspected dyadic point satisfies
\(q\le F^-(2^r)\), and choose the smallest such \(r\) as \(U=2^r\).  The
stored endpoint certificates give the invariant
\[
F^+(L)<q\le F^-(U).
\]

Let
\[
K=\max\left\{0,\left\lceil\log_2\frac{U-L}{\eta_c}\right\rceil\right\}.
\]
For \(k=1,\ldots,K\), form the rational midpoint \(m=(L+U)/2\).  Run
\(\mathsf{CDF}(m,\eta_0),\ldots,\mathsf{CDF}(m,\eta_J)\).  If some certified
enclosure has \(F^+(m)<q\), replace \(L\) by \(m\) and keep the certificate
for the new lower endpoint.  If some certified enclosure has
\(q\le F^-(m)\), replace \(U\) by \(m\) and keep the certificate for the new
upper endpoint.  If, after the \(J+1\) prescribed refinements,
\[
F^-(m)<q\le F^+(m),
\]
return the undecided-but-bracketed transcript with the current endpoint
certificates and the midpoint certificate.  If no undecided midpoint is
returned during the \(K\) passes, return the resolved bracket \((L,U]\); its
length is at most \(\eta_c\) and its endpoint certificates still satisfy
\(F^+(L)<q\le F^-(U)\).
\end{algorithmiclemma}

\begin{proof}
The transformation \(Z=CY\) reduces the Gaussian density to the product
standard-normal density.  The bound
\eqref{eq:certified-gaussian-tail-truncation-main} and the union bound give
the displayed square-truncation error.  On a retained box \(B\), directed
interval arithmetic encloses every value of the half-space sign, the
unprojected quadratic form on \(H_z\), and the projected quadratic form on
\(H_z^c\).  A box added to the lower sum is therefore wholly contained in one
of the two defining events for \(F_{z,\Sigma}(c)\), and a box removed from the
upper sum is wholly contained in the complement of the relevant event.  The
remaining boxes are charged to the upper sum, so
\[
F^-(c)\le F_{z,\Sigma}(c)\le F^+(c)
\]
after adding the tail only to the upper side.

It remains to justify finite termination of each distribution-function
enclosure.  For fixed rational \(c\), the ambiguous set
is contained, up to an arbitrarily small rectangular neighbourhood, in the
union of the line \(n_z^\top C y=0\) and the two quadratic level curves
\((Cy)^\top\Sigma^{-1}(Cy)=c\) and
\((\Pi_{H_z}Cy)^\top\Sigma^{-1}(\Pi_{H_z}Cy)=c\).  These sets have
two-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero.  Since the standard-normal density is
bounded on \(S_R\) and the Gaussian measure is regular, sufficiently fine
rectangular partitions make the total Gaussian mass of undecided boxes below
any prescribed positive value.  Hence the refinement loop achieves
\(F^+(c)-F^-(c)\le\eta\) in finitely many steps for every requested
\(\eta>0\).  This proves finite termination of each call to
\(\mathsf{CDF}(c,\eta)\).

The initial endpoint search is also finite.  At \(c=0\), the no-atom
statement in \Cref{lem:deterministic-full-rank-projected-gaussian-quantile-main}
gives \(F_{z,\Sigma}(0)=\PP\{T_{z,\Sigma}=0\}=0<q\); once
\(\eta<q\), any certified enclosure with width at most \(\eta\) has
\(F^+(0)<q\).  For the upper endpoint,
\(F_{z,\Sigma}(c)\to1\) as \(c\to\infty\), so some dyadic point \(2^r\) has
\(F_{z,\Sigma}(2^r)>q\).  Because the same lemma proves continuity and
strict increase, this inequality is strict at that dyadic point; once the CDF
enclosure is refined below the positive margin
\(F_{z,\Sigma}(2^r)-q\), the certificate has \(F^-(2^r)\ge q\).  Thus the
mechanical endpoint search reaches a certified pair \(L<U\) after finitely
many rational CDF calls.

The certified endpoint inequalities \(F^+(L)<q\) and \(F^-(U)\ge q\) imply
\[
F_{z,\Sigma}(L)<q,\qquad F_{z,\Sigma}(U)\ge q,
\]
and therefore \(L<c_q(z,\Sigma)\le U\).  The bisection loop preserves this
same invariant by construction.  If the midpoint certificate proves
\(F^+(m)<q\), then \(F_{z,\Sigma}(m)<q\), so \(m<c_q(z,\Sigma)\) and \(m\) is
a valid new lower endpoint.  If it proves \(q\le F^-(m)\), then
\(q\le F_{z,\Sigma}(m)\), so \(c_q(z,\Sigma)\le m\) and \(m\) is a valid new
upper endpoint.  If neither side is certified after the prescribed finite
refinement budget, the algorithm returns the explicitly allowed undecided
midpoint transcript; the stored endpoint certificates still imply
\(L<c_q(z,\Sigma)\le U\), while the midpoint certificate records only
\(F^-(m)<q\le F^+(m)\).  This is a finite certificate of a bracket, not a
claim that the exact midpoint comparison has been resolved.

There are at most \(K\) midpoint passes before the resolved output, and each
pass makes at most \(J+1\) finite CDF calls.  Hence the whole procedure has a
finite transcript.  The final comparison with \([Q]\) follows immediately
from \(L<c_q(z,\Sigma)\le U\) and the fact that \(Q\in[Q]\).
\end{proof}


\begin{lemma}[Certified rank-one non-normal projected-Gaussian quantile]\label{lem:certified-rank-one-nonnormal-projected-gaussian-quantile-main}
Fix \(0<z<1\), put
\[
n_z=(-z,1)^\top,\qquad H_z=\{u:n_z^\top u\le0\},
\]
and let \(\Sigma=\lambda vv^\top\), where \(\lambda>0\),
\(\|v\|=1\), and
\(\operatorname{span}\{v\}\ne\operatorname{span}\{n_z\}\).  Let
\(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma)\) and
\[
T_{z,\Sigma}
=(\Pi_{H_z}Z)^\top\Sigma^+(\Pi_{H_z}Z).
\]
Define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rank-one-nonnormal-scale-main}
c_v(z)=1-\frac{(n_z^\top v)^2}{\|n_z\|^2},
\qquad
a(z,v)=c_v(z)^2 .
\end{equation}
Then \(0<c_v(z)\le1\), hence \(0<a(z,v)\le1\).  One support half-line gives a
\(\chi^2_1\) variate and the other gives \(c_v(z)^2\chi^2_1\), with weights
\(1/2\) and \(1/2\).  Equivalently, for \(c\ge0\)
\begin{equation}\label{eq:rank-one-nonnormal-cdf-main}
F^{(1)}_{z,v}(c)
:=\PP\{T_{z,\Sigma}\le c\}
=\frac12F_{\chi^2_1}(c)
 +\frac12F_{\chi^2_1}\!\left(\frac{c}{a(z,v)}\right).
\end{equation}
The formula is independent of the scale \(\lambda\).  The distribution is
continuous and strictly increasing on \([0,\infty)\), so for \(0<q<1\)
\[
c^{(1)}_q(z,v):=\inf\{c\ge0:F^{(1)}_{z,v}(c)\ge q\}
\]
is the unique exact lower \(q\)-quantile.

Moreover this quantile has a certified one-dimensional construction.  Suppose
a diagonal branch certificate proves the rank-one non-normal branch and gives
an outward-rounded enclosure \([a]\Subset(0,1]\) of the scale
\(a(z,v)\), together with an outward-rounded enclosure \([Q]\) of a reported
statistic.  For every abscissa tolerance \(\eta_c>0\), directed-evaluation
tolerance schedule, and finite midpoint refinement budget, a deterministic
rational bisection returns either a resolved bracket \(L<U\), \(U-L\le\eta_c\),
or an undecided-but-bracketed midpoint transcript.  In both cases the endpoint
certificates satisfy
\[
F^{(1),+}_{[a]}(L)<q\le F^{(1),-}_{[a]}(U),
\]
where, for \(c\ge0\),
\[
F^{(1),-}_{[a]}(c)
=\frac12F_{\chi^2_1}^{-}(c)
 +\frac12F_{\chi^2_1}^{-}\!\left(\frac{c}{[a]^+}\right),
\qquad
F^{(1),+}_{[a]}(c)
=\frac12F_{\chi^2_1}^{+}(c)
 +\frac12F_{\chi^2_1}^{+}\!\left(\frac{c}{[a]^-}\right).
\]
Here \(F_{\chi^2_1}^{-}(x)\le F_{\chi^2_1}(x)\le
F_{\chi^2_1}^{+}(x)\) are directed interval evaluations of
\[
F_{\chi^2_1}(x)=2\Phi(\sqrt x)-1,\qquad x\ge0 .
\]
An undecided midpoint transcript also contains a rational \(m\in(L,U)\) with
\[
F^{(1),-}_{[a]}(m)<q\le F^{(1),+}_{[a]}(m).
\]
Consequently, for either output,
\[
L<c^{(1)}_q(z,v)\le U.
\]
The same transcript certifies the comparison with the ideal quantile:
\[
[Q]^+\le L\Rightarrow Q<c^{(1)}_q(z,v),\qquad
[Q]^->U\Rightarrow Q>c^{(1)}_q(z,v),
\]
and otherwise certifies only
\[
Q-c^{(1)}_q(z,v)\in[[Q]^--U,[Q]^+-L].
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write \(Z=\xi v\), where \(\xi\sim\mathcal N(0,\lambda)\).  Since
\(\Sigma^+=\lambda^{-1}vv^\top\), the inside half-line
\(\{n_z^\top(\xi v)\le0\}\) contributes
\[
T_{z,\Sigma}=\xi^2/\lambda .
\]
On the other half-line,
\[
\Pi_{H_z}(\xi v)
=\xi\left(v-\frac{n_z^\top v}{\|n_z\|^2}n_z\right),
\]
and therefore
\[
T_{z,\Sigma}
=\frac{\xi^2}{\lambda}
\left(1-\frac{(n_z^\top v)^2}{\|n_z\|^2}\right)^2 .
\]
The factor in parentheses is strictly positive because \(v\) is not parallel
to \(n_z\), and it is at most \(1\) by Cauchy's inequality.  The sign of
\(\xi\) is independent of \(\xi^2\), so the two half-lines have equal
probability whenever \(n_z^\top v\ne0\), and the displayed mixture follows.
If \(n_z^\top v=0\), the whole support lies on the boundary of \(H_z\);
then \(c_v(z)=a(z,v)=1\), and the same display reduces to the single
\(\chi^2_1\) law.  This proves
\eqref{eq:rank-one-nonnormal-cdf-main}, continuity, strict increase, and the
exact lower-quantile statement.

For the certificate, monotonicity of \(F_{\chi^2_1}\) and
\([a]\Subset(0,1]\) give the displayed lower and upper enclosures of
\(F^{(1)}_{z,v}(c)\).  The endpoint \(0\) has certified upper value \(0<q\),
and sufficiently large dyadic \(b\) has certified lower value at least \(p\)
because \(F^{(1)}_{z,v}(c)\to1\).  The bisection is exactly the mechanical
rule used above: split the current bracket at a rational midpoint, keep the
left half when the directed upper CDF bound is \(<q\), keep the right half
when the directed lower CDF bound is \(\ge q\), and otherwise stop after the
prescribed finite refinement budget with the displayed undecided midpoint
certificate.  Every accepted endpoint preserves
\(F^{(1),+}_{[a]}(L)<q\le F^{(1),-}_{[a]}(U)\), and therefore
\(L<c^{(1)}_q(z,v)\le U\).  The procedure is finite because it performs only
the prescribed endpoint search and finitely many midpoint evaluations; it
certifies the bracket and does not require a total decision at a midpoint
where the interval comparison straddles \(q\).  The comparison statements
follow from \(Q\in[Q]\) and \(L<c^{(1)}_q(z,v)\le U\).
\end{proof}


\begin{algorithmiclemma}[Certified projected-Gaussian quantile bracketing algorithm]\label{alg:certified-projected-gaussian-quantile-algorithm-long-copy}
Fix \(0<z<1\), a positive definite \(2\times2\) covariance matrix
\(\Sigma\), and \(0<q<1\).  Put
\[
H_z=\{u\in\RR^2:u_2\le zu_1\},\qquad
\Pi_{H_z}u=u-\frac{(u_2-zu_1)_+}{1+z^2}(-z,1)^\top ,
\]
and, with \(\phi_\Sigma\) denoting the density of
\(\mathcal N(0,\Sigma)\), define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:certified-projected-gaussian-cdf-main}
F_{z,\Sigma}(c)
:=\int_{H_z}\mathbf1\{u^\top\Sigma^{-1}u\le c\}\phi_\Sigma(u)\,du
+\int_{H_z^c}
\mathbf1\{(\Pi_{H_z}u)^\top\Sigma^{-1}(\Pi_{H_z}u)\le c\}
\phi_\Sigma(u)\,du .
\end{equation}
The lower projected-Gaussian quantile
\[
c_q(z,\Sigma):=\inf\{c\ge0:F_{z,\Sigma}(c)\ge q\}
\]
is a reproducible mathematical object in the following finite-certificate
sense.  The algorithm certifies an enclosing bracket for the lower quantile
and a comparison with a reported statistic only when the statistic interval is
separated from that bracket; it does not decide all finite-precision
midpoints.

For every abscissa tolerance \(\eta_c>0\), probability tolerance schedule
\((\eta_k)_{k\ge0}\), and finite midpoint refinement budget \(J\), the
deterministic procedure of
\Cref{lem:certified-deterministic-projected-gaussian-quantile-main} produces
a finite transcript consisting of outward-rounded enclosures for \(z\),
\(\Sigma\), \(\Sigma^{-1}\), a Cholesky factor \(C\), a certified tail square
\([-R,R]^2\), finite box partitions of that square, interval lower and upper
distribution sums \(F^-(c)\le F_{z,\Sigma}(c)\le F^+(c)\), rational split
points, and certified endpoints \(L<U\) satisfying the invariant
\[
F^+(L)<q\le F^-(U).
\]
The transcript is of one of the following two forms.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=2.4em,itemsep=0.2em]
\item A resolved bracket, where \(U-L\le\eta_c\).
\item An undecided-but-bracketed midpoint, where the transcript also prints a
rational \(m\in(L,U)\) satisfying
\[
F^-(m)<q\le F^+(m).
\]
\end{enumerate}
Both outputs certify the same theorem-level statement,
\[
L<c_q(z,\Sigma)\le U .
\]
The theorem does not require the finite computation to decide a midpoint whose
outward-rounded distribution-function enclosure straddles \(q\); such a
midpoint is reported as undecided, while the endpoint bracket remains
certified.
If a computed statistic \(Q\) is given by an outward-rounded interval
\([Q]\), the same transcript certifies the comparison with the ideal quantile:
\[
[Q]^+\le L\Rightarrow Q<c_q(z,\Sigma),\qquad
[Q]^->U\Rightarrow Q>c_q(z,\Sigma),
\]
and otherwise certifies only the enclosure
\[
Q-c_q(z,\Sigma)\in[[Q]^--U,[Q]^+-L].
\]

Moreover, conditional finite Monte Carlo simulation is coverage-certified only
after a one-sided domination certificate is attached.  Given conditionally
independent draws \(T_1^\ast,\ldots,T_R^\ast\) from the law with distribution
function \(F_{z,\Sigma}\), let
\[
\widehat F_R(t)=R^{-1}\sum_{m=1}^R\mathbf1_{\{T_m^\ast\le t\}},\qquad
\widehat c_R=T_{(\lceil qR\rceil)}^\ast ,
\]
with the draws sorted increasingly, and let
\[
\varepsilon_{R,\delta}:=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2R}},\qquad
d_{R,\delta}:=
\inf\{d\ge0:\widehat F_R(\widehat c_R+d)-\varepsilon_{R,\delta}\ge q\}.
\]
If \(q+\varepsilon_{R,\delta}<1\), then
\[
\PP^\ast\{\widehat c_R+d_{R,\delta}\ge c_q(z,\Sigma)\}\ge1-\delta .
\]
Thus a raw simulated quantile is diagnostic by itself; the reproducible
coverage-certified simulated critical value is the inflated value
\(\widehat c_R+d_{R,\delta}\), or another value accompanied by an explicitly proved
one-sided domination event of the same form.
\end{algorithmiclemma}

\begin{proof}
The identity \eqref{eq:certified-projected-gaussian-cdf-main} is the
distribution function of
\((\Pi_{H_z}Z)^\top\Sigma^{-1}\Pi_{H_z}Z\),
\(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,\Sigma)\), by
\Cref{lem:deterministic-full-rank-projected-gaussian-quantile-main}.  The
same lemma proves that \(F_{z,\Sigma}\) is continuous and strictly increasing
on \([0,\infty)\).  The interval-integration and bisection procedure in
\Cref{lem:certified-deterministic-projected-gaussian-quantile-main} constructs
the displayed \(F^-,F^+\), rational split points, and endpoint inequalities.
The endpoint inequalities imply
\[
F_{z,\Sigma}(L)\le F^+(L)<q,\qquad
F_{z,\Sigma}(U)\ge F^-(U)\ge q,
\]
so the lower quantile lies in \((L,U]\).  If the output is an undecided
midpoint, the additional displayed inequality is only a record of the
midpoint's unresolved interval comparison and is not used to infer equality or
coverage.  The three comparison statements with \([Q]\) are then immediate
from \(Q\in[Q]\) and \(L<c_q(z,\Sigma)\le U\).

For the simulation statement, the Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz inequality gives
\[
\PP^\ast\{\sup_t|\widehat F_R(t)-F_{z,\Sigma}(t)|
\le\varepsilon_{R,\delta}\}\ge1-\delta .
\]
On this event the defining inequality for \(d_{R,\delta}\) gives
\[
F_{z,\Sigma}(\widehat c_R+d_{R,\delta})
\ge \widehat F_R(\widehat c_R+d_{R,\delta})-\varepsilon_{R,\delta}
\ge q .
\]
By the definition of the lower quantile,
\(\widehat c_R+d_{R,\delta}\ge c_q(z,\Sigma)\).  The stated conditional probability
bound follows.
\end{proof}


\begin{definition}[Finite diagonal report certificate]\label{def:finite-diagonal-report-main}
Fix \(0<\alpha<1\).  A finite diagonal report certificate is the additional
record-specific transcript needed to turn the fixed-null asymptotic theorem
into an executed finite comparison.  It is allowed only at
\[
z_0=\frac12,\qquad \sigma_{z_0}=(2z_0,z_0^2)=(1,1/4),
\]
and only on the reporting event \(\mathcal E_N\).  The present article prints
the \(z_0=1/2\) population branch certificate, but it does not print a
record-specific critical-value bracket or statistic interval.  Consequently
this definition is a reproducibility contract for an implementation transcript,
not an executed finite-record decision in the article.

On \(\mathcal E_N\), compute
\[
Q_N(z_0)=
N(\widehat\sigma_N-\sigma_{z_0})^\top
\widehat\Sigma_{\sigma,N}^{+}
(\widehat\sigma_N-\sigma_{z_0}),
\]
where \(\widehat\Sigma_{\sigma,N}^{+}\) is the retained-rank pseudoinverse
used in \Cref{thm:e-fixed-candidate-exchange-diagonal-main}.  The report must
also carry the population branch certificate for the computable diagonal
covariance \(\Sigma_\sigma(z_0)\) in the sense of
\Cref{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main}.  For the submitted manuscript
this population certificate is the full-rank certificate
\Cref{lem:z-half-diagonal-branch-certificate-main}.

Given this branch certificate, an executed finite report must add the
record-specific components
\[
\mathcal C_N(z_0,\alpha)
=\bigl([z_0],[\widehat\Sigma_{\sigma,N}],[Q_N],[L_N,U_N]\bigr)
\]
or the same tuple with a DKW-dominated simulated critical value in place of
\([L_N,U_N]\).  The critical value must be supplied by exactly one of the
following two routes.  These two routes are exhaustive for the finite-record
certificate interfaces cross-referenced after Theorem~E: a raw simulated
quantile, a finite-sample eigenvalue branch guess, or an undocumented
numerical CDF value is a diagnostic, not a coverage-certified critical value.

\emph{Certified ideal-CDF route.}  Let \(F_N^\ast\) be the conditional CDF of
the ideal projected-Gaussian statistic \(T_N^\ast(z_0)\).  A certified ideal
conditional CDF routine returns outward-rounded functions
\[
F_N^-(c)\le F_N^\ast(c)\le F_N^+(c).
\]
A certified critical-value transcript consists of this CDF bracket, a pair
\(L_N<U_N\) satisfying
\[
F_N^+(L_N)<1-\alpha\le F_N^-(U_N),\qquad
U_N-L_N=o(1).
\]
The statistic computation also returns an outward-rounded interval
\([Q_N]=[[Q_N]^-,[Q_N]^+]\) containing the realized value \(Q_N(z_0)\).
The transcript is converted into a realized finite-record decision only by
\Cref{thm:certified-diagonal-inference-main}.  Without that complete
transcript, no accept/reject decision is asserted; the numerical values are
diagnostic only.
The deterministic routines in
\Cref{thm:certified-projected-gaussian-quantile-algorithm-main,lem:certified-deterministic-projected-gaussian-quantile-main,lem:certified-rank-one-nonnormal-projected-gaussian-quantile-main}
produce exactly such endpoint inequalities on their certified branches.  A
rank-one-normal zero-atom branch or a zero-covariance branch uses the buffered
coverage statement of \Cref{thm:e-fixed-candidate-exchange-diagonal-main};
without the corresponding printed buffered inequality the finite output is
diagnostic only.

\emph{Canonical DKW simulation route.}  Conditional on the observed record,
let \(\PP^\ast\) denote the auxiliary simulation law of
\(T_N^\ast(z_0)\).  This route certifies only a conditional domination
property under \(\PP^\ast\) for the simulated critical value; record
probabilities remain governed by the separate law \(\PP\) and by the
fixed-candidate coverage theorem.  Draw \(N\) projected-Gaussian values from
\(T_N^\ast(z_0)\), sort them increasingly, and set
\[
\widehat c_{N,\mathrm{DKW}}
=T^*_{N,(\lceil(1-\alpha+\epsilon_N^{\rm MC})N\rceil)},\qquad
\epsilon_N^{\rm MC}=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2N^2)}{2N}} .
\]
This route is available only when \(\epsilon_N^{\rm MC}<\alpha\).  Then
\[
\PP^\ast\{\widehat c_{N,\mathrm{DKW}}
\ge c_{1-\alpha,N}^{-,*}\}\ge1-N^{-2},
\]
where \(c_{1-\alpha,N}^{-,*}\) is the ideal lower conditional
\((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(T_N^\ast(z_0)\).  The finite simulation report
uses this critical value in the accept/reject comparison with the interval
\([Q_N]\).  Without the displayed DKW domination statement, simulated
quantiles are diagnostics only.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[Master rule for finite diagonal reports]\label{prop:finite-diagonal-report-master-main}
Under \Cref{ass:finite-record-master-main}, every coverage-certified
exchange-diagonal finite-record decision in this framework must be a finite
diagonal report certificate in the sense of
\Cref{def:finite-diagonal-report-main}.  Equivalently, the operational
certificate is
\[
\text{branch certificate}
\quad+\quad
\bigl(\text{ideal quantile bracket deciding }[Q_N]\bigr),
\]
or
\[
\text{branch certificate}
\quad+\quad
\bigl(R_N=N,\ \delta_N^{\rm MC}=N^{-2}\text{ DKW-inflated empirical quantile}\bigr).
\]
If either the branch certificate or the critical-value certificate is absent,
the projected-Gaussian calculation remains an asymptotic diagnostic and no
coverage-certified finite diagonal report is formed.
In the submitted article the critical-value certificate and the realized
statistic interval are absent, so the finite diagonal report is deliberately
not formed.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The exhaustive alternatives are part of
\Cref{def:finite-diagonal-report-main}; it remains only to verify that the two
allowed critical-value routes dominate or bracket the same ideal conditional
quantile used in the coverage theorem.
For the certified ideal-CDF route, the transcript inequalities
\(F_N^+(L_N)<1-\alpha\le F_N^-(U_N)\) imply
\[
F_N^\ast(L_N)<1-\alpha,\qquad F_N^\ast(U_N)\ge1-\alpha.
\]
Hence the ideal lower conditional quantile
\[
c_{1-\alpha,N}^{-,*}:=\inf\{c:F_N^\ast(c)\ge1-\alpha\}
\]
satisfies \(L_N<c_{1-\alpha,N}^{-,*}\le U_N\).  The realized finite-record
decision is then exactly the interval-separation decision in
\Cref{thm:certified-diagonal-inference-main}: separation certifies the
corresponding side of the ideal inequality, and absence of separation leaves
the finite transcript undecided.

For the DKW route, let \(\widehat F_N^\ast\) be the empirical CDF of the \(N\)
conditional projected-Gaussian draws.  The record is fixed throughout this
paragraph.  Massart's DKW inequality under the auxiliary simulation law
\(\PP^\ast\) gives
\[
\PP^\ast\left\{\sup_c|\widehat F_N^\ast(c)-F_N^\ast(c)|
\le \epsilon_N^{\rm MC}\right\}
\ge
1-2e^{-2N(\epsilon_N^{\rm MC})^2}
=1-N^{-2}.
\]
On this event, at
\(\widehat c_{N,\mathrm{DKW}}
=T^*_{N,(\lceil(1-\alpha+\epsilon_N^{\rm MC})N\rceil)}\),
the empirical CDF satisfies
\[
\widehat F_N^\ast(\widehat c_{N,\mathrm{DKW}})
\ge1-\alpha+\epsilon_N^{\rm MC}.
\]
Therefore
\[
F_N^\ast(\widehat c_{N,\mathrm{DKW}})
\ge
\widehat F_N^\ast(\widehat c_{N,\mathrm{DKW}})
-\epsilon_N^{\rm MC}
\ge1-\alpha.
\]
By the definition of the lower conditional quantile,
\(\widehat c_{N,\mathrm{DKW}}\ge c_{1-\alpha,N}^{-,*}\).  This proves the
displayed conditional domination probability.  The restriction
\(\epsilon_N^{\rm MC}<\alpha\) ensures that the requested empirical level
\(1-\alpha+\epsilon_N^{\rm MC}\) is strictly below one.
\end{proof}


\subsection{Finite-record implementation protocols}\label{app:finite-record-implementation-protocols-main}

The following protocols implement the reporting conventions used by
Theorems~C--E.  They are computational recipes and certificate checks, not
additional assumptions or paper-level theorem statements.

\phantomsection\label{alg:all-complete-cycle-separated-batch-main}
\paragraph{Algorithm 1: all-complete-cycle separated-batch covariance.}

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{\arabic*.},leftmargin=2.0em,itemsep=0.35em]
\item From the retained record \(A_0,\ldots,A_{N-1}\), form the complete-cycle
sets \(J_{m,N}\) of
\Cref{def:cycle-index-inclusion-estimator-main} and use only the common set
\[
J_N:=J_{0,N}\cap J_{1,N}\cap J_{2,N}.
\]
Initial incomplete cycles, terminal incomplete cycles, and the fixed terminal
look-ahead cycles required by the local windows are omitted.

\item For each \(j\in J_N\), compute the observable centered reward
\[
\widehat Y_j=
\bigl(U_j^{(0)}-\widehat r_{0,N}^{\mathrm{cyc}}L_j,\,
U_j^{(1)}-\widehat r_{1,N}^{\mathrm{cyc}}L_j,\,
U_j^{(2)}-\widehat r_{2,N}^{\mathrm{cyc}}L_j\bigr)^\top .
\]

\item With \(b_N=\lfloor N^{1/3}\rfloor\), set \(d_N=b_N+1\) and use separated
batch grids
\[
I_{\ell,N}:=\{(\ell-1)d_N,\ldots,(\ell-1)d_N+b_N-1\}.
\]
The omitted index \(\ell d_N-1\) is the separator.

\item Let
\[
M_N:=\max\{m\ge0:\ I_{\ell,N}\subseteq J_N
\text{ for every }1\le\ell\le m\},
\]
with \(M_N=0\) if the set is empty.  A partial terminal batch is omitted.
With \(K_N=\max\{k:\tau_k<N\}\), and with \(K_N=-1\) if no click is observed,
set
\[
\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{inv},N}=
\widehat r_{1,N}^{\mathrm{cyc}}-(\widehat r_{0,N}^{\mathrm{cyc}})^2,
\qquad
\mathcal E_N=
\{K_N\ge K_{\min},\ M_N\ge2,
\widehat r_{0,N}^{\mathrm{cyc}}\ge\varepsilon_N,
|\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{inv},N}|\ge\varepsilon_N\}.
\]

\item Define
\[
\widehat B_{\ell,N}:=\sum_{j\in I_{\ell,N}}\widehat Y_j,\qquad
\overline{\widehat B}_N:=M_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_N}\widehat B_{\ell,N}
\quad\text{on }\mathcal E_N.
\]
Report the covariance estimator only on \(\mathcal E_N\):
\[
\widehat\Sigma_{r,N}
=
\frac{K_N}{N}\,
\frac1{b_N(M_N-1)}
\sum_{\ell=1}^{M_N}
(\widehat B_{\ell,N}-\overline{\widehat B}_N)
(\widehat B_{\ell,N}-\overline{\widehat B}_N)^\top .
\]
On \(\mathcal E_N^c\), do not form a zero replacement; report
``insufficient complete cycles; finite-record report withheld.''
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{Algorithm 2: quotient inverse, projection, and chart retention.}

Compute \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{inv},N}\) and apply the denominator thresholds
\(\widehat r_{0,N}^{\mathrm{cyc}}\ge\varepsilon_N\) and
\(|\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{inv},N}|\ge\varepsilon_N\).  If \(\mathcal E_N^c\) occurs, stop
retained-record inference and report ``insufficient complete cycles;
finite-record report withheld.''  On \(\mathcal E_N\), compute
\(\Phi(\widehat r_N^{\mathrm{cyc}})\) and project the resulting raw symmetric
coordinate by
\(\widetilde\sigma_N=\Pi_F^{\rm tb}(\Phi(\widehat r_N^{\mathrm{cyc}}))\).
The visible-record output at this stage is only the quotient coordinate, the
unordered root set, and the unordered rate set.  Report separated labelled
rates only as a side-data output, and only when
\[
\widehat\Delta_{\sigma,N}\ge(\delta_N^{\rm root})^2,
\qquad
\widehat p_N,\widehat s_N\in[\eta_N,1-\eta_N],
\]
and the deterministic oracle branch map \(\mathcal B\) is unique on the two
projected roots.  If an estimated branch map is used, require the
high-probability oracle-agreement condition from
\Cref{conv:branch-map-labelled-rates-main}; otherwise withhold separated
labels and retain only the quotient/unordered report.  At a population
exchange diagonal, use only the fixed-candidate common-rate pullback calibrated
by Algorithm~3; a simultaneous diagonal band needs a separate certified
inversion rule.

\paragraph{Algorithm 3: fixed-candidate projected-Gaussian diagonal calibration.}

Fix \(0<\alpha<1\).  In this manuscript the coverage-certified candidate set
is the singleton
\[
Z_{\rm cert}^{\rm paper}=\{1/2\},
\]
because \(\Cref{lem:z-half-diagonal-branch-certificate-main}\) is the only
printed terminal branch certificate.  Thus the paper-level operational
algorithm is run at \(z=1/2\), with \(n_z=(-z,1)^\top\).  A finite set or
finite interval union \(Z_{\rm cert}\) from
\Cref{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main,lem:diagonal-certified-interval-cover-main}
is only an implementation extension: every displayed candidate in that set
must carry its own finite branch transcript and a certified conditional
quantile transcript before it can be used for coverage reporting.  The finite
Monte Carlo add-on, when used for a coverage-certified report rather than a
plot, has the fixed theorem-level settings
\[
R_N=N,\qquad \delta_N^{\rm MC}=N^{-2},\qquad
\varepsilon_N^{\rm MC}:=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2N^2)}{2N}} .
\]
Here \(\delta_N^{\rm root}\) is the deterministic root-discriminant reporting
threshold from the finite-record chart, while \(\delta_N^{\rm MC}\) is the
conditional DKW error probability for the simulated quantile.
The algorithm has two outputs: an ideal conditional projected-Gaussian
calculation and, only when all certificates below are present, a
coverage-certified finite report.  The latter means a finite diagonal report
in the precise sense of \Cref{def:finite-diagonal-report-main}: the candidate
must have a branch certificate and then exactly one critical-value certificate:
either the certified ideal-CDF bracket with the interval decision
\([Q_N]^+\le L_N\), \([Q_N]^->U_N\), or undecided diagnostic output, or the
canonical DKW-inflated empirical quantile with \(R_N=N\) and
\(\delta_N^{\rm MC}=N^{-2}\).  In the submitted manuscript, if
\(z\ne1/2\), continue only for diagnostic plotting or diagnostic
ideal-quantile evaluation and report ``diagonal candidate outside the printed
paper certificate; no coverage-certified acceptance event.''  In an
implementation extension, the same diagnostic-only rule applies to every
\(z\notin Z_{\rm cert}\).  For a certified candidate, compute the population diagonal
covariance \(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) from the finite D-MAP formula
\eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-finite-main} and attach the outward-rounded
branch certificate specified in
\Cref{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main,lem:diagonal-interval-branch-certificate-main}.
The certificate transcript must display the intervals for
\(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)\), \(\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)\), and
\(\Sigma_\sigma(z)(1,z)^\top\).  If the branch certificate is inconclusive,
continue only if a diagnostic projected-Gaussian plot or diagnostic ideal
quantile is desired, and report ``diagonal covariance branch not certified; no
coverage-certified acceptance event.''  A finite-sample eigenvalue calculation of
\(\widehat\Sigma_{\sigma,N}\) is not a substitute for this population
certificate.

Compute
\[
\widehat\Sigma_{\sigma,N}
=D\Phi(\widehat r_N^{\mathrm{cyc}})
 \widehat\Sigma_{r,N}
 D\Phi(\widehat r_N^{\mathrm{cyc}})^\top
\]
on the reporting event \(\mathcal E_N\); if \(\mathcal E_N^c\) occurs, stop
and report ``insufficient complete cycles; finite-record report withheld.''  Symmetrize
the matrix for numerical reporting and truncate only roundoff-negative
eigenvalues to zero.

Diagonalize
\[
\widehat\Sigma_{\sigma,N}
=\sum_{i=1}^2\widehat\lambda_{i,N}
\widehat v_{i,N}\widehat v_{i,N}^{\top},
\qquad
\widehat\lambda_{1,N}\ge\widehat\lambda_{2,N}\ge0,
\]
retain exactly
\[
\widehat I_N=\{i:\widehat\lambda_{i,N}>t_N\},
\qquad \widehat k_N=|\widehat I_N|,
\]
and use
\[
\widehat\Sigma_{\sigma,N}^{+}
=\sum_{i\in\widehat I_N}
\widehat\lambda_{i,N}^{-1}
\widehat v_{i,N}\widehat v_{i,N}^{\top}.
\]
If \(\widehat k_N=0\), report ``retained rank zero'' and use only the
buffered conservative acceptance event from
\Cref{thm:e-fixed-candidate-exchange-diagonal-main} when the population
certificate is the zero-covariance branch; otherwise this finite retained-rank
event is an asymptotic pseudoinverse event, not a population branch label.  If
the population certificate is ``rank-one normal direction,'' then, with
\(p_c=1-\alpha\),
the limiting law satisfies
\[
\PP(T_z=0)=\frac12,\qquad
\PP(T_z\le t)=\frac12+\frac12F_{\chi^2_1}(t),\quad t>0.
\]
Thus \(c_{p_c}=0\) for \(p_c\le1/2\), in which case use the buffered
conservative acceptance event from
\Cref{thm:e-fixed-candidate-exchange-diagonal-main}.  For \(p_c>1/2\),
\(c_{p_c}=F_{\chi^2_1}^{-1}(2p_c-1)>0\), and the unbuffered exact branch of
\Cref{thm:e-fixed-candidate-exchange-diagonal-main} applies.  If the population certificate is full rank or
rank-one non-normal, use the exact projected-Gaussian branch.  In the
rank-one non-normal case the branch certificate must also display
\([a_{\rm rn}]\) from
\eqref{eq:diagonal-rank-one-nonnormal-scale-certificate-main}; the ideal
conditional law is
\[
F^{(1)}_{z,[a_{\rm rn}]}(c)
=\frac12F_{\chi^2_1}(c)
 +\frac12F_{\chi^2_1}\!\left(\frac{c}{a_{\rm rn}}\right),
\]
with \(a_{\rm rn}\) interpreted through its certified interval enclosure and
the lower quantile bracketed by the one-dimensional directed bisection in
\Cref{lem:certified-rank-one-nonnormal-projected-gaussian-quantile-main}.  If
the population certificate is zero covariance, use the retained-rank-zero
buffered branch.  If it is inconclusive, no coverage-certified branch is
selected.

Generate conditionally independent auxiliary Gaussian draws
\[
Z_{N,m}^{\ast}\sim\mathcal N(0,\widehat\Sigma_{\sigma,N}),
\qquad 1\le m\le N,
\]
when a finite simulation diagnostic or DKW-certified simulated critical value
is requested.  These are plug-in draws from the limiting projected Gaussian
law, not resampled records, and their count is unrelated to the separated-
batch count \(M_N\).  Project each draw onto
\[
H_z=\{h:h_2\le zh_1\},\qquad
\Pi_{H_z}(u)
=u-\frac{(u_2-zu_1)_+}{1+z^2}\binom{-z}{1},
\]
and sort the quadratic values
\[
T_{N,m}^{\ast}(z)
=\Pi_{H_z}(Z_{N,m}^{\ast})^\top
\widehat\Sigma_{\sigma,N}^{+}
\Pi_{H_z}(Z_{N,m}^{\ast}).
\]
The ideal critical value \(c^{-}_{1-\alpha,N}(z)\) is the lower conditional
\((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of this projected-Gaussian law.  In the retained
full-rank branch it is constructed from the conditional analogue of
\[
F_{z,\Sigma}(c)=
\PP\{Z\in H_z,\ Z^\top\Sigma^{-1}Z\le c\}
+\PP\{Z\notin H_z,\
(\Pi_{H_z}Z)^\top\Sigma^{-1}(\Pi_{H_z}Z)\le c\}
\]
in \Cref{lem:deterministic-full-rank-projected-gaussian-quantile-main}, with
\(\Sigma\) replaced by the retained \(\widehat\Sigma_{\sigma,N}\).  In the
rank-one non-normal branch it is constructed from the scalar mixture
\eqref{eq:rank-one-nonnormal-cdf-main}, with \(a\) replaced by the certified
conditional enclosure obtained from the retained rank-one covariance.  A
coverage-certified report must evaluate the applicable ideal conditional
quantile directly, either analytically or by the appropriate deterministic
certified enclosure routine:
\Cref{thm:certified-projected-gaussian-quantile-algorithm-main,lem:certified-deterministic-projected-gaussian-quantile-main}
for full rank and
\Cref{lem:certified-rank-one-nonnormal-projected-gaussian-quantile-main}
for rank-one non-normal.  The full-rank
routine must use a certified Gaussian tail truncation, interval quadrature over
the two projected regions in the full-rank display above, and a certified
critical-value transcript with endpoint inequalities
\[
F_N^+(L_N)<1-\alpha\le F_N^-(U_N).
\]
In the rank-one non-normal branch, the one-dimensional
routine of
\Cref{lem:certified-rank-one-nonnormal-projected-gaussian-quantile-main}
instead uses directed evaluations of \(F_{\chi^2_1}(x)=2\Phi(\sqrt x)-1\)
and bisection on the scalar mixture.  In either case the statistic computation
must also print an outward-rounded interval
\([Q_N]=[[Q_N]^-,[Q_N]^+]\).  The realized finite decision is not made in this
algorithm paragraph; it is the separate transcript decision in
\Cref{thm:certified-diagonal-inference-main}.  Equivalently, a
certified accept/reject output requires a quantile bracket that decides the
inequality
\[
Q_N(z)\le c^{-}_{1-\alpha,N}(z)
\]
or, on a buffered branch, the inequality with
\(c^{-}_{1-\alpha,N}(z)+\varepsilon\).  If no such certified ideal-quantile
evaluation is available, the branch certificate alone is insufficient: report
``ideal quantile only; Monte Carlo diagnostic not coverage-certified'' for
this candidate.

When optional Monte Carlo draws are generated, the raw simulation quantile
estimate is the order statistic
\[
\widehat c^{-}_{1-\alpha,N}(z)
=T_{N,(\lceil(1-\alpha)N\rceil)}^{\ast}(z),
\]
after sorting increasingly.  It may be displayed as a diagnostic for the ideal
conditional quantile.  To turn finite simulation into an operational
coverage-certified critical value, the algorithm uses only the canonical DKW
choice \(R_N=N\), \(\delta_N^{\rm MC}=N^{-2}\).  If
\(\varepsilon_N^{\rm MC}\ge\alpha\), the simulated quantile remains
diagnostic.  If \(\varepsilon_N^{\rm MC}<\alpha\), the DKW one-sided simulated
critical value is
\[
\widehat c_{N,\mathrm{DKW}}(z)
=T_{N,(\lceil(1-\alpha+\varepsilon_N^{\rm MC})N\rceil)}^\ast(z),
\]
equivalently
\[
\widehat c_{N,\mathrm{DKW}}(z)
=\widehat c^{-}_{1-\alpha,N}(z)
+\Bigl[
T_{N,(\lceil(1-\alpha+\varepsilon_N^{\rm MC})N\rceil)}^\ast(z)
-T_{N,(\lceil(1-\alpha)N\rceil)}^\ast(z)
\Bigr].
\]
The event
\[
G_{\mathrm{MC},N}^{\mathrm{DKW}}(z)
=\{\Delta_{N,N}(z)\le\varepsilon_N^{\rm MC}\},
\qquad
\Delta_{N,N}(z)=
\sup_t|\widehat F^\ast_{N,N}(t;z)-F_N^\ast(t;z)|,
\]
has auxiliary conditional probability \(\PP^\ast\) at least \(1-N^{-2}\) for
the fixed observed record, and on it
\[
\widehat c_{N,\mathrm{DKW}}(z)
\ge c^{-}_{1-\alpha,N}(z).
\]
Equivalently, after conditioning on the observed record but before drawing the
auxiliary simulation,
\[
\PP^\ast\{\widehat c_{N,\mathrm{DKW}}(z)
\ge c^{-}_{1-\alpha,N}(z)\}\ge1-N^{-2}.
\]
This is the default certified DKW domination choice in
\Cref{lem:conditional-monte-carlo-quantile-main}.  The reported simulated event is then
\[
Q_N(z)\le
\widehat c_{N,\mathrm{DKW}}(z),
\]
with record probability controlled only after combining the ideal Theorem~E
statement, the high-probability reporting gate
\Cref{lem:finite-record-reporting-gate-main}, and the conditional DKW
domination lemma
\Cref{lem:conditional-monte-carlo-quantile-main}.  This is the simulation route in
\Cref{def:finite-diagonal-report-main}.  No other finite simulation choice is
treated as an operational certificate.  Without the canonical DKW event above,
all simulated quantiles are diagnostic only: report
``ideal quantile only; Monte Carlo diagnostic not coverage-certified'' for
this candidate.

When several diagonal candidates are displayed, repeat the preceding steps
only for the finite list or finite interval union in \(Z_{\rm cert}\).  Any
uncertified continuum curve, heat map, or dense grid is a visualization of the
diagnostic statistic and is not a confidence-set inversion.

\phantomsection\label{alg:projected-plugin-word-law-reconstruction-main}
\paragraph{Algorithm 4: projected plug-in word-law reconstruction.}

This protocol implements
\Cref{def:projected-plugin-word-law-reconstruction-main,prop:finite-record-complete-law-renewal-consistency-main}.
It is a numerical reconstruction recipe for a retained projected renewal law,
not an uncertainty statement or a confidence procedure for word probabilities.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{\arabic*.},leftmargin=2.0em,itemsep=0.35em]
\item Start with the finite-record reporting gate \(\mathcal E_N\), the
quotient inverse map \(\Phi\), the feasible projection \(\Pi_F^{\rm tb}\),
and the thresholds \(\varepsilon_N,\eta_N\) of the fixed protocol
\eqref{prot:finite-record-main}.  If \(\mathcal E_N^c\) occurs, stop and
return ``insufficient complete cycles; projected plug-in word-law
reconstruction not formed.''

\item On \(\mathcal E_N\), compute
\[
\widetilde\sigma_N
:=\Pi_F^{\rm tb}\{\Phi(\widehat r_N^{\mathrm{cyc}})\},
\]
and let \(\{\widetilde z_{1,N},\widetilde z_{2,N}\}\) be the unordered roots of
\[
z^2-\widetilde\sigma_{1,N}z+\widetilde\sigma_{2,N}=0 .
\]
Retain the word-law branch only on
\[
\mathcal E_N^{\rm law}
=\mathcal E_N\cap
\{\widetilde z_{1,N},\widetilde z_{2,N}\in[\eta_N,1-\eta_N]\}.
\]
On \((\mathcal E_N^{\rm law})^c\), do not form projected plug-in word
probabilities.

\item On \(\mathcal E_N^{\rm law}\), compute the projected root gap law
\(\widetilde g_{k,N}\) from the reconstruction formulas in
\Cref{lem:algorithmic-complete-law-reconstruction-main}.  Define the projected
renewal intensity by
\[
\widetilde\rho_N
=\rho_*(\widetilde\sigma_N)
:=\left(1+\sum_{k\ge0}k\,\widetilde g_{k,N}\right)^{-1}.
\]
Do not insert the noisy empirical intensity
\(\widehat r_{0,N}^{\mathrm{cyc}}\) into the final renewal inclusion product.

\item For a requested finite window \(I\), put \(d_I=0\) if \(|I|\le1\), and
otherwise put \(d_I=\max I-\min I\).  The reconstruction uses only
\(\widetilde u_{0,N},\ldots,\widetilde u_{d_I,N}\), obtained from
\[
\widetilde U_N(t):=\sum_{n\ge0}\widetilde u_{n,N}t^n
:=\frac{1}{1-\sum_{k\ge0}\widetilde g_{k,N}t^{k+1}},
\]
or equivalently from the finite recursion
\[
\widetilde u_{0,N}=1,\qquad
\widetilde u_{n,N}
=\sum_{\ell=1}^{n}\widetilde g_{\ell-1,N}\,
  \widetilde u_{n-\ell,N},\qquad 1\le n\le d_I .
\]
If the implementation truncates the gap law after \(K\ge d_I-1\), the renewal
masses needed for this finite window are unchanged; the truncation error in
\(\widetilde u_{0,N},\ldots,\widetilde u_{d_I,N}\) is exactly zero.

\item The only infinite-tail numerical quantity in a finite-window
reconstruction is the scalar mean in \(\widetilde\rho_N\).  Evaluate it either from the closed
root formula in
\Cref{rem:complete-law-numerical-implementation-main} or from a truncated
sum accompanied by the certified tail bound stated there.  If the declared
tail tolerance certificate fails, withhold the projected plug-in word-law
reconstruction instead of replacing the failed quantity by an uncertified
number.

\item For every nonempty \(B=\{i_1<\cdots<i_m\}\subset I\), form the projected
renewal inclusion probability
\[
\widetilde\PP_N(B\subset\varXi)
:=\widetilde\rho_N
\prod_{\ell=1}^{m-1}\widetilde u_{i_{\ell+1}-i_\ell,N},
\]
with empty inclusion value \(1\), and obtain the word probabilities on \(I\)
by finite inclusion--exclusion.  The resulting object is the projected plug-in
word-law reconstruction of \(\Cref{def:projected-plugin-word-law-reconstruction-main}\).
It contains projected word probabilities only, not confidence intervals, bands,
\(p\)-values, or critical values for those word probabilities.
\end{enumerate}


\paragraph{Estimated branch-map reduction.}\label{app:branch-map-oracle-reduction-main}
Work at a separated population point \(p\ne s\), and let \(\mathcal B\) be the
deterministic oracle branch map from
\Cref{conv:branch-map-labelled-rates-main}.  Choose disjoint open
neighbourhoods \(U_p,U_s\subset(0,1)\) of the two population roots on which the
oracle labels are constant.  Let \(\widehat{\mathcal B}_N\) be any branch map
formed from calibration or side data, and let
\[
\mathcal C_N=\{\widehat{\mathcal B}_N
\text{ agrees with }\mathcal B\text{ on }U_p\cup U_s\}.
\]
If \(\PP(\mathcal C_N)\to1\), then every retained labelled-root or
labelled-rate estimator obtained by replacing \(\mathcal B\) with
\(\widehat{\mathcal B}_N\) is asymptotically equivalent to the oracle-labelled
estimator.  In particular, all Gaussian limits, plug-in covariance
consistency statements, and retained-rank Wald limits proved conditionally on
\(\mathcal B\) remain valid for the estimated branch map.  If only the weaker
bound \(\PP(\mathcal C_N^c)\le\epsilon_N\) is available, each corresponding
one-sided coverage lower bound is reduced by at most \(\epsilon_N+o(1)\).

The retained empirical roots converge in probability to the separated
population roots.  Hence, with probability tending to one, the retained roots
lie in \(U_p\cup U_s\).  On the intersection of this event with
\(\mathcal C_N\), the estimated-map and oracle-map labelled estimators are
identical.  Therefore their difference is zero with probability tending to
one, and Slutsky's theorem transfers the oracle Gaussian, covariance, and Wald
limits.  For coverage, the reported event can fail relative to the oracle
event only on \(\mathcal C_N^c\), up to the \(o(1)\) probability that the
retained roots have not entered \(U_p\cup U_s\).  This gives the stated loss
bound.
\else
\iffalse % Obsolete diagonal confidence protocols withdrawn under response B2.

\subsection{Diagonal branch certificate interface}
\label{app:finite-domain-diagonal-certification-main}
\label{app:diagonal-branch-certificate-protocol-main}
\label{app:finite-projected-gaussian-certificates-main}
\label{app:finite-record-implementation-protocols-main}

The detailed interval-cover verifier, projected-Gaussian quadrature brackets,
canonical DKW simulation rule, and implementation algorithms are supplementary
extension material.  The main article uses only the population branch
interface below to support the ideal fixed-null asymptotic theorem at
\(z_0=1/2\).  It does not print any record-specific finite diagonal transcript.

\begin{remark}[Worked diagonal branch certificate]\label{rem:worked-diagonal-branch-certificate-main}
The printed point transcript for \(z=1/2\) is
\Cref{lem:z-half-diagonal-branch-certificate-main}.  It certifies the
full-rank branch for that single candidate only; it is not a continuum or
neighbouring-point branch classification.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[Certified diagonal covariance branch]\label{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main}
Fix \(0<z<1\), set \(n_z=(-z,1)^\top\), \(t_z=(1,z)^\top\), and form the
actual D-MAP covariance \(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) by
\eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-finite-main}.  A diagonal branch certificate is
a population certificate for the covariance branch at a fixed candidate.  It
proves exactly one of:
\[
\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)>0,
\]
\[
\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0,\quad
\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)>0,\quad
\Sigma_\sigma(z)t_z=0,
\]
\[
\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0,\quad
\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)>0,\quad
\Sigma_\sigma(z)t_z\ne0,
\]
or
\[
\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0.
\]
Strict inequalities require a displayed positive margin.  Rank-deficient
branches require exact equalities, either symbolic identities or certified
zero-width interval enclosures.  A floating-point eigenvalue calculation is
not a branch certificate.  A branch certificate alone is not a finite
accept/reject transcript; a realized finite diagonal report also needs the
record-specific statistic enclosure \([Q]\) and critical-value bracket
\([L,U]\), neither of which is printed in the main article.  In the submitted
main article the only printed branch transcript is
the full-rank point certificate at \(z=1/2\) in
\Cref{lem:z-half-diagonal-branch-certificate-main}; all other diagonal
candidates are diagnostics unless a separate branch transcript is attached,
and no candidate has an executed finite-report transcript in this article.
\end{definition}

\begin{algorithmiclemma}[Outward-rounded diagonal branch certificate]\label{lem:diagonal-interval-branch-certificate-main}
The supplementary protocol evaluates
\eqref{eq:dmap-diagonal-sigma-finite-main} with directed rounding, records
enclosures for \(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)\),
\(\det\Sigma_\sigma(z)\), and \(\Sigma_\sigma(z)t_z\), and accepts a branch
only when those enclosures prove one alternative in
\Cref{def:dmap-diagonal-rank-certificate-main}.  This main-text lemma is the
mathematical interface used by Theorem~E: accepted transcripts certify the
population covariance branch; failed transcripts leave the candidate
diagnostic only.
\end{algorithmiclemma}

\begin{algorithmiclemma}[Supplementary interval-cover branch certification]\label{lem:diagonal-certified-interval-cover-main}
A future finite-domain extension may cover a compact interval
\([z^-,z^+]\Subset(0,1)\) by finitely many certified subintervals.  Each
terminal subinterval must satisfy
\Cref{lem:diagonal-interval-branch-certificate-main} with one branch label,
and the transcript must prove that the accepted subintervals cover the stated
domain with no undecided remainder.  If any terminal interval remains
undecided, that part of the domain is not coverage-certified.
\end{algorithmiclemma}

\begin{lemma}[D-MAP diagonal covariance alternatives]\label{lem:dmap-diagonal-covariance-alternatives-main}
At each fixed exchange-diagonal population point
\(\sigma_z=(2z,z^2)\), \(0<z<1\), the nonnegative definite matrix
\(\Sigma_\sigma(z)\) satisfies exactly one of four alternatives: full rank,
rank one with range different from \(\operatorname{span}\{n_z\}\), rank one
with range equal to \(\operatorname{span}\{n_z\}\), or zero covariance.  The
tests are
\[
\operatorname{rank}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=2
\Longleftrightarrow \det\Sigma_\sigma(z)>0,
\qquad
\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0
\Longleftrightarrow \operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=0,
\]
and, in the remaining rank-one case,
\[
\operatorname{Range}\Sigma_\sigma(z)=\operatorname{span}\{n_z\}
\Longleftrightarrow \Sigma_\sigma(z)t_z=0 .
\]
The rank-one-normal branch has limiting law
\(\frac12\delta_0+\frac12\chi^2_1\); the zero-covariance branch has an
identically zero limiting statistic.  The full-rank and rank-one non-normal
branches have continuous projected-Gaussian laws and exact lower quantiles.
\end{lemma}

\begin{remark}[Supplementary finite diagonal report protocols]\label{def:finite-diagonal-report-main}\label{prop:finite-diagonal-report-master-main}

\end{remark}

 succeeded in 251ms:
# Feasibility note: n-state killed-reset D-MAP identifiability

## Decision

A universal labelled-kernel inverse is false, but a sharp minimal-class
dichotomy is attainable. Deterministic reset reduces the visible law to the
scalar Palm tail S_k = e_n^T K^k 1. Standard minimal realization theory says
that two rank-n representations of this sequence differ by a unique
similarity preserving 1 and e_n^T. Therefore a declared subclass is
identifiable, up to its allowed state relabellings, exactly when the
intersection of each such similarity orbit with the subclass's nonnegative
substochastic cone has one declared structural-equivalence class.

This orbit--cone criterion is necessary and sufficient, but its realization
input is established theory rather than a new general phase-type theorem.
The new model-specific conclusion is the location of two opposite classes:

- every minimal interior point of the unrestricted killed-reset cone has a
  continuum visible fibre;
- the pure serial absorption subclass identifies the unordered rate multiset
  for all positive rates, including repeated rates.

Pole collision is therefore not the identifiability boundary. In the serial
model it produces confluent Prony terms and singular finite-sample root
coordinates, while algebraic multiplicity still identifies the repeated rate
at population level. The boundary is the Markovian orbit fibre.

## Scope

The theorem assumes minimal/Hankel rank n. Lower-rank nominal n-state
representations require a separate stratified augmentation theory. For an
arbitrary fixed nonserial zero pattern, deciding the orbit--cone intersection
remains a graph-specific semialgebraic problem. These limitations are explicit
open interfaces in the manuscript.

## Machine evidence

verify_nstate_identifiability.py evaluates representative n=2,3,4 serial
models, including repeated sampled poles. It computes Palm tails and stationary
click moments, reconstructs the order-n Hankel recurrence, verifies full
Hankel rank, checks permutation invariance, runs deterministic fibre searches,
and constructs distinct reset-preserving similarity equivalents with identical
visible tails. The saved output is
artifacts/verify_nstate_identifiability_output.txt.

Exact citations, arXiv API queries, DOI checks, and the restricted novelty
claim are recorded in artifacts/literature_check.md.


 succeeded in 256ms:
"""Numerical feasibility checks for killed-reset D-MAP identifiability.

The serial model has a transient continuous-time generator with successive
rates ``rates``.  Sampling it at unit time gives T0=exp(Q); absorption is a
click and deterministically resets the next hidden state to the last phase,
so T1=(I-T0)1 e_n^T.  Its visible record is renewal.

This script checks five different questions that must not be conflated:

1. In the serial subclass, do visible coordinates recover the unordered rate
   multiset, including pole collisions?  A Hankel recurrence applied to the
   Palm gap-tail sequence recovers the sampled poles exp(-rate_i), with their
   algebraic multiplicities, for representative n=2,3,4 examples.
2. Does killed reset alone identify a hidden kernel?  No.  A stochastic
   similarity transform gives a different nonnegative killed-reset kernel
   with exactly the same visible renewal law.
3. Does a physical two-state inclusion triple satisfy the exact scalar image
   equation?  The residual is checked on separated and repeated-rate examples.
4. Does the hidden mode obey its sharp global secant-slope bound?
5. Does the exact mean sampled cycle have the stated small-interval expansion?

The numerical searches are evidence and diagnostics, not proofs of global
injectivity.  The associated manuscript theorem supplies the exact minimal
similarity-orbit criterion and proves serial identifiability for arbitrary
positive rates, including collision strata.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np
from numpy.typing import ArrayLike, NDArray
from scipy.linalg import eig, expm
from scipy.optimize import least_squares
from scipy.spatial import cKDTree


FloatArray = NDArray[np.float64]


def hidden_mode_secant(x: float, y: float) -> float:
    """Return the secant slope of t*exp(-t), with its diagonal limit."""
    if not np.isfinite(x) or not np.isfinite(y) or min(x, y) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("x and y must be finite and positive")
    if x == y:
        return float(np.exp(-x) * (1.0 - x))
    return float((y * np.exp(-y) - x * np.exp(-x)) / (y - x))


def symmetric_log_divided_difference(p: float, s: float) -> float:
    """Return the symmetric logarithmic divided difference C(p,s)."""
    if not np.isfinite(p) or not np.isfinite(s) or min(p, s) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("p and s must be finite and positive")
    midpoint = 0.5 * (p + s)
    half_gap = 0.5 * (p - s)
    if abs(half_gap) <= 1e-6 * midpoint:
        log_midpoint = np.log(midpoint)
        return float(
            midpoint * (1.0 - log_midpoint)
            + half_gap**2 / midpoint * (0.5 + log_midpoint / 3.0)
            + half_gap**4 / midpoint**3 * (1.0 / 12.0 + 4.0 * log_midpoint / 45.0)
        )
    return float((s * np.log(p) - p * np.log(s)) / (np.log(p) - np.log(s)))


def two_state_inclusion_coordinates(
    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
) -> FloatArray:
    """Return (r0,r1,r2) for the physical two-state sampled counter."""
    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
    x = gamma * delta
    y = recovery * delta
    p = float(np.exp(-x))
    s = float(np.exp(-y))
    if x == y:
        b = x * p
    else:
        b = y * (p - s) / (y - x)
    a = 1.0 - s - b
    rho = (1.0 - p) * (1.0 - s) / (1.0 - p + b)
    hidden_lambda = p - b
    r1 = rho * a
    r2 = rho * rho + hidden_lambda * (r1 - rho * rho)
    return np.array([rho, r1, r2])


def physical_image_residual(inclusions: ArrayLike) -> float:
    """Evaluate the exact three-inclusion sampled-counter image equation."""
    coordinates = np.asarray(inclusions, dtype=float)
    if coordinates.size != 3:
        raise ValueError("exactly r0, r1, and r2 are required")
    r0, r1, r2 = coordinates
    denominator = r1 - r0 * r0
    if r0 <= 0.0 or denominator == 0.0:
        raise ValueError("the inclusion triple is outside the stable inverse chart")
    a = r1 / r0
    hidden_lambda = (r2 - r0 * r0) / denominator
    sigma1 = 1.0 - a + hidden_lambda
    sigma2 = r0 * (1.0 - hidden_lambda) - a + hidden_lambda
    discriminant = sigma1 * sigma1 - 4.0 * sigma2
    if discriminant < -1e-13:
        raise ValueError("the quotient polynomial has nonreal roots")
    root_gap = np.sqrt(max(discriminant, 0.0))
    p = 0.5 * (sigma1 + root_gap)
    s = 0.5 * (sigma1 - root_gap)
    return float(a - 1.0 + symmetric_log_divided_difference(p, s))


def mean_cycle_length(gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float) -> float:
    """Return E(G+1) for the two-stage sampled cycle."""
    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
    x = gamma * delta
    y = recovery * delta
    gx = 1.0 / (-np.expm1(-x))
    if x == y:
        return float(gx + x * np.exp(-x) * gx * gx)
    gy = 1.0 / (-np.expm1(-y))
    return float((y * gx - x * gy) / (y - x))


def small_delta_mean_expansion(
    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
) -> float:
    """Return the expansion of delta*E(G+1) through order delta^4."""
    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
    return float(
        1.0 / gamma
        + 1.0 / recovery
        + delta / 2.0
        + gamma * recovery * (gamma + recovery) * delta**4 / 720.0
    )


def serial_generator(rates: ArrayLike) -> FloatArray:
    """Return the lower-bidiagonal transient generator for serial phases."""
    rate_array = np.asarray(rates, dtype=float)
    if rate_array.ndim != 1 or rate_array.size < 2:
        raise ValueError("rates must be a one-dimensional tuple of length at least two")
    if not np.all(np.isfinite(rate_array)) or np.any(rate_array <= 0.0):
        raise ValueError("all rates must be finite and positive")
    generator = np.diag(-rate_array)
    for index in range(1, rate_array.size):
        generator[index, index - 1] = rate_array[index]
    return generator


def serial_killed_reset_kernels(
    rates: ArrayLike, delta: float = 1.0
) -> tuple[FloatArray, FloatArray]:
    """Construct the serial killed-reset D-MAP kernels T0 and T1."""
    if not np.isfinite(delta) or delta <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("delta must be finite and positive")
    t0 = expm(delta * serial_generator(rates))
    n_states = t0.shape[0]
    reset = np.zeros(n_states)
    reset[-1] = 1.0
    click_probability = np.ones(n_states) - t0 @ np.ones(n_states)
    t1 = np.outer(click_probability, reset)
    if min(float(t0.min()), float(t1.min())) < -1e-12:
        raise ArithmeticError("matrix exponential did not produce nonnegative kernels")
    return t0, t1


def kernel_tail_coordinates(t0: ArrayLike, count: int) -> FloatArray:
    """Return S_k=e_n^T T0^k 1 for k=0,...,count-1."""
    matrix = np.asarray(t0, dtype=float)
    if matrix.ndim != 2 or matrix.shape[0] != matrix.shape[1]:
        raise ValueError("t0 must be square")
    if count < 1:
        raise ValueError("count must be positive")
    alpha = np.zeros(matrix.shape[0])
    alpha[-1] = 1.0
    ones = np.ones(matrix.shape[0])
    power = np.eye(matrix.shape[0])
    tails = np.empty(count)
    for lag in range(count):
        tails[lag] = alpha @ power @ ones
        power = power @ matrix
    return tails


def visible_tail_coordinates(
    rates: ArrayLike, count: int, delta: float = 1.0
) -> FloatArray:
    """Return visible Palm zero-run tails for a serial rate tuple."""
    t0, _ = serial_killed_reset_kernels(rates, delta)
    return kernel_tail_coordinates(t0, count)


def recover_sampled_poles(tails: ArrayLike, n_states: int) -> FloatArray:
    """Recover the unordered poles from a square Hankel matrix pencil."""
    tail_array = np.asarray(tails, dtype=float)
    if tail_array.size < 2 * n_states:
        raise ValueError("the n-state pencil needs S_0 through S_{2n-1}")
    h0 = np.array(
        [[tail_array[row + col] for col in range(n_states)] for row in range(n_states)]
    )
    h1 = np.array(
        [
            [tail_array[row + col + 1] for col in range(n_states)]
            for row in range(n_states)
        ]
    )
    poles = eig(h1, h0, right=False)
    if np.max(np.abs(poles.imag)) > 1e-8:
        raise ArithmeticError("recovered poles are not numerically real")
    real_poles = np.sort(poles.real)
    if np.any(real_poles <= 0.0) or np.any(real_poles >= 1.0):
        raise ArithmeticError("recovered poles are outside (0,1)")
    return real_poles


def visible_click_moments(
    rates: ArrayLike, max_lag: int, delta: float = 1.0
) -> FloatArray:
    """Return E[A_0] and E[A_0 A_l] for l=1,...,max_lag."""
    if max_lag < 0:
        raise ValueError("max_lag must be nonnegative")
    t0, _ = serial_killed_reset_kernels(rates, delta)
    n_states = t0.shape[0]
    alpha = np.zeros(n_states)
    alpha[-1] = 1.0
    ones = np.ones(n_states)
    rho = 1.0 / (alpha @ np.linalg.solve(np.eye(n_states) - t0, ones))
    tails = kernel_tail_coordinates(t0, max_lag + 1)
    interarrival = np.zeros(max_lag + 1)
    for lag in range(1, max_lag + 1):
        interarrival[lag] = tails[lag - 1] - tails[lag]
    renewal_mass = np.zeros(max_lag + 1)
    renewal_mass[0] = 1.0
    for lag in range(1, max_lag + 1):
        renewal_mass[lag] = sum(
            interarrival[jump] * renewal_mass[lag - jump]
            for jump in range(1, lag + 1)
        )
    return rho * renewal_mass


def recover_two_state_rates_from_three_inclusions(
    moments: ArrayLike, delta: float = 1.0
) -> FloatArray:
    """Apply the paper's existing n=2 three-inclusion quotient inverse."""
    coordinates = np.asarray(moments, dtype=float)
    if coordinates.size < 3:
        raise ValueError("r0, r1, and r2 are required")
    rho, r1, r2 = coordinates[:3]
    a = r1 / rho
    u2 = r2 / rho
    hidden_lambda = (u2 - rho) / (a - rho)
    pole_sum = 1.0 - a + hidden_lambda
    pole_product = rho * (1.0 - hidden_lambda) - a + hidden_lambda
    poles = np.sort(np.roots([1.0, -pole_sum, pole_product]).real)
    return np.sort(-np.log(poles) / delta)


def equivalent_killed_reset_kernel(t0: ArrayLike, epsilon: float) -> FloatArray:
    """Return a nontrivial stochastic-similarity equivalent killed kernel."""
    matrix = np.asarray(t0, dtype=float)
    n_states = matrix.shape[0]
    if matrix.ndim != 2 or matrix.shape[1] != n_states or n_states < 2:
        raise ValueError("t0 must be square with at least two states")
    transform = np.eye(n_states)
    transform[0, 0] = 1.0 - epsilon
    transform[0, 1] = epsilon
    equivalent = np.linalg.solve(transform, matrix @ transform)
    deficits = np.ones(n_states) - equivalent @ np.ones(n_states)
    if float(equivalent.min()) < -1e-12 or float(deficits.min()) < -1e-12:
        raise ValueError("epsilon does not preserve a nonnegative killed-reset kernel")
    return equivalent


def finite_difference_jacobian(rates: ArrayLike, max_lag: int) -> FloatArray:
    """Differentiate the visible click-moment map by centered differences."""
    rate_array = np.asarray(rates, dtype=float)
    jacobian = np.empty((max_lag + 1, rate_array.size))
    for column, rate in enumerate(rate_array):
        step = 1e-6 * max(1.0, rate)
        upper = rate_array.copy()
        lower = rate_array.copy()
        upper[column] += step
        lower[column] -= step
        jacobian[:, column] = (
            visible_click_moments(upper, max_lag)
            - visible_click_moments(lower, max_lag)
        ) / (2.0 * step)
    return jacobian


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SearchSummary:
    starts: int
    converged: int
    canonical_fibers: tuple[tuple[float, ...], ...]
    labelled_orders: tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]
    best_nonpermutation_residual: float


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HankelDiagnostics:
    rank: int
    determinant: float
    condition_number: float
    smallest_singular_value: float


def hankel_diagnostics(tails: ArrayLike, n_states: int) -> HankelDiagnostics:
    """Return numerical rank and conditioning of the leading Hankel block."""
    tail_array = np.asarray(tails, dtype=float)
    if tail_array.size < 2 * n_states - 1:
        raise ValueError("the Hankel block needs S_0 through S_{2n-2}")
    hankel = np.array(
        [[tail_array[row + col] for col in range(n_states)] for row in range(n_states)]
    )
    singular_values = np.linalg.svd(hankel, compute_uv=False)
    tolerance = singular_values[0] * max(hankel.shape) * np.finfo(float).eps
    return HankelDiagnostics(
        rank=int(np.sum(singular_values > tolerance)),
        determinant=float(np.linalg.det(hankel)),
        condition_number=float(singular_values[0] / singular_values[-1]),
        smallest_singular_value=float(singular_values[-1]),
    )


def recover_minimal_recurrence(
    tails: ArrayLike, n_states: int
) -> tuple[FloatArray, float]:
    """Recover the monic order-n annihilator and its tail residual.

    If ``p(x)=x^n+c_{n-1}x^(n-1)+...+c_0``, the returned coefficients are
    ``[1,c_{n-1},...,c_0]``.  Repeated roots retain their multiplicities.
    """
    tail_array = np.asarray(tails, dtype=float)
    if tail_array.size < 2 * n_states:
        raise ValueError("the recurrence needs S_0 through S_{2n-1}")
    h0 = np.array(
        [[tail_array[row + col] for col in range(n_states)] for row in range(n_states)]
    )
    future = np.array([tail_array[row + n_states] for row in range(n_states)])
    ascending = np.linalg.solve(h0, -future)
    polynomial = np.concatenate(([1.0], ascending[::-1]))
    residuals = []
    for offset in range(tail_array.size - n_states):
        residuals.append(
            tail_array[offset + n_states]
            + float(ascending @ tail_array[offset : offset + n_states])
        )
    return polynomial, float(np.max(np.abs(residuals)))


def reset_similarity_lie_basis(n_states: int) -> tuple[FloatArray, ...]:
    """Basis of B1=0 and e_n^T B=0, the reset-preserving similarity tangent."""
    if n_states < 2:
        raise ValueError("n_states must be at least two")
    basis = []
    for row in range(n_states - 1):
        for column in range(n_states - 1):
            tangent = np.zeros((n_states, n_states))
            tangent[row, column] = 1.0
            tangent[row, -1] = -1.0
            basis.append(tangent)
    return tuple(basis)


def multistart_fiber_search(
    target_rates: ArrayLike, starts: int, seed: int
) -> SearchSummary:
    """Search numerically for rate tuples sharing the target click moments."""
    target = np.asarray(target_rates, dtype=float)
    max_lag = 2 * target.size + 2
    target_moments = visible_click_moments(target, max_lag)
    scale = np.maximum(np.abs(target_moments), 1e-4)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    accepted: list[FloatArray] = []
    residuals: list[float] = []

    def residual(log_rates: FloatArray) -> FloatArray:
        return (visible_click_moments(np.exp(log_rates), max_lag) - target_moments) / scale

    for _ in range(starts):
        initial = rng.uniform(np.log(0.15), np.log(3.5), size=target.size)
        fit = least_squares(
            residual,
            initial,
            bounds=(np.log(0.08), np.log(5.0)),
            xtol=1e-12,
            ftol=1e-12,
            gtol=1e-12,
            max_nfev=2500,
        )
        norm = float(np.linalg.norm(residual(fit.x)))
        if norm < 1e-8:
            accepted.append(np.exp(fit.x))
            residuals.append(norm)

    canonical = sorted(
        {
            tuple(np.round(np.sort(solution), 4))
            for solution in accepted
        }
    )
    labelled_orders = sorted(
        {
            tuple(np.argsort(solution).tolist())
            for solution in accepted
        }
    )
    target_sorted = np.sort(target)
    nonpermutation = [
        residual_value
        for solution, residual_value in zip(accepted, residuals)
        if np.linalg.norm(np.sort(solution) - target_sorted) > 1e-3
    ]
    return SearchSummary(
        starts=starts,
        converged=len(accepted),
        canonical_fibers=tuple(canonical),
        labelled_orders=tuple(labelled_orders),
        best_nonpermutation_residual=min(nonpermutation, default=float("inf")),
    )


def random_nearest_pair_search(
    n_states: int, samples: int, seed: int
) -> tuple[float, float, tuple[float, ...], tuple[float, ...]]:
    """Find the closest sampled moment vectors among sorted random tuples."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    rates = np.sort(
        np.exp(rng.uniform(np.log(0.15), np.log(3.5), size=(samples, n_states))),
        axis=1,
    )
    moments = np.array([visible_click_moments(row, 2 * n_states + 2) for row in rates])
    scale = np.maximum(moments.std(axis=0), 1e-10)
    normalized = moments / scale
    distances, indices = cKDTree(normalized).query(normalized, k=2)
    index = int(np.argmin(distances[:, 1]))
    partner = int(indices[index, 1])
    moment_distance = float(np.linalg.norm(normalized[index] - normalized[partner]))
    rate_distance = float(np.linalg.norm(rates[index] - rates[partner]))
    return (
        moment_distance,
        rate_distance,
        tuple(rates[index]),
        tuple(rates[partner]),
    )


def array_string(values: ArrayLike) -> str:
    return np.array2string(
        np.asarray(values), precision=10, suppress_small=False, floatmode="fixed"
    )


def report_example(rates: tuple[float, ...], search_starts: int = 80) -> None:
    n_states = len(rates)
    t0, t1 = serial_killed_reset_kernels(rates)
    tails = kernel_tail_coordinates(t0, 2 * n_states)
    extended_tails = kernel_tail_coordinates(t0, 3 * n_states + 1)
    moments = visible_click_moments(rates, 2 * n_states + 2)
    recurrence, recurrence_residual = recover_minimal_recurrence(
        extended_tails, n_states
    )
    roots = np.roots(recurrence)
    recovered_rates = np.sort(-np.log(np.abs(roots)))
    diagnostics = hankel_diagnostics(tails, n_states)
    permutations = list(itertools.permutations(rates))
    permutation_error = max(
        float(np.max(np.abs(visible_click_moments(item, 2 * n_states + 2) - moments)))
        for item in permutations
    )
    singular_values = np.linalg.svd(
        finite_difference_jacobian(rates, 2 * n_states + 2), compute_uv=False
    )

    print(f"n={n_states} serial killed-reset example")
    print(f"rates={rates}")
    print("T0=")
    print(array_string(t0))
    print("T1=")
    print(array_string(t1))
    print(f"Palm tails S_0,...,S_{2 * n_states - 1}={array_string(tails)}")
    print(f"click moments r_0,...,r_{2 * n_states + 2}={array_string(moments)}")
    print(f"Hankel recurrence polynomial={array_string(recurrence)}")
    print(f"expected sampled-pole polynomial={array_string(np.poly(np.exp(-np.asarray(rates))))}")
    print(f"maximum recurrence residual={recurrence_residual:.3e}")
    print(
        "leading Hankel diagnostics: "
        f"rank={diagnostics.rank}, determinant={diagnostics.determinant:.3e}, "
        f"condition={diagnostics.condition_number:.3e}, "
        f"sigma_min={diagnostics.smallest_singular_value:.3e}"
    )
    print(f"recovered unordered rates (root moduli)={array_string(recovered_rates)}")
    if n_states == 2:
        print(
            "three-inclusion recovered unordered rates="
            f"{array_string(recover_two_state_rates_from_three_inclusions(moments))}"
        )
    print(f"maximum moment error over all labelled permutations={permutation_error:.3e}")
    print(f"moment-map Jacobian singular values={array_string(singular_values)}")

    search = multistart_fiber_search(rates, starts=search_starts, seed=100 + n_states)
    print(
        f"multistart search: {search.converged}/{search.starts} converged; "
        f"canonical sorted fibers={search.canonical_fibers}"
    )
    print(f"labelled permutation orders reached={search.labelled_orders}")
    if np.isfinite(search.best_nonpermutation_residual):
        print(
            "WARNING: accepted non-permutation solution with scaled residual="
            f"{search.best_nonpermutation_residual:.3e}"
        )
    else:
        print("no accepted non-permutation solution found")

    nearest = random_nearest_pair_search(n_states, samples=900, seed=200 + n_states)
    print(
        "random nearest-pair search: normalized moment distance="
        f"{nearest[0]:.3e}, rate distance={nearest[1]:.3e}"
    )
    print(f"nearest sorted tuples={nearest[2]} and {nearest[3]}")

    equivalent = equivalent_killed_reset_kernel(t0, epsilon=0.02)
    tail_difference = float(
        np.max(
            np.abs(
                kernel_tail_coordinates(t0, 20)
                - kernel_tail_coordinates(equivalent, 20)
            )
        )
    )
    print("non-serial stochastic-similarity equivalent T0'=")
    print(array_string(equivalent))
    print(f"||T0'-T0||_F={np.linalg.norm(equivalent - t0):.3e}")
    print(f"maximum S_0,...,S_19 difference={tail_difference:.3e}")
    print(f"reset-preserving similarity tangent dimension={(n_states - 1) ** 2}")
    print(
        "interpretation: killed reset alone has a nontrivial hidden-kernel "
        "fiber, while the serial rate tuple is recovered here only as an "
        "unordered multiset."
    )
    print()

    print("Sharp killed-reset D-MAP identifiability dichotomy verification")
    print("delta=1; all searches use deterministic random seeds")
    print()

        for item in image_examples

    report_example((0.7, 1.2, 1.2, 2.3), search_starts=50)

    collision = (0.7, 1.2, 1.2)

        finite_difference_jacobian(collision, 8), compute_uv=False

    print("n=3 conditioning diagnostic")

        "smallest-singular-value ratio (collision/separated)="
        f"{collision_singular_values[-1] / separated_singular_values[-1]:.3e}"
    )

\section{Record, inverse, and finite-record results}\label{sec:records}

This section gives the record-side results in compressed form.  Each main
result is read under the constrained D-MAP record assumption
\Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, with any extra regularity or
finite-record protocol stated locally.  Between those statements, all
probabilities below are probabilities of the stationary visible binary record
generated by the sampled-counter labelled kernels \(T_0,T_1\).
The killed entries \(T_1(R,R)=T_1(D,R)=0\) are used as assumptions, not as
conclusions; \Cref{prop:model-fragility-boundary-reset-main} states exactly
which renewal and inverse conclusions are lost for same-bin recovery leakage.
Throughout this section \((A_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}\) denotes that two-sided
stationary extension.
One-sided strings such as \(A_0,\ldots,A_{N-1}\) are finite restrictions used
only for observed-record statistics; when a proof conditions on a past event
or shifts a renewal epoch, it is using the same stationary two-sided process.

\subsection{Model and renewal law}

\begin{proposition}[Constrained D-MAP labelled kernels]\label{prop:instrument-kernels-main}
Fix \(\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Delta\tau>0\).  With hidden states ordered as
\((R,D)\), let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:t0-t1-main}
T_0=
\begin{pmatrix}
p&0\\ b&s
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
T_1=
\begin{pmatrix}
0&1-p\\0&a
\end{pmatrix},
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}\label{eq:p-c-main}
p=e^{-\Gamma\Delta\tau},
\qquad
s=e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau},
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:a-b-main}
a=\int_0^{\Delta\tau}\kappa_{\mathrm r}e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}r}
\bigl(1-e^{-\Gamma(\Delta\tau-r)}\bigr)\,dr,
\qquad
b=\int_0^{\Delta\tau}\kappa_{\mathrm r}e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}r}
e^{-\Gamma(\Delta\tau-r)}\,dr .
\end{equation}
For \(\kappa_{\mathrm r}\ne\Gamma\),
\[
a=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(1-p)-\Gamma(1-s)}
        {\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
\qquad
b=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(p-s)}
        {\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
\]
with continuous equal-rate limits.  The labelled-kernel convention is
\((T_i)_{XY}=\PP(A_n=i,H_{n+1}=Y\mid H_n=X)\), and word probabilities are
\(\pi T_{u_0}\cdots T_{u_{m-1}}\mathbf1\) from the stationary hidden law.
These are the kernels fixed in \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The two rows define a labelled transition kernel directly.  From state \(R\),
the zero-labelled transition remains in \(R\) with probability \(p\), while the
one-labelled transition goes to \(D\) with probability \(1-p\).  From state
\(D\), the zero-labelled transition has weights \(b\) to \(R\) and \(s\) to
\(D\), and the one-labelled transition has weight \(a\) to \(D\).  The
integrals define nonnegative weights with \(a+b=1-s\), so the two row sums of
\(T_0+T_1\) are one.  Thus \(T_0,T_1\) form the stated D-MAP kernels.  The
displayed unequal-rate formulas are the elementary evaluations of the two
integrals, with continuous limits on the equal-rate diagonal.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Equal-rate and critical notation]\label{lem:equal-rate-critical-convention-main}
The survival factors are always
\[
p=e^{-\Gamma\Delta\tau},\qquad
s=e^{-\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau},
\]
and throughout the stipulated-kernel algebra
\[
q=1-p .
\]
The hidden eigenvalue is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lambda-hid-main}
\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}}
=p-b
=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}s-\Gamma p}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma}
\quad(\kappa_{\mathrm r}\ne\Gamma),
\end{equation}
with continuous equal-rate value
\(\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}}=e^{-y}(1-y)\), where
\(y=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau=\Gamma\Delta\tau\) on the equal-rate
diagonal.  Put
\[
x=\Gamma\Delta\tau,\qquad y=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\Delta\tau .
\]
For \(x\ne y\),
\[
\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}}=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x e^{-x}=y e^{-y}.
\]
The equation \(x e^{-x}=y e^{-y}\) always has the formal solution \(x=y\).
For \(y\ne1\) this diagonal solution is only the removable zero of the
multiplied quotient numerator, not a zero of the continuous eigenvalue
\(\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}}\).  The critical rate is therefore the non-removable
branch
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gamma-crit-piecewise-main}
\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Delta\tau)
=\Delta\tau^{-1}
\begin{cases}
x_+(y),&0<y<1,\quad x_+(y)>1,\quad x_+(y)e^{-x_+(y)}=y e^{-y},\\
1,&y=1,\\
x_-(y),&y>1,\quad 0<x_-(y)<1,\quad x_-(y)e^{-x_-(y)}=y e^{-y}.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
Equivalently, for \(y\ne1\) it is the unique positive solution of
\(x e^{-x}=y e^{-y}\) on the opposite side of \(1\) from \(y\), and the
removable equal-rate branch \(x=y\) is explicitly excluded.  Only at \(y=1\)
does the equal-rate branch become a genuine zero, giving
\(\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}=\kappa_{\mathrm r}=1/\Delta\tau\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The identity \(p-b\) and the quotient form follow from
\eqref{eq:a-b-main}.  The equal-rate value is l'Hopital's rule, equivalently
\(b=y e^{-y}\) when \(\kappa_{\mathrm r}=\Gamma\), and hence
\(\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}}=e^{-y}(1-y)\).  For \(x\ne y\), multiplying the
quotient numerator by \(\Delta\tau\) gives the scalar equation
\(x e^{-x}=y e^{-y}\).  The function \(x\mapsto xe^{-x}\) is strictly
increasing on \((0,1)\), strictly decreasing on \((1,\infty)\), and has its
only maximum at \(1\).  Hence the level through \(y\ne1\) has exactly one
positive solution on the opposite side of \(1\), in addition to the removable
solution \(x=y\).  This gives the two non-removable branches in
\eqref{eq:gamma-crit-piecewise-main}.  When \(y=1\), the opposite branch
coalesces with the diagonal and the equal-rate limit \(e^{-1}(1-1)=0\) gives
\(\Gamma_{\mathrm{crit}}=1/\Delta\tau=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\).
\end{proof}

For later audits, the equal-rate diagonal
\(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), \(y=\Gamma\Delta\tau\), \(p=e^{-y}\), is
summarized by the single dictionary
\begin{equation}\label{eq:equal-rate-dictionary-main}
\begin{aligned}
a&=1-(1+y)p,&
b&=yp,\\
\lambda_{\mathrm{hid}}&=p-b=(1-y)p,&
S_k&=\PP(G\ge k)=p^k(1+yk),\\
g_k&=p^k\bigl((1-p)(1+yk)-yp\bigr),&
h_k&=\frac{(1-p)+y(k(1-p)-p)}{1+yk},
\qquad k\ge0 .
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}

\begin{lemma}[Regeneration and zero-run law]\label{lem:renewal-gap-main}
Let \(G\) be the number of zeros between consecutive clicks in the stationary
constrained D-MAP record.  Click times are regeneration times.  For
\(k\ge0\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gap-main}
g_k=\PP(G=k)=e_D^\top T_0^kT_1\mathbf1 .
\end{equation}
If \(\kappa_{\mathrm r}\ne\Gamma\), then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gap-closed-main}
g_k=
\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(1-p)p^k-\Gamma(1-s)s^k}
     {\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma}.
\end{equation}
The gap law has full support on \(\mathbb N_0\) and an exponential tail.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
After a click the next hidden state is \(D\), independently of the earlier
record.  Thus a gap of \(k\) zeros followed by a click has probability
