+\begin{theorem}[Complete two-state fibre arc and exchange dichotomy]
+\label{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main}
+Under \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, put (K=T_0),
+(q_\ast=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), and
+\[
+ I_\ast=[\min\{1,q_\ast\},\max\{1,q_\ast\}].
+\]
+Then (K) is minimal, and its complete visible-law fibre in
+(\mathcal K_2) is the injectively parametrized closed arc
+\[
+ \{K(q):q\in I_\ast\},
+ \qquad
+ K(q)=
+ \begin{pmatrix}
+ p-b+bq & \displaystyle\frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\\[5pt]
+ bq & s+b(1-q)
+ \end{pmatrix}.
+ \tag{F1}
+\]
+Here complete means that every (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same stationary
+visible click law as (K) is (K(q)) for exactly one (q\in I_\ast).
+Writing (T_0(\alpha,\eta)) for the no-click kernel constructed with attempt
+rate (\alpha) and recovery rate (\eta), the endpoints are the two physical
+triangular kernels obtained by exchanging those rates:
+\[
+ K(1)=T_0(\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r}),
+ \qquad
+ K(q_\ast)=T_0(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Gamma).
+ \tag{F2}
+\]
+If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), every (q) strictly between the
+endpoints gives a strictly positive kernel with strictly positive killing
+deficits, and the physical triangular subfamily meets the arc only at the two
+endpoints.  If \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), then (I_\ast=\{1\}), so
+the entire two-state killed-reset fibre is a singleton.  Thus the unrestricted
+two-state hidden kernel is identifiable exactly on the exchange diagonal and
+has a continuum fibre off it; within the physical sampled-counter subfamily,
+the only ambiguity off the diagonal is the rate exchange.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+First (b>0).  If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), direct evaluation of
+the defining integral gives
+\[
+ b=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
+ \qquad
+ b+s-p=\frac{\Gamma(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma}
+          =bq_\ast>0.
+ \tag{F3}
+\]
+The same identities hold by continuity on the diagonal, where
+(p=s), (b=\Gamma\Delta\tau p>0), and (q_\ast=1).  Consequently
+\[
+ \det[\mathbf1,K\mathbf1]=b+s-p=bq_\ast>0,
+ \qquad
+ \det\begin{bmatrix}e_2^\top\\e_2^\top K\end{bmatrix}=-b\ne0,
+\]
+so (K) is minimal.
+
+Every member of \(\mathcal G_2\) has the unique form
+\[
+ M_q=\begin{pmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad q\ne0.
+\]
+Multiplication, using (b+s-p=bq_\ast), gives
+(M_q^{-1}KM_q=K(q)) in \textup{(F1)}.  Since (K) is minimal, its scalar
+Hankel sequence has rank two.  Any (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same visible
+law has the same leading Hankel matrix; its factorization as
+(\mathcal O(L)\mathcal C(L)) has rank two, so both factors have rank two and
+(L) is minimal as well.  The recalled orbit--fibre proposition therefore
+forces every such (L) to have the displayed form.  If
+(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2), its lower-left entry
+is (bq\ge0).  Invertibility excludes (q=0), hence (q>0).  Its
+upper-right entry then yields the exact condition
+\[
+ \frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\ge0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q\in I_\ast.
+ \tag{F4}
+\]
+
+Conversely, let (q\in I_\ast).  The two diagonal entries in
+\textup{(F1)} are affine in (q), with endpoint values (p,s) and (s,p),
+respectively, and are therefore positive.  The lower-left entry is positive,
+and \textup{(F4)} makes the upper-right entry nonnegative.  Writing
+(a=1-b-s>0), the two killing deficits are
+\[
+ 1-K(q)\mathbf1
+ =\begin{pmatrix}a+bq_\ast/q\\a\end{pmatrix}>0.
+ \tag{F5}
+\]
+Similarity preserves the spectral radius
+(\max\{p,s\}<1), so (K(q)\in\mathcal K_2).  This proves that the
+displayed arc is the complete fibre.  It is injective because its lower-left
+entry is (bq).
+
+At (q=1) one recovers (K).  At (q=q_\ast),
+\[
+ K(q_\ast)=\begin{pmatrix}s&0\\bq_\ast&p\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+Equation~\textup{(F3)} says that (bq_\ast) is precisely the no-click
+recovery-to-ready probability after exchanging the two rates, and its second
+row has the same killing deficit (a); this proves \textup{(F2)}.  If
+(q_\ast\ne1), the product in the upper-right entry is strictly positive
+inside (I_\ast) and vanishes only at its endpoints.  All remaining entries
+and both deficits are already strict there.  If (q_\ast=1),
+\textup{(F4)} forces (q=1).  The endpoint, triangular-intersection, and
+identifiability statements follow.
+\end{proof}
+

\section{Killed-reset fibres: an exact two-state arc and higher-state structure}

The minimal-realization statements in this subsection are recalled background,
not contributions of this paper.  Kalman's similarity theorem is the classical
source, and minimal MAP/phase-type formulations and canonical-coordinate
developments are given in
\cite{Kalman1963LinearSystems,TelekHorvath2007MinimalMAP,
BladtNielsen2017MatrixExponential,MeszarosTelek2013DiscreteMAP2Canonical,
PappTelek2013DiscretePHCanonical}.  We state the consequence needed to locate
the visible fibre, then prove the new quantitative assertion: at a minimal
interior killed-reset kernel the admissible fibre has local dimension
\((n-1)^2\).  Nonunique MAP and Coxian representatives are documented in
\cite{RamirezCoboLilloWiper2010MAP2Nonidentifiability,
RamirezCoboLillo2012WeakEquivalentMAP,RizkBurkeWalsh2019CoxianNonuniqueness}.
Graph-specific time-to-event inverses are treated algebraically by
Radulescu et al.\ \cite{RadulescuEtAl2025TimeToEventIdentifiability}; the
criterion below instead isolates the exact orbit fibre for any declared
minimal killed-reset subclass.

+## Selected result
+
+The first candidate maximizes reach times value and directly completes the
+paper's physical quotient story. For
+(K=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&0\\b&s\end{smallmatrix}\right)), every
+reset-preserving similarity is generated by
+(M_q=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)).
+Writing (q_*=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), the transformed upper-right entry
+is (b(1-q)(q-q_*)/q). The lower-left entry forces (q>0), so Markov
+nonnegativity is equivalent to (q) lying between (1) and (q_*). The two
+endpoints are exactly the original and rate-swapped physical kernels; strict
+interior points are positive nontriangular kernels. At equal rates (q_*=1),
+the full two-state fibre collapses to one point.

+def sampled_counter_killed_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the physical two-state no-click kernel."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery, delta))):
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be finite")
+    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
+    p = float(np.exp(-gamma * delta))
+    s = float(np.exp(-recovery * delta))
+    difference = recovery - gamma
+    if difference == 0.0:
+        b = recovery * delta * p
+    else:
+        b = recovery * p * (-np.expm1(-difference * delta)) / difference
+    return np.array([[p, 0.0], [b, s]])
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_interval(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float
+) -> tuple[float, float]:
+    """Return the exact closed q-interval of Markovian similarity equivalents."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery))) or min(gamma, recovery) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates must be finite and positive")
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    return min(1.0, endpoint), max(1.0, endpoint)
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float, q: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the q member of the exact physical two-state Markovian fibre."""
+    if not np.isfinite(q):
+        raise ValueError("q must be finite")
+    lower, upper = sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
+    if q < lower or q > upper:
+        raise ValueError("q lies outside the exact Markovian fibre interval")
+    physical = sampled_counter_killed_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta)
+    p = float(physical[0, 0])
+    b = float(physical[1, 0])
+    s = float(physical[1, 1])
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    equivalent = np.array(
+        [
+            [p - b + b * q, b * (1.0 - q) * (q - endpoint) / q],
+            [b * q, s + b * (1.0 - q)],
+        ]
+    )
+    deficits = np.ones(2) - equivalent @ np.ones(2)
+    if float(equivalent.min()) < -1e-12 or float(deficits.min()) < -1e-12:
+        raise ArithmeticError("closed-form fibre member is not substochastic")
+    return equivalent
+

+\begin{theorem}[Complete two-state fibre arc and exchange dichotomy]
+\label{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main}
+Under \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, put (K=T_0),
+(q_\ast=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), and
+\[
+ I_\ast=[\min\{1,q_\ast\},\max\{1,q_\ast\}].
+\]
+Then (K) is minimal, and its complete visible-law fibre in
+(\mathcal K_2) is the injectively parametrized closed arc
+\[
+ \{K(q):q\in I_\ast\},
+ \qquad
+ K(q)=
+ \begin{pmatrix}
+ p-b+bq & \displaystyle\frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\\[5pt]
+ bq & s+b(1-q)
+ \end{pmatrix}.
+ \tag{F1}
+\]
+Here complete means that every (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same stationary
+visible click law as (K) is (K(q)) for exactly one (q\in I_\ast).
+Writing (T_0(\alpha,\eta)) for the no-click kernel constructed with attempt
+rate (\alpha) and recovery rate (\eta), the endpoints are the two physical
+triangular kernels obtained by exchanging those rates:
+\[
+ K(1)=T_0(\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r}),
+ \qquad
+ K(q_\ast)=T_0(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Gamma).
+ \tag{F2}
+\]
+If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), every (q) strictly between the
+endpoints gives a strictly positive kernel with strictly positive killing
+deficits, and the physical triangular subfamily meets the arc only at the two
+endpoints.  If \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), then (I_\ast=\{1\}), so
+the entire two-state killed-reset fibre is a singleton.  Thus the unrestricted
+two-state hidden kernel is identifiable exactly on the exchange diagonal and
+has a continuum fibre off it; within the physical sampled-counter subfamily,
+the only ambiguity off the diagonal is the rate exchange.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+First (b>0).  If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), direct evaluation of
+the defining integral gives
+\[
+ b=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
+ \qquad
+ b+s-p=\frac{\Gamma(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma}
+          =bq_\ast>0.
+ \tag{F3}
+\]
+The same identities hold by continuity on the diagonal, where
+(p=s), (b=\Gamma\Delta\tau p>0), and (q_\ast=1).  Consequently
+\[
+ \det[\mathbf1,K\mathbf1]=b+s-p=bq_\ast>0,
+ \qquad
+ \det\begin{bmatrix}e_2^\top\\e_2^\top K\end{bmatrix}=-b\ne0,
+\]
+so (K) is minimal.
+
+Every member of \(\mathcal G_2\) has the unique form
+\[
+ M_q=\begin{pmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad q\ne0.
+\]
+Multiplication, using (b+s-p=bq_\ast), gives
+(M_q^{-1}KM_q=K(q)) in \textup{(F1)}.  Since (K) is minimal, its scalar
+Hankel sequence has rank two.  Any (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same visible
+law has the same leading Hankel matrix; its factorization as
+(\mathcal O(L)\mathcal C(L)) has rank two, so both factors have rank two and
+(L) is minimal as well.  The recalled orbit--fibre proposition therefore
+forces every such (L) to have the displayed form.  If
+(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2), its lower-left entry
+is (bq\ge0).  Invertibility excludes (q=0), hence (q>0).  Its
+upper-right entry then yields the exact condition
+\[
+ \frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\ge0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q\in I_\ast.
+ \tag{F4}
+\]
+
+Conversely, let (q\in I_\ast).  The two diagonal entries in
+\textup{(F1)} are affine in (q), with endpoint values (p,s) and (s,p),
+respectively, and are therefore positive.  The lower-left entry is positive,
+and \textup{(F4)} makes the upper-right entry nonnegative.  Writing
+(a=1-b-s>0), the two killing deficits are
+\[
+ 1-K(q)\mathbf1
+ =\begin{pmatrix}a+bq_\ast/q\\a\end{pmatrix}>0.
+ \tag{F5}
+\]
+Similarity preserves the spectral radius
+(\max\{p,s\}<1), so (K(q)\in\mathcal K_2).  This proves that the
+displayed arc is the complete fibre.  It is injective because its lower-left
+entry is (bq).
+
+At (q=1) one recovers (K).  At (q=q_\ast),
+\[
+ K(q_\ast)=\begin{pmatrix}s&0\\bq_\ast&p\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+Equation~\textup{(F3)} says that (bq_\ast) is precisely the no-click
+recovery-to-ready probability after exchanging the two rates, and its second
+row has the same killing deficit (a); this proves \textup{(F2)}.  If
+(q_\ast\ne1), the product in the upper-right entry is strictly positive
+inside (I_\ast) and vanishes only at its endpoints.  All remaining entries
+and both deficits are already strict there.  If (q_\ast=1),
+\textup{(F4)} forces (q=1).  The endpoint, triangular-intersection, and
+identifiability statements follow.
+\end{proof}

+## Selected result
+
+The first candidate maximizes reach times value and directly completes the
+paper's physical quotient story. For
+(K=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&0\\b&s\end{smallmatrix}\right)), every
+reset-preserving similarity is generated by
+(M_q=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)).
+Writing (q_*=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), the transformed upper-right entry
+is (b(1-q)(q-q_*)/q). The lower-left entry forces (q>0), so Markov
+nonnegativity is equivalent to (q) lying between (1) and (q_*). The two
+endpoints are exactly the original and rate-swapped physical kernels; strict
+interior points are positive nontriangular kernels. At equal rates (q_*=1),
+the full two-state fibre collapses to one point.

+def sampled_counter_killed_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the physical two-state no-click kernel."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery, delta))):
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be finite")
+    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
+    p = float(np.exp(-gamma * delta))
+    s = float(np.exp(-recovery * delta))
+    difference = recovery - gamma
+    if difference == 0.0:
+        b = recovery * delta * p
+    else:
+        b = recovery * p * (-np.expm1(-difference * delta)) / difference
+    return np.array([[p, 0.0], [b, s]])
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_interval(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float
+) -> tuple[float, float]:
+    """Return the exact closed q-interval of Markovian similarity equivalents."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery))) or min(gamma, recovery) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates must be finite and positive")
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    return min(1.0, endpoint), max(1.0, endpoint)
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float, q: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the q member of the exact physical two-state Markovian fibre."""
+    if not np.isfinite(q):
+        raise ValueError("q must be finite")
+    lower, upper = sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
+    if q < lower or q > upper:
+        raise ValueError("q lies outside the exact Markovian fibre interval")
+    physical = sampled_counter_killed_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta)
+    p = float(physical[0, 0])
+    b = float(physical[1, 0])
+    s = float(physical[1, 1])
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    equivalent = np.array(
+        [
+            [p - b + b * q, b * (1.0 - q) * (q - endpoint) / q],
+            [b * q, s + b * (1.0 - q)],
+        ]
+    )
+    deficits = np.ones(2) - equivalent @ np.ones(2)
+    if float(equivalent.min()) < -1e-12 or float(deficits.min()) < -1e-12:
+        raise ArithmeticError("closed-form fibre member is not substochastic")
+    return equivalent
+

+\begin{theorem}[Complete two-state fibre arc and exchange dichotomy]
+\label{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main}
+Under \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, put (K=T_0),
+(q_\ast=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), and
+\[
+ I_\ast=[\min\{1,q_\ast\},\max\{1,q_\ast\}].
+\]
+Then (K) is minimal, and its complete visible-law fibre in
+(\mathcal K_2) is the injectively parametrized closed arc
+\[
+ \{K(q):q\in I_\ast\},
+ \qquad
+ K(q)=
+ \begin{pmatrix}
+ p-b+bq & \displaystyle\frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\\[5pt]
+ bq & s+b(1-q)
+ \end{pmatrix}.
+ \tag{F1}
+\]
+Here complete means that every (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same stationary
+visible click law as (K) is (K(q)) for exactly one (q\in I_\ast).
+Writing (T_0(\alpha,\eta)) for the no-click kernel constructed with attempt
+rate (\alpha) and recovery rate (\eta), the endpoints are the two physical
+triangular kernels obtained by exchanging those rates:
+\[
+ K(1)=T_0(\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r}),
+ \qquad
+ K(q_\ast)=T_0(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Gamma).
+ \tag{F2}
+\]
+If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), every (q) strictly between the
+endpoints gives a strictly positive kernel with strictly positive killing
+deficits, and the physical triangular subfamily meets the arc only at the two
+endpoints.  If \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), then (I_\ast=\{1\}), so
+the entire two-state killed-reset fibre is a singleton.  Thus the unrestricted
+two-state hidden kernel is identifiable exactly on the exchange diagonal and
+has a continuum fibre off it; within the physical sampled-counter subfamily,
+the only ambiguity off the diagonal is the rate exchange.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+First (b>0).  If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), direct evaluation of
+the defining integral gives
+\[
+ b=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
+ \qquad
+ b+s-p=\frac{\Gamma(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma}
+          =bq_\ast>0.
+ \tag{F3}
+\]
+The same identities hold by continuity on the diagonal, where
+(p=s), (b=\Gamma\Delta\tau p>0), and (q_\ast=1).  Consequently
+\[
+ \det[\mathbf1,K\mathbf1]=b+s-p=bq_\ast>0,
+ \qquad
+ \det\begin{bmatrix}e_2^\top\\e_2^\top K\end{bmatrix}=-b\ne0,
+\]
+so (K) is minimal.
+
+Every member of \(\mathcal G_2\) has the unique form
+\[
+ M_q=\begin{pmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad q\ne0.
+\]
+Multiplication, using (b+s-p=bq_\ast), gives
+(M_q^{-1}KM_q=K(q)) in \textup{(F1)}.  Since (K) is minimal, its scalar
+Hankel sequence has rank two.  Any (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same visible
+law has the same leading Hankel matrix; its factorization as
+(\mathcal O(L)\mathcal C(L)) has rank two, so both factors have rank two and
+(L) is minimal as well.  The recalled orbit--fibre proposition therefore
+forces every such (L) to have the displayed form.  If
+(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2), its lower-left entry
+is (bq\ge0).  Invertibility excludes (q=0), hence (q>0).  Its
+upper-right entry then yields the exact condition
+\[
+ \frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\ge0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q\in I_\ast.
+ \tag{F4}
+\]
+
+Conversely, let (q\in I_\ast).  The two diagonal entries in
+\textup{(F1)} are affine in (q), with endpoint values (p,s) and (s,p),
+respectively, and are therefore positive.  The lower-left entry is positive,
+and \textup{(F4)} makes the upper-right entry nonnegative.  Writing
+(a=1-b-s>0), the two killing deficits are
+\[
+ 1-K(q)\mathbf1
+ =\begin{pmatrix}a+bq_\ast/q\\a\end{pmatrix}>0.
+ \tag{F5}
+\]
+Similarity preserves the spectral radius
+(\max\{p,s\}<1), so (K(q)\in\mathcal K_2).  This proves that the
+displayed arc is the complete fibre.  It is injective because its lower-left
+entry is (bq).
+
+At (q=1) one recovers (K).  At (q=q_\ast),
+\[
+ K(q_\ast)=\begin{pmatrix}s&0\\bq_\ast&p\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+Equation~\textup{(F3)} says that (bq_\ast) is precisely the no-click
+recovery-to-ready probability after exchanging the two rates, and its second
+row has the same killing deficit (a); this proves \textup{(F2)}.  If
+(q_\ast\ne1), the product in the upper-right entry is strictly positive
+inside (I_\ast) and vanishes only at its endpoints.  All remaining entries
+and both deficits are already strict there.  If (q_\ast=1),
+\textup{(F4)} forces (q=1).  The endpoint, triangular-intersection, and
+identifiability statements follow.
+\end{proof}
+

 \label{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main}
 Fix \(n\ge2\), a known \(\Delta\tau>0\), and arbitrary positive rates

+
+## Selected result
+
+The first candidate maximizes reach times value and directly completes the
+paper's physical quotient story. For
+(K=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&0\\b&s\end{smallmatrix}\right)), every
+reset-preserving similarity is generated by
+(M_q=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)).
+Writing (q_*=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), the transformed upper-right entry
+is (b(1-q)(q-q_*)/q). The lower-left entry forces (q>0), so Markov
+nonnegativity is equivalent to (q) lying between (1) and (q_*). The two
+endpoints are exactly the original and rate-swapped physical kernels; strict
+interior points are positive nontriangular kernels. At equal rates (q_*=1),
+the full two-state fibre collapses to one point.
+

+def sampled_counter_killed_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the physical two-state no-click kernel."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery, delta))):
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be finite")
+    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
+    p = float(np.exp(-gamma * delta))
+    s = float(np.exp(-recovery * delta))
+    difference = recovery - gamma
+    if difference == 0.0:
+        b = recovery * delta * p
+    else:
+        b = recovery * p * (-np.expm1(-difference * delta)) / difference
+    return np.array([[p, 0.0], [b, s]])
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_interval(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float
+) -> tuple[float, float]:
+    """Return the exact closed q-interval of Markovian similarity equivalents."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery))) or min(gamma, recovery) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates must be finite and positive")
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    return min(1.0, endpoint), max(1.0, endpoint)
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float, q: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the q member of the exact physical two-state Markovian fibre."""
+    if not np.isfinite(q):
+        raise ValueError("q must be finite")
+    lower, upper = sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
+    if q < lower or q > upper:
+        raise ValueError("q lies outside the exact Markovian fibre interval")
+    physical = sampled_counter_killed_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta)
+    p = float(physical[0, 0])
+    b = float(physical[1, 0])
+    s = float(physical[1, 1])
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    equivalent = np.array(
+        [
+            [p - b + b * q, b * (1.0 - q) * (q - endpoint) / q],
+            [b * q, s + b * (1.0 - q)],
+        ]
+    )
+    deficits = np.ones(2) - equivalent @ np.ones(2)
+    if float(equivalent.min()) < -1e-12 or float(deficits.min()) < -1e-12:
+        raise ArithmeticError("closed-form fibre member is not substochastic")
+    return equivalent
+

+\begin{theorem}[Complete two-state fibre arc and exchange dichotomy]
+\label{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main}
+Under \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, put (K=T_0),
+(q_\ast=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), and
+\[
+ I_\ast=[\min\{1,q_\ast\},\max\{1,q_\ast\}].
+\]
+Then (K) is minimal, and its complete visible-law fibre in
+(\mathcal K_2) is the injectively parametrized closed arc
+\[
+ \{K(q):q\in I_\ast\},
+ \qquad
+ K(q)=
+ \begin{pmatrix}
+ p-b+bq & \displaystyle\frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\\[5pt]
+ bq & s+b(1-q)
+ \end{pmatrix}.
+ \tag{F1}
+\]
+Here complete means that every (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same stationary
+visible click law as (K) is (K(q)) for exactly one (q\in I_\ast).
+Writing (T_0(\alpha,\eta)) for the no-click kernel constructed with attempt
+rate (\alpha) and recovery rate (\eta), the endpoints are the two physical
+triangular kernels obtained by exchanging those rates:
+\[
+ K(1)=T_0(\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r}),
+ \qquad
+ K(q_\ast)=T_0(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Gamma).
+ \tag{F2}
+\]
+If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), every (q) strictly between the
+endpoints gives a strictly positive kernel with strictly positive killing
+deficits, and the physical triangular subfamily meets the arc only at the two
+endpoints.  If \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), then (I_\ast=\{1\}), so
+the entire two-state killed-reset fibre is a singleton.  Thus the unrestricted
+two-state hidden kernel is identifiable exactly on the exchange diagonal and
+has a continuum fibre off it; within the physical sampled-counter subfamily,
+the only ambiguity off the diagonal is the rate exchange.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+First (b>0).  If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), direct evaluation of
+the defining integral gives
+\[
+ b=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
+ \qquad
+ b+s-p=\frac{\Gamma(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma}
+          =bq_\ast>0.
+ \tag{F3}
+\]
+The same identities hold by continuity on the diagonal, where
+(p=s), (b=\Gamma\Delta\tau p>0), and (q_\ast=1).  Consequently
+\[
+ \det[\mathbf1,K\mathbf1]=b+s-p=bq_\ast>0,
+ \qquad
+ \det\begin{bmatrix}e_2^\top\\e_2^\top K\end{bmatrix}=-b\ne0,
+\]
+so (K) is minimal.
+
+Every member of \(\mathcal G_2\) has the unique form
+\[
+ M_q=\begin{pmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad q\ne0.
+\]
+Multiplication, using (b+s-p=bq_\ast), gives
+(M_q^{-1}KM_q=K(q)) in \textup{(F1)}.  Since (K) is minimal, its scalar
+Hankel sequence has rank two.  Any (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same visible
+law has the same leading Hankel matrix; its factorization as
+(\mathcal O(L)\mathcal C(L)) has rank two, so both factors have rank two and
+(L) is minimal as well.  The recalled orbit--fibre proposition therefore
+forces every such (L) to have the displayed form.  If
+(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2), its lower-left entry
+is (bq\ge0).  Invertibility excludes (q=0), hence (q>0).  Its
+upper-right entry then yields the exact condition
+\[
+ \frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\ge0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q\in I_\ast.
+ \tag{F4}
+\]
+
+Conversely, let (q\in I_\ast).  The two diagonal entries in
+\textup{(F1)} are affine in (q), with endpoint values (p,s) and (s,p),
+respectively, and are therefore positive.  The lower-left entry is positive,
+and \textup{(F4)} makes the upper-right entry nonnegative.  Writing
+(a=1-b-s>0), the two killing deficits are
+\[
+ 1-K(q)\mathbf1
+ =\begin{pmatrix}a+bq_\ast/q\\a\end{pmatrix}>0.
+ \tag{F5}
+\]
+Similarity preserves the spectral radius
+(\max\{p,s\}<1), so (K(q)\in\mathcal K_2).  This proves that the
+displayed arc is the complete fibre.  It is injective because its lower-left
+entry is (bq).
+
+At (q=1) one recovers (K).  At (q=q_\ast),
+\[
+ K(q_\ast)=\begin{pmatrix}s&0\\bq_\ast&p\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+Equation~\textup{(F3)} says that (bq_\ast) is precisely the no-click
+recovery-to-ready probability after exchanging the two rates, and its second
+row has the same killing deficit (a); this proves \textup{(F2)}.  If
+(q_\ast\ne1), the product in the upper-right entry is strictly positive
+inside (I_\ast) and vanishes only at its endpoints.  All remaining entries
+and both deficits are already strict there.  If (q_\ast=1),
+\textup{(F4)} forces (q=1).  The endpoint, triangular-intersection, and
+identifiability statements follow.
+\end{proof}

+## Selected result
+
+The first candidate maximizes reach times value and directly completes the
+paper's physical quotient story. For
+(K=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&0\\b&s\end{smallmatrix}\right)), every
+reset-preserving similarity is generated by

+def sampled_counter_killed_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the physical two-state no-click kernel."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery, delta))):
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be finite")
+    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
+    p = float(np.exp(-gamma * delta))
+    s = float(np.exp(-recovery * delta))
+    difference = recovery - gamma
+    if difference == 0.0:
+        b = recovery * delta * p
+    else:
+        b = recovery * p * (-np.expm1(-difference * delta)) / difference
+    return np.array([[p, 0.0], [b, s]])
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_interval(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float
+) -> tuple[float, float]:
+    """Return the exact closed q-interval of Markovian similarity equivalents."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery))) or min(gamma, recovery) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates must be finite and positive")
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    return min(1.0, endpoint), max(1.0, endpoint)
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float, q: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the q member of the exact physical two-state Markovian fibre."""
+    if not np.isfinite(q):
+        raise ValueError("q must be finite")
+    lower, upper = sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
+    if q < lower or q > upper:
+        raise ValueError("q lies outside the exact Markovian fibre interval")
+    physical = sampled_counter_killed_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta)
+    p = float(physical[0, 0])
+    b = float(physical[1, 0])
+    s = float(physical[1, 1])
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    equivalent = np.array(
+        [
+            [p - b + b * q, b * (1.0 - q) * (q - endpoint) / q],
+            [b * q, s + b * (1.0 - q)],
+        ]
+    )
+    deficits = np.ones(2) - equivalent @ np.ones(2)
+    if float(equivalent.min()) < -1e-12 or float(deficits.min()) < -1e-12:
+        raise ArithmeticError("closed-form fibre member is not substochastic")
+    return equivalent
+

+\begin{theorem}[Complete two-state fibre arc and exchange dichotomy]
+\label{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main}
+Under \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, put (K=T_0),
+(q_\ast=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), and
+\[
+ I_\ast=[\min\{1,q_\ast\},\max\{1,q_\ast\}].
+\]
+Then (K) is minimal, and its complete visible-law fibre in
+(\mathcal K_2) is the injectively parametrized closed arc
+\[
+ \{K(q):q\in I_\ast\},
+ \qquad
+ K(q)=
+ \begin{pmatrix}
+ p-b+bq & \displaystyle\frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\\[5pt]
+ bq & s+b(1-q)
+ \end{pmatrix}.
+ \tag{F1}
+\]
+Here complete means that every (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same stationary
+visible click law as (K) is (K(q)) for exactly one (q\in I_\ast).
+Writing (T_0(\alpha,\eta)) for the no-click kernel constructed with attempt
+rate (\alpha) and recovery rate (\eta), the endpoints are the two physical
+triangular kernels obtained by exchanging those rates:
+\[
+ K(1)=T_0(\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r}),
+ \qquad
+ K(q_\ast)=T_0(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Gamma).
+ \tag{F2}
+\]
+If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), every (q) strictly between the
+endpoints gives a strictly positive kernel with strictly positive killing
+deficits, and the physical triangular subfamily meets the arc only at the two
+endpoints.  If \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), then (I_\ast=\{1\}), so
+the entire two-state killed-reset fibre is a singleton.  Thus the unrestricted
+two-state hidden kernel is identifiable exactly on the exchange diagonal and
+has a continuum fibre off it; within the physical sampled-counter subfamily,
+the only ambiguity off the diagonal is the rate exchange.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+First (b>0).  If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), direct evaluation of
+the defining integral gives
+\[
+ b=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
+ \qquad
+ b+s-p=\frac{\Gamma(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma}
+          =bq_\ast>0.
+ \tag{F3}
+\]
+The same identities hold by continuity on the diagonal, where
+(p=s), (b=\Gamma\Delta\tau p>0), and (q_\ast=1).  Consequently
+\[
+ \det[\mathbf1,K\mathbf1]=b+s-p=bq_\ast>0,
+ \qquad
+ \det\begin{bmatrix}e_2^\top\\e_2^\top K\end{bmatrix}=-b\ne0,
+\]
+so (K) is minimal.
+
+Every member of \(\mathcal G_2\) has the unique form
+\[
+ M_q=\begin{pmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad q\ne0.
+\]
+Multiplication, using (b+s-p=bq_\ast), gives
+(M_q^{-1}KM_q=K(q)) in \textup{(F1)}.  Since (K) is minimal, its scalar
+Hankel sequence has rank two.  Any (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same visible
+law has the same leading Hankel matrix; its factorization as
+(\mathcal O(L)\mathcal C(L)) has rank two, so both factors have rank two and
+(L) is minimal as well.  The recalled orbit--fibre proposition therefore
+forces every such (L) to have the displayed form.  If
+(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2), its lower-left entry
+is (bq\ge0).  Invertibility excludes (q=0), hence (q>0).  Its
+upper-right entry then yields the exact condition
+\[
+ \frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\ge0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q\in I_\ast.
+ \tag{F4}
+\]
+
+Conversely, let (q\in I_\ast).  The two diagonal entries in
+\textup{(F1)} are affine in (q), with endpoint values (p,s) and (s,p),
+respectively, and are therefore positive.  The lower-left entry is positive,
+and \textup{(F4)} makes the upper-right entry nonnegative.  Writing
+(a=1-b-s>0), the two killing deficits are
+\[
+ 1-K(q)\mathbf1
+ =\begin{pmatrix}a+bq_\ast/q\\a\end{pmatrix}>0.
+ \tag{F5}
+\]
+Similarity preserves the spectral radius
+(\max\{p,s\}<1), so (K(q)\in\mathcal K_2).  This proves that the
+displayed arc is the complete fibre.  It is injective because its lower-left
+entry is (bq).
+
+At (q=1) one recovers (K).  At (q=q_\ast),
+\[
+ K(q_\ast)=\begin{pmatrix}s&0\\bq_\ast&p\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+Equation~\textup{(F3)} says that (bq_\ast) is precisely the no-click
+recovery-to-ready probability after exchanging the two rates, and its second
+row has the same killing deficit (a); this proves \textup{(F2)}.  If
+(q_\ast\ne1), the product in the upper-right entry is strictly positive
+inside (I_\ast) and vanishes only at its endpoints.  All remaining entries
+and both deficits are already strict there.  If (q_\ast=1),
+\textup{(F4)} forces (q=1).  The endpoint, triangular-intersection, and
+identifiability statements follow.
+\end{proof}

+## Selected result
+
+The first candidate maximizes reach times value and directly completes the
+paper's physical quotient story. For
+(K=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&0\\b&s\end{smallmatrix}\right)), every
+reset-preserving similarity is generated by
+(M_q=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)).
+Writing (q_*=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), the transformed upper-right entry
+is (b(1-q)(q-q_*)/q). The lower-left entry forces (q>0), so Markov
+nonnegativity is equivalent to (q) lying between (1) and (q_*). The two
+endpoints are exactly the original and rate-swapped physical kernels; strict
+interior points are positive nontriangular kernels. At equal rates (q_*=1),
+the full two-state fibre collapses to one point.

+def sampled_counter_killed_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the physical two-state no-click kernel."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery, delta))):
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be finite")
+    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
+    p = float(np.exp(-gamma * delta))
+    s = float(np.exp(-recovery * delta))
+    difference = recovery - gamma
+    if difference == 0.0:
+        b = recovery * delta * p
+    else:
+        b = recovery * p * (-np.expm1(-difference * delta)) / difference
+    return np.array([[p, 0.0], [b, s]])
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_interval(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float
+) -> tuple[float, float]:
+    """Return the exact closed q-interval of Markovian similarity equivalents."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery))) or min(gamma, recovery) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates must be finite and positive")
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    return min(1.0, endpoint), max(1.0, endpoint)
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float, q: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the q member of the exact physical two-state Markovian fibre."""
+    if not np.isfinite(q):
+        raise ValueError("q must be finite")
+    lower, upper = sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
+    if q < lower or q > upper:
+        raise ValueError("q lies outside the exact Markovian fibre interval")
+    physical = sampled_counter_killed_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta)
+    p = float(physical[0, 0])
+    b = float(physical[1, 0])
+    s = float(physical[1, 1])
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    equivalent = np.array(
+        [
+            [p - b + b * q, b * (1.0 - q) * (q - endpoint) / q],
+            [b * q, s + b * (1.0 - q)],
+        ]
+    )
+    deficits = np.ones(2) - equivalent @ np.ones(2)
+    if float(equivalent.min()) < -1e-12 or float(deficits.min()) < -1e-12:
+        raise ArithmeticError("closed-form fibre member is not substochastic")
+    return equivalent
+

+\begin{theorem}[Complete two-state fibre arc and exchange dichotomy]
+\label{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main}
+Under \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, put (K=T_0),
+(q_\ast=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), and
+\[
+ I_\ast=[\min\{1,q_\ast\},\max\{1,q_\ast\}].
+\]
+Then (K) is minimal, and its complete visible-law fibre in
+(\mathcal K_2) is the injectively parametrized closed arc
+\[
+ \{K(q):q\in I_\ast\},
+ \qquad
+ K(q)=
+ \begin{pmatrix}
+ p-b+bq & \displaystyle\frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\\[5pt]
+ bq & s+b(1-q)
+ \end{pmatrix}.
+ \tag{F1}
+\]
+Here complete means that every (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same stationary
+visible click law as (K) is (K(q)) for exactly one (q\in I_\ast).
+Writing (T_0(\alpha,\eta)) for the no-click kernel constructed with attempt
+rate (\alpha) and recovery rate (\eta), the endpoints are the two physical
+triangular kernels obtained by exchanging those rates:
+\[
+ K(1)=T_0(\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r}),
+ \qquad
+ K(q_\ast)=T_0(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Gamma).
+ \tag{F2}
+\]
+If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), every (q) strictly between the
+endpoints gives a strictly positive kernel with strictly positive killing
+deficits, and the physical triangular subfamily meets the arc only at the two
+endpoints.  If \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), then (I_\ast=\{1\}), so
+the entire two-state killed-reset fibre is a singleton.  Thus the unrestricted
+two-state hidden kernel is identifiable exactly on the exchange diagonal and
+has a continuum fibre off it; within the physical sampled-counter subfamily,
+the only ambiguity off the diagonal is the rate exchange.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+First (b>0).  If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), direct evaluation of
+the defining integral gives
+\[
+ b=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
+ \qquad
+ b+s-p=\frac{\Gamma(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma}
+          =bq_\ast>0.
+ \tag{F3}
+\]
+The same identities hold by continuity on the diagonal, where
+(p=s), (b=\Gamma\Delta\tau p>0), and (q_\ast=1).  Consequently
+\[
+ \det[\mathbf1,K\mathbf1]=b+s-p=bq_\ast>0,
+ \qquad
+ \det\begin{bmatrix}e_2^\top\\e_2^\top K\end{bmatrix}=-b\ne0,
+\]
+so (K) is minimal.
+
+Every member of \(\mathcal G_2\) has the unique form
+\[
+ M_q=\begin{pmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad q\ne0.
+\]
+Multiplication, using (b+s-p=bq_\ast), gives
+(M_q^{-1}KM_q=K(q)) in \textup{(F1)}.  Since (K) is minimal, its scalar
+Hankel sequence has rank two.  Any (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same visible
+law has the same leading Hankel matrix; its factorization as
+(\mathcal O(L)\mathcal C(L)) has rank two, so both factors have rank two and
+(L) is minimal as well.  The recalled orbit--fibre proposition therefore
+forces every such (L) to have the displayed form.  If
+(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2), its lower-left entry
+is (bq\ge0).  Invertibility excludes (q=0), hence (q>0).  Its
+upper-right entry then yields the exact condition
+\[
+ \frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\ge0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q\in I_\ast.
+ \tag{F4}
+\]
+
+Conversely, let (q\in I_\ast).  The two diagonal entries in
+\textup{(F1)} are affine in (q), with endpoint values (p,s) and (s,p),
+respectively, and are therefore positive.  The lower-left entry is positive,
+and \textup{(F4)} makes the upper-right entry nonnegative.  Writing
+(a=1-b-s>0), the two killing deficits are
+\[
+ 1-K(q)\mathbf1
+ =\begin{pmatrix}a+bq_\ast/q\\a\end{pmatrix}>0.
+ \tag{F5}
+\]
+Similarity preserves the spectral radius
+(\max\{p,s\}<1), so (K(q)\in\mathcal K_2).  This proves that the
+displayed arc is the complete fibre.  It is injective because its lower-left
+entry is (bq).
+
+At (q=1) one recovers (K).  At (q=q_\ast),
+\[
+ K(q_\ast)=\begin{pmatrix}s&0\\bq_\ast&p\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+Equation~\textup{(F3)} says that (bq_\ast) is precisely the no-click
+recovery-to-ready probability after exchanging the two rates, and its second
+row has the same killing deficit (a); this proves \textup{(F2)}.  If
+(q_\ast\ne1), the product in the upper-right entry is strictly positive
+inside (I_\ast) and vanishes only at its endpoints.  All remaining entries
+and both deficits are already strict there.  If (q_\ast=1),
+\textup{(F4)} forces (q=1).  The endpoint, triangular-intersection, and
+identifiability statements follow.
+\end{proof}

## Independent prior-art and proof reassessment, 2026-08-08

This reassessment used the arXiv Atom API, Crossref, Google Scholar, the zbMATH
Open API as a MathSciNet-style index, Semantic Scholar's reference graph, and
the complete published/arXiv text and bibliography of
Cattaneo--Masini--Underwood (CMU). The arXiv query `all:"Yurinskii coupling"`
returned arXiv:2210.00362v4 and one application paper. The earlier exact
Helmert/one-dependent API queries listed above returned zero results; later API
retries were throttled and are not used as negative evidence. Crossref
confirmed DOI `10.1214/25-AOS2538`, *Annals of Statistics* **53**(5) (2025),
and returned no matching weighted-Helmert renewal theorem. A Google Scholar
query for `"weighted Helmert" "Gaussian coupling"` returned only unrelated
Gauss--Helmert engineering papers; exact follow-ups triggered Scholar's
captcha, so Scholar is recorded as searched but is not used to claim absence.
The zbMATH query for Yurinskii martingale coupling returned CMU; its
phase-type-identifiability query recovered Ryden's classical identifiability
paper and related phase-type work, but no deterministic-reset refinement.

CMU's own reference graph identifies the relevant general predecessors:
Yurinskii (1978), Le Cam (1988), Pollard (2002), Zaitsev (1987),
Dudley--Philipp (1983), Dehling (1983), Belloni--Oliveira (2018), Li--Liao
(2020), and Berthet--Mason (2006). These sources contain the general coupling,
strong-approximation, or dependent-vector machinery. They do not make the
sampled-counter Helmert calculation a new coupling method.

Most importantly, CMU Corollary 2.3 does not follow from the manuscript's old
quantity `beta_N -> 0`. For Euclidean norm it uses
`phi_2(d)^2 = 2d`, and its `beta_{2,2}` includes both the block third moments
and the Gaussian comparison third moments. The block calculation gives

`beta_{2,2} <= C{sqrt(L)d^(3/2)/sqrt(n) + 1/(sqrt(n)S_J)}`,

so the cited corollary requires `d beta_{2,2} -> 0`. The rare-cell term is
therefore `d/(sqrt(n)S_J)`, not merely `1/(sqrt(n)S_J)`. The proposition has
been weakened accordingly: `n S_J^2 -> infinity` is necessary,
`d/(sqrt(n)S_J) -> 0` is sufficient, and the resulting
`4 log log n` second-order window is an explicit open interface.

The requested compact-class extension is not valid from the pointwise tail
display alone. Compactness of parameter labels does not make the `o(1)`
uniform or control `g_j/S_j`: a family can move a finite near-plateau to layer
`j=m`, while every fixed law eventually has the same geometric-polynomial
tail. Adding a uniform tail-ratio remainder, uniform atom-to-tail bounds, and
compact bounds on `(c,a,x)` makes the CMU verification uniform under the same
stronger sufficient condition; that is a direct application, not a tier-raising
theorem. The coupling line is therefore not extended. The manuscript is
positioned instead around its killed-reset D-MAP visible quotient and
similarity-fibre structure, while acknowledging that minimal-realization and
confluent-Prony inputs are established theory.

+## Selected result
+
+The first candidate maximizes reach times value and directly completes the
+paper's physical quotient story. For
+(K=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&0\\b&s\end{smallmatrix}\right)), every
+reset-preserving similarity is generated by
+(M_q=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)).
+Writing (q_*=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), the transformed upper-right entry
+is (b(1-q)(q-q_*)/q). The lower-left entry forces (q>0), so Markov
+nonnegativity is equivalent to (q) lying between (1) and (q_*). The two
+endpoints are exactly the original and rate-swapped physical kernels; strict
+interior points are positive nontriangular kernels. At equal rates (q_*=1),
+the full two-state fibre collapses to one point.
+

+def sampled_counter_killed_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the physical two-state no-click kernel."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery, delta))):
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be finite")
+    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
+    p = float(np.exp(-gamma * delta))
+    s = float(np.exp(-recovery * delta))
+    difference = recovery - gamma
+    if difference == 0.0:
+        b = recovery * delta * p
+    else:
+        b = recovery * p * (-np.expm1(-difference * delta)) / difference
+    return np.array([[p, 0.0], [b, s]])
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_interval(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float
+) -> tuple[float, float]:
+    """Return the exact closed q-interval of Markovian similarity equivalents."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery))) or min(gamma, recovery) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates must be finite and positive")
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    return min(1.0, endpoint), max(1.0, endpoint)
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float, q: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the q member of the exact physical two-state Markovian fibre."""
+    if not np.isfinite(q):
+        raise ValueError("q must be finite")
+    lower, upper = sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
+    if q < lower or q > upper:
+        raise ValueError("q lies outside the exact Markovian fibre interval")
+    physical = sampled_counter_killed_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta)
+    p = float(physical[0, 0])
+    b = float(physical[1, 0])
+    s = float(physical[1, 1])
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    equivalent = np.array(
+        [
+            [p - b + b * q, b * (1.0 - q) * (q - endpoint) / q],
+            [b * q, s + b * (1.0 - q)],
+        ]
+    )
+    deficits = np.ones(2) - equivalent @ np.ones(2)
+    if float(equivalent.min()) < -1e-12 or float(deficits.min()) < -1e-12:
+        raise ArithmeticError("closed-form fibre member is not substochastic")
+    return equivalent
+

+\begin{theorem}[Complete two-state fibre arc and exchange dichotomy]
+\label{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main}
+Under \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, put (K=T_0),
+(q_\ast=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), and
+\[
+ I_\ast=[\min\{1,q_\ast\},\max\{1,q_\ast\}].
+\]
+Then (K) is minimal, and its complete visible-law fibre in
+(\mathcal K_2) is the injectively parametrized closed arc
+\[
+ \{K(q):q\in I_\ast\},
+ \qquad
+ K(q)=
+ \begin{pmatrix}
+ p-b+bq & \displaystyle\frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\\[5pt]
+ bq & s+b(1-q)
+ \end{pmatrix}.
+ \tag{F1}
+\]
+Here complete means that every (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same stationary
+visible click law as (K) is (K(q)) for exactly one (q\in I_\ast).
+Writing (T_0(\alpha,\eta)) for the no-click kernel constructed with attempt
+rate (\alpha) and recovery rate (\eta), the endpoints are the two physical
+triangular kernels obtained by exchanging those rates:
+\[
+ K(1)=T_0(\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r}),
+ \qquad
+ K(q_\ast)=T_0(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Gamma).
+ \tag{F2}
+\]
+If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), every (q) strictly between the
+endpoints gives a strictly positive kernel with strictly positive killing
+deficits, and the physical triangular subfamily meets the arc only at the two
+endpoints.  If \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), then (I_\ast=\{1\}), so
+the entire two-state killed-reset fibre is a singleton.  Thus the unrestricted
+two-state hidden kernel is identifiable exactly on the exchange diagonal and
+has a continuum fibre off it; within the physical sampled-counter subfamily,
+the only ambiguity off the diagonal is the rate exchange.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+First (b>0).  If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), direct evaluation of
+the defining integral gives
+\[
+ b=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
+ \qquad
+ b+s-p=\frac{\Gamma(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma}
+          =bq_\ast>0.
+ \tag{F3}
+\]
+The same identities hold by continuity on the diagonal, where
+(p=s), (b=\Gamma\Delta\tau p>0), and (q_\ast=1).  Consequently
+\[
+ \det[\mathbf1,K\mathbf1]=b+s-p=bq_\ast>0,
+ \qquad
+ \det\begin{bmatrix}e_2^\top\\e_2^\top K\end{bmatrix}=-b\ne0,
+\]
+so (K) is minimal.
+
+Every member of \(\mathcal G_2\) has the unique form
+\[
+ M_q=\begin{pmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad q\ne0.
+\]
+Multiplication, using (b+s-p=bq_\ast), gives
+(M_q^{-1}KM_q=K(q)) in \textup{(F1)}.  Since (K) is minimal, its scalar
+Hankel sequence has rank two.  Any (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same visible
+law has the same leading Hankel matrix; its factorization as
+(\mathcal O(L)\mathcal C(L)) has rank two, so both factors have rank two and
+(L) is minimal as well.  The recalled orbit--fibre proposition therefore
+forces every such (L) to have the displayed form.  If
+(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2), its lower-left entry
+is (bq\ge0).  Invertibility excludes (q=0), hence (q>0).  Its
+upper-right entry then yields the exact condition
+\[
+ \frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\ge0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q\in I_\ast.
+ \tag{F4}
+\]
+
+Conversely, let (q\in I_\ast).  The two diagonal entries in
+\textup{(F1)} are affine in (q), with endpoint values (p,s) and (s,p),
+respectively, and are therefore positive.  The lower-left entry is positive,
+and \textup{(F4)} makes the upper-right entry nonnegative.  Writing
+(a=1-b-s>0), the two killing deficits are
+\[
+ 1-K(q)\mathbf1
+ =\begin{pmatrix}a+bq_\ast/q\\a\end{pmatrix}>0.
+ \tag{F5}
+\]
+Similarity preserves the spectral radius
+(\max\{p,s\}<1), so (K(q)\in\mathcal K_2).  This proves that the
+displayed arc is the complete fibre.  It is injective because its lower-left
+entry is (bq).
+
+At (q=1) one recovers (K).  At (q=q_\ast),
+\[
+ K(q_\ast)=\begin{pmatrix}s&0\\bq_\ast&p\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+Equation~\textup{(F3)} says that (bq_\ast) is precisely the no-click
+recovery-to-ready probability after exchanging the two rates, and its second
+row has the same killing deficit (a); this proves \textup{(F2)}.  If
+(q_\ast\ne1), the product in the upper-right entry is strictly positive
+inside (I_\ast) and vanishes only at its endpoints.  All remaining entries
+and both deficits are already strict there.  If (q_\ast=1),
+\textup{(F4)} forces (q=1).  The endpoint, triangular-intersection, and
+identifiability statements follow.
+\end{proof}

+## Selected result
+
+The first candidate maximizes reach times value and directly completes the
+paper's physical quotient story. For
+(K=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&0\\b&s\end{smallmatrix}\right)), every
+reset-preserving similarity is generated by
+(M_q=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)).
+Writing (q_*=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), the transformed upper-right entry
+is (b(1-q)(q-q_*)/q). The lower-left entry forces (q>0), so Markov
+nonnegativity is equivalent to (q) lying between (1) and (q_*). The two
+endpoints are exactly the original and rate-swapped physical kernels; strict
+interior points are positive nontriangular kernels. At equal rates (q_*=1),
+the full two-state fibre collapses to one point.
+

+def sampled_counter_killed_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the physical two-state no-click kernel."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery, delta))):
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be finite")
+    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
+    p = float(np.exp(-gamma * delta))
+    s = float(np.exp(-recovery * delta))
+    difference = recovery - gamma
+    if difference == 0.0:
+        b = recovery * delta * p
+    else:
+        b = recovery * p * (-np.expm1(-difference * delta)) / difference
+    return np.array([[p, 0.0], [b, s]])
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_interval(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float
+) -> tuple[float, float]:
+    """Return the exact closed q-interval of Markovian similarity equivalents."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery))) or min(gamma, recovery) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates must be finite and positive")
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    return min(1.0, endpoint), max(1.0, endpoint)
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float, q: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the q member of the exact physical two-state Markovian fibre."""
+    if not np.isfinite(q):
+        raise ValueError("q must be finite")
+    lower, upper = sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
+    if q < lower or q > upper:
+        raise ValueError("q lies outside the exact Markovian fibre interval")
+    physical = sampled_counter_killed_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta)
+    p = float(physical[0, 0])
+    b = float(physical[1, 0])
+    s = float(physical[1, 1])
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    equivalent = np.array(
+        [
+            [p - b + b * q, b * (1.0 - q) * (q - endpoint) / q],
+            [b * q, s + b * (1.0 - q)],
+        ]
+    )
+    deficits = np.ones(2) - equivalent @ np.ones(2)
+    if float(equivalent.min()) < -1e-12 or float(deficits.min()) < -1e-12:
+        raise ArithmeticError("closed-form fibre member is not substochastic")
+    return equivalent
+

+\begin{theorem}[Complete two-state fibre arc and exchange dichotomy]
+\label{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main}
+Under \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, put (K=T_0),
+(q_\ast=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), and
+\[
+ I_\ast=[\min\{1,q_\ast\},\max\{1,q_\ast\}].
+\]
+Then (K) is minimal, and its complete visible-law fibre in
+(\mathcal K_2) is the injectively parametrized closed arc
+\[
+ \{K(q):q\in I_\ast\},
+ \qquad
+ K(q)=
+ \begin{pmatrix}
+ p-b+bq & \displaystyle\frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\\[5pt]
+ bq & s+b(1-q)
+ \end{pmatrix}.
+ \tag{F1}
+\]
+Here complete means that every (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same stationary
+visible click law as (K) is (K(q)) for exactly one (q\in I_\ast).
+Writing (T_0(\alpha,\eta)) for the no-click kernel constructed with attempt
+rate (\alpha) and recovery rate (\eta), the endpoints are the two physical
+triangular kernels obtained by exchanging those rates:
+\[
+ K(1)=T_0(\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r}),
+ \qquad
+ K(q_\ast)=T_0(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Gamma).
+ \tag{F2}
+\]
+If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), every (q) strictly between the
+endpoints gives a strictly positive kernel with strictly positive killing
+deficits, and the physical triangular subfamily meets the arc only at the two
+endpoints.  If \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), then (I_\ast=\{1\}), so
+the entire two-state killed-reset fibre is a singleton.  Thus the unrestricted
+two-state hidden kernel is identifiable exactly on the exchange diagonal and
+has a continuum fibre off it; within the physical sampled-counter subfamily,
+the only ambiguity off the diagonal is the rate exchange.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+First (b>0).  If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), direct evaluation of
+the defining integral gives
+\[
+ b=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
+ \qquad
+ b+s-p=\frac{\Gamma(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma}
+          =bq_\ast>0.
+ \tag{F3}
+\]
+The same identities hold by continuity on the diagonal, where
+(p=s), (b=\Gamma\Delta\tau p>0), and (q_\ast=1).  Consequently
+\[
+ \det[\mathbf1,K\mathbf1]=b+s-p=bq_\ast>0,
+ \qquad
+ \det\begin{bmatrix}e_2^\top\\e_2^\top K\end{bmatrix}=-b\ne0,
+\]
+so (K) is minimal.
+
+Every member of \(\mathcal G_2\) has the unique form
+\[
+ M_q=\begin{pmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad q\ne0.
+\]
+Multiplication, using (b+s-p=bq_\ast), gives
+(M_q^{-1}KM_q=K(q)) in \textup{(F1)}.  Since (K) is minimal, its scalar
+Hankel sequence has rank two.  Any (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same visible
+law has the same leading Hankel matrix; its factorization as
+(\mathcal O(L)\mathcal C(L)) has rank two, so both factors have rank two and
+(L) is minimal as well.  The recalled orbit--fibre proposition therefore
+forces every such (L) to have the displayed form.  If
+(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2), its lower-left entry
+is (bq\ge0).  Invertibility excludes (q=0), hence (q>0).  Its
+upper-right entry then yields the exact condition
+\[
+ \frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\ge0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q\in I_\ast.
+ \tag{F4}
+\]
+
+Conversely, let (q\in I_\ast).  The two diagonal entries in
+\textup{(F1)} are affine in (q), with endpoint values (p,s) and (s,p),
+respectively, and are therefore positive.  The lower-left entry is positive,
+and \textup{(F4)} makes the upper-right entry nonnegative.  Writing
+(a=1-b-s>0), the two killing deficits are
+\[
+ 1-K(q)\mathbf1
+ =\begin{pmatrix}a+bq_\ast/q\\a\end{pmatrix}>0.
+ \tag{F5}
+\]
+Similarity preserves the spectral radius
+(\max\{p,s\}<1), so (K(q)\in\mathcal K_2).  This proves that the
+displayed arc is the complete fibre.  It is injective because its lower-left
+entry is (bq).
+
+At (q=1) one recovers (K).  At (q=q_\ast),
+\[
+ K(q_\ast)=\begin{pmatrix}s&0\\bq_\ast&p\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+Equation~\textup{(F3)} says that (bq_\ast) is precisely the no-click
+recovery-to-ready probability after exchanging the two rates, and its second
+row has the same killing deficit (a); this proves \textup{(F2)}.  If
+(q_\ast\ne1), the product in the upper-right entry is strictly positive
+inside (I_\ast) and vanishes only at its endpoints.  All remaining entries
+and both deficits are already strict there.  If (q_\ast=1),
+\textup{(F4)} forces (q=1).  The endpoint, triangular-intersection, and
+identifiability statements follow.
+\end{proof}
+

 Fix \(n\ge2\), a known \(\Delta\tau>0\), and arbitrary positive rates

+## Selected result
+
+The first candidate maximizes reach times value and directly completes the
+paper's physical quotient story. For
+(K=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&0\\b&s\end{smallmatrix}\right)), every
+reset-preserving similarity is generated by
+(M_q=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)).
+Writing (q_*=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), the transformed upper-right entry
+is (b(1-q)(q-q_*)/q). The lower-left entry forces (q>0), so Markov
+nonnegativity is equivalent to (q) lying between (1) and (q_*). The two
+endpoints are exactly the original and rate-swapped physical kernels; strict
+interior points are positive nontriangular kernels. At equal rates (q_*=1),
+the full two-state fibre collapses to one point.

+def sampled_counter_killed_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the physical two-state no-click kernel."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery, delta))):
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be finite")
+    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
+    p = float(np.exp(-gamma * delta))
+    s = float(np.exp(-recovery * delta))
+    difference = recovery - gamma
+    if difference == 0.0:
+        b = recovery * delta * p
+    else:
+        b = recovery * p * (-np.expm1(-difference * delta)) / difference
+    return np.array([[p, 0.0], [b, s]])
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_interval(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float
+) -> tuple[float, float]:
+    """Return the exact closed q-interval of Markovian similarity equivalents."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery))) or min(gamma, recovery) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates must be finite and positive")
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    return min(1.0, endpoint), max(1.0, endpoint)
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float, q: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the q member of the exact physical two-state Markovian fibre."""
+    if not np.isfinite(q):
+        raise ValueError("q must be finite")
+    lower, upper = sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
+    if q < lower or q > upper:
+        raise ValueError("q lies outside the exact Markovian fibre interval")
+    physical = sampled_counter_killed_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta)
+    p = float(physical[0, 0])
+    b = float(physical[1, 0])
+    s = float(physical[1, 1])
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    equivalent = np.array(
+        [
+            [p - b + b * q, b * (1.0 - q) * (q - endpoint) / q],
+            [b * q, s + b * (1.0 - q)],
+        ]
+    )
+    deficits = np.ones(2) - equivalent @ np.ones(2)
+    if float(equivalent.min()) < -1e-12 or float(deficits.min()) < -1e-12:
+        raise ArithmeticError("closed-form fibre member is not substochastic")
+    return equivalent
+

+\begin{theorem}[Complete two-state fibre arc and exchange dichotomy]
+\label{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main}
+Under \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, put (K=T_0),
+(q_\ast=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), and
+\[
+ I_\ast=[\min\{1,q_\ast\},\max\{1,q_\ast\}].
+\]
+Then (K) is minimal, and its complete visible-law fibre in
+(\mathcal K_2) is the injectively parametrized closed arc
+\[
+ \{K(q):q\in I_\ast\},
+ \qquad
+ K(q)=
+ \begin{pmatrix}
+ p-b+bq & \displaystyle\frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\\[5pt]
+ bq & s+b(1-q)
+ \end{pmatrix}.
+ \tag{F1}
+\]
+Here complete means that every (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same stationary
+visible click law as (K) is (K(q)) for exactly one (q\in I_\ast).
+Writing (T_0(\alpha,\eta)) for the no-click kernel constructed with attempt
+rate (\alpha) and recovery rate (\eta), the endpoints are the two physical
+triangular kernels obtained by exchanging those rates:
+\[
+ K(1)=T_0(\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r}),
+ \qquad
+ K(q_\ast)=T_0(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Gamma).
+ \tag{F2}
+\]
+If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), every (q) strictly between the
+endpoints gives a strictly positive kernel with strictly positive killing
+deficits, and the physical triangular subfamily meets the arc only at the two
+endpoints.  If \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), then (I_\ast=\{1\}), so
+the entire two-state killed-reset fibre is a singleton.  Thus the unrestricted
+two-state hidden kernel is identifiable exactly on the exchange diagonal and
+has a continuum fibre off it; within the physical sampled-counter subfamily,
+the only ambiguity off the diagonal is the rate exchange.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+First (b>0).  If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), direct evaluation of
+the defining integral gives
+\[
+ b=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
+ \qquad
+ b+s-p=\frac{\Gamma(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma}
+          =bq_\ast>0.
+ \tag{F3}
+\]
+The same identities hold by continuity on the diagonal, where
+(p=s), (b=\Gamma\Delta\tau p>0), and (q_\ast=1).  Consequently
+\[
+ \det[\mathbf1,K\mathbf1]=b+s-p=bq_\ast>0,
+ \qquad
+ \det\begin{bmatrix}e_2^\top\\e_2^\top K\end{bmatrix}=-b\ne0,
+\]
+so (K) is minimal.
+
+Every member of \(\mathcal G_2\) has the unique form
+\[
+ M_q=\begin{pmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad q\ne0.
+\]
+Multiplication, using (b+s-p=bq_\ast), gives
+(M_q^{-1}KM_q=K(q)) in \textup{(F1)}.  Since (K) is minimal, its scalar
+Hankel sequence has rank two.  Any (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same visible
+law has the same leading Hankel matrix; its factorization as
+(\mathcal O(L)\mathcal C(L)) has rank two, so both factors have rank two and
+(L) is minimal as well.  The recalled orbit--fibre proposition therefore
+forces every such (L) to have the displayed form.  If
+(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2), its lower-left entry
+is (bq\ge0).  Invertibility excludes (q=0), hence (q>0).  Its
+upper-right entry then yields the exact condition
+\[
+ \frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\ge0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q\in I_\ast.
+ \tag{F4}
+\]
+
+Conversely, let (q\in I_\ast).  The two diagonal entries in
+\textup{(F1)} are affine in (q), with endpoint values (p,s) and (s,p),
+respectively, and are therefore positive.  The lower-left entry is positive,
+and \textup{(F4)} makes the upper-right entry nonnegative.  Writing
+(a=1-b-s>0), the two killing deficits are
+\[
+ 1-K(q)\mathbf1
+ =\begin{pmatrix}a+bq_\ast/q\\a\end{pmatrix}>0.
+ \tag{F5}
+\]
+Similarity preserves the spectral radius
+(\max\{p,s\}<1), so (K(q)\in\mathcal K_2).  This proves that the
+displayed arc is the complete fibre.  It is injective because its lower-left
+entry is (bq).
+
+At (q=1) one recovers (K).  At (q=q_\ast),
+\[
+ K(q_\ast)=\begin{pmatrix}s&0\\bq_\ast&p\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+Equation~\textup{(F3)} says that (bq_\ast) is precisely the no-click
+recovery-to-ready probability after exchanging the two rates, and its second
+row has the same killing deficit (a); this proves \textup{(F2)}.  If
+(q_\ast\ne1), the product in the upper-right entry is strictly positive
+inside (I_\ast) and vanishes only at its endpoints.  All remaining entries
+and both deficits are already strict there.  If (q_\ast=1),
+\textup{(F4)} forces (q=1).  The endpoint, triangular-intersection, and
+identifiability statements follow.
+\end{proof}
+
 \begin{corollary}[All-collision serial identifiability]
 \label{cor:nstate-serial-all-collision-identifiability-main}
 Fix \(n\ge2\), a known \(\Delta\tau>0\), and arbitrary positive rates

+## Selected result
+
+The first candidate maximizes reach times value and directly completes the
+paper's physical quotient story. For
+(K=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&0\\b&s\end{smallmatrix}\right)), every
+reset-preserving similarity is generated by
+(M_q=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)).
+Writing (q_*=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), the transformed upper-right entry
+is (b(1-q)(q-q_*)/q). The lower-left entry forces (q>0), so Markov
+nonnegativity is equivalent to (q) lying between (1) and (q_*). The two
+endpoints are exactly the original and rate-swapped physical kernels; strict
+interior points are positive nontriangular kernels. At equal rates (q_*=1),
+the full two-state fibre collapses to one point.

+def sampled_counter_killed_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the physical two-state no-click kernel."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery, delta))):
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be finite")
+    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
+    p = float(np.exp(-gamma * delta))
+    s = float(np.exp(-recovery * delta))
+    difference = recovery - gamma
+    if difference == 0.0:
+        b = recovery * delta * p
+    else:
+        b = recovery * p * (-np.expm1(-difference * delta)) / difference
+    return np.array([[p, 0.0], [b, s]])
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_interval(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float
+) -> tuple[float, float]:
+    """Return the exact closed q-interval of Markovian similarity equivalents."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery))) or min(gamma, recovery) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates must be finite and positive")
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    return min(1.0, endpoint), max(1.0, endpoint)
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float, q: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the q member of the exact physical two-state Markovian fibre."""
+    if not np.isfinite(q):
+        raise ValueError("q must be finite")
+    lower, upper = sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
+    if q < lower or q > upper:
+        raise ValueError("q lies outside the exact Markovian fibre interval")
+    physical = sampled_counter_killed_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta)
+    p = float(physical[0, 0])
+    b = float(physical[1, 0])
+    s = float(physical[1, 1])
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    equivalent = np.array(
+        [
+            [p - b + b * q, b * (1.0 - q) * (q - endpoint) / q],
+            [b * q, s + b * (1.0 - q)],
+        ]
+    )
+    deficits = np.ones(2) - equivalent @ np.ones(2)
+    if float(equivalent.min()) < -1e-12 or float(deficits.min()) < -1e-12:
+        raise ArithmeticError("closed-form fibre member is not substochastic")
+    return equivalent
+

+\begin{theorem}[Complete two-state fibre arc and exchange dichotomy]
+\label{thm:two-state-complete-fibre-arc-main}
+Under \Cref{ass:model-inference-contract-main}, put (K=T_0),
+(q_\ast=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), and
+\[
+ I_\ast=[\min\{1,q_\ast\},\max\{1,q_\ast\}].
+\]
+Then (K) is minimal, and its complete visible-law fibre in
+(\mathcal K_2) is the injectively parametrized closed arc
+\[
+ \{K(q):q\in I_\ast\},
+ \qquad
+ K(q)=
+ \begin{pmatrix}
+ p-b+bq & \displaystyle\frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\\[5pt]
+ bq & s+b(1-q)
+ \end{pmatrix}.
+ \tag{F1}
+\]
+Here complete means that every (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same stationary
+visible click law as (K) is (K(q)) for exactly one (q\in I_\ast).
+Writing (T_0(\alpha,\eta)) for the no-click kernel constructed with attempt
+rate (\alpha) and recovery rate (\eta), the endpoints are the two physical
+triangular kernels obtained by exchanging those rates:
+\[
+ K(1)=T_0(\Gamma,\kappa_{\mathrm r}),
+ \qquad
+ K(q_\ast)=T_0(\kappa_{\mathrm r},\Gamma).
+ \tag{F2}
+\]
+If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), every (q) strictly between the
+endpoints gives a strictly positive kernel with strictly positive killing
+deficits, and the physical triangular subfamily meets the arc only at the two
+endpoints.  If \(\Gamma=\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), then (I_\ast=\{1\}), so
+the entire two-state killed-reset fibre is a singleton.  Thus the unrestricted
+two-state hidden kernel is identifiable exactly on the exchange diagonal and
+has a continuum fibre off it; within the physical sampled-counter subfamily,
+the only ambiguity off the diagonal is the rate exchange.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+First (b>0).  If \(\Gamma\ne\kappa_{\mathrm r}\), direct evaluation of
+the defining integral gives
+\[
+ b=\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm r}(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma},
+ \qquad
+ b+s-p=\frac{\Gamma(p-s)}{\kappa_{\mathrm r}-\Gamma}
+          =bq_\ast>0.
+ \tag{F3}
+\]
+The same identities hold by continuity on the diagonal, where
+(p=s), (b=\Gamma\Delta\tau p>0), and (q_\ast=1).  Consequently
+\[
+ \det[\mathbf1,K\mathbf1]=b+s-p=bq_\ast>0,
+ \qquad
+ \det\begin{bmatrix}e_2^\top\\e_2^\top K\end{bmatrix}=-b\ne0,
+\]
+so (K) is minimal.
+
+Every member of \(\mathcal G_2\) has the unique form
+\[
+ M_q=\begin{pmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad q\ne0.
+\]
+Multiplication, using (b+s-p=bq_\ast), gives
+(M_q^{-1}KM_q=K(q)) in \textup{(F1)}.  Since (K) is minimal, its scalar
+Hankel sequence has rank two.  Any (L\in\mathcal K_2) with the same visible
+law has the same leading Hankel matrix; its factorization as
+(\mathcal O(L)\mathcal C(L)) has rank two, so both factors have rank two and
+(L) is minimal as well.  The recalled orbit--fibre proposition therefore
+forces every such (L) to have the displayed form.  If
+(K(q)\in\mathcal K_2), its lower-left entry
+is (bq\ge0).  Invertibility excludes (q=0), hence (q>0).  Its
+upper-right entry then yields the exact condition
+\[
+ \frac{b(1-q)(q-q_\ast)}q\ge0
+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q\in I_\ast.
+ \tag{F4}
+\]
+
+Conversely, let (q\in I_\ast).  The two diagonal entries in
+\textup{(F1)} are affine in (q), with endpoint values (p,s) and (s,p),
+respectively, and are therefore positive.  The lower-left entry is positive,
+and \textup{(F4)} makes the upper-right entry nonnegative.  Writing
+(a=1-b-s>0), the two killing deficits are
+\[
+ 1-K(q)\mathbf1
+ =\begin{pmatrix}a+bq_\ast/q\\a\end{pmatrix}>0.
+ \tag{F5}
+\]
+Similarity preserves the spectral radius
+(\max\{p,s\}<1), so (K(q)\in\mathcal K_2).  This proves that the
+displayed arc is the complete fibre.  It is injective because its lower-left
+entry is (bq).
+
+At (q=1) one recovers (K).  At (q=q_\ast),
+\[
+ K(q_\ast)=\begin{pmatrix}s&0\\bq_\ast&p\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+Equation~\textup{(F3)} says that (bq_\ast) is precisely the no-click
+recovery-to-ready probability after exchanging the two rates, and its second
+row has the same killing deficit (a); this proves \textup{(F2)}.  If
+(q_\ast\ne1), the product in the upper-right entry is strictly positive
+inside (I_\ast) and vanishes only at its endpoints.  All remaining entries
+and both deficits are already strict there.  If (q_\ast=1),
+\textup{(F4)} forces (q=1).  The endpoint, triangular-intersection, and
+identifiability statements follow.
+\end{proof}

+## Selected result
+
+The first candidate maximizes reach times value and directly completes the
+paper's physical quotient story. For
+(K=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&0\\b&s\end{smallmatrix}\right)), every
+reset-preserving similarity is generated by
+(M_q=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}q&1-q\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)).
+Writing (q_*=\Gamma/\kappa_{\mathrm r}), the transformed upper-right entry
+is (b(1-q)(q-q_*)/q). The lower-left entry forces (q>0), so Markov
+nonnegativity is equivalent to (q) lying between (1) and (q_*). The two
+endpoints are exactly the original and rate-swapped physical kernels; strict
+interior points are positive nontriangular kernels. At equal rates (q_*=1),
+the full two-state fibre collapses to one point.
+

+def sampled_counter_killed_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the physical two-state no-click kernel."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery, delta))):
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be finite")
+    if min(gamma, recovery, delta) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates and sampling interval must be positive")
+    p = float(np.exp(-gamma * delta))
+    s = float(np.exp(-recovery * delta))
+    difference = recovery - gamma
+    if difference == 0.0:
+        b = recovery * delta * p
+    else:
+        b = recovery * p * (-np.expm1(-difference * delta)) / difference
+    return np.array([[p, 0.0], [b, s]])
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_interval(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float
+) -> tuple[float, float]:
+    """Return the exact closed q-interval of Markovian similarity equivalents."""
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite((gamma, recovery))) or min(gamma, recovery) <= 0.0:
+        raise ValueError("rates must be finite and positive")
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    return min(1.0, endpoint), max(1.0, endpoint)
+
+
+def sampled_counter_fibre_kernel(
+    gamma: float, recovery: float, delta: float, q: float
+) -> FloatArray:
+    """Return the q member of the exact physical two-state Markovian fibre."""
+    if not np.isfinite(q):
+        raise ValueError("q must be finite")
+    lower, upper = sampled_counter_fibre_interval(gamma, recovery)
+    if q < lower or q > upper:
+        raise ValueError("q lies outside the exact Markovian fibre interval")
+    physical = sampled_counter_killed_kernel(gamma, recovery, delta)
+    p = float(physical[0, 0])
+    b = float(physical[1, 0])
+    s = float(physical[1, 1])
+    endpoint = gamma / recovery
+    equivalent = np.array(
+        [
+            [p - b + b * q, b * (1.0 - q) * (q - endpoint) / q],
+            [b * q, s + b * (1.0 - q)],
+        ]
+    )
+    deficits = np.ones(2) - equivalent @ np.ones(2)
+    if float(equivalent.min()) < -1e-12 or float(deficits.min()) < -1e-12:
+        raise ArithmeticError("closed-form fibre member is not substochastic")
+    return equivalent
+
